documents.title: 1.1.1 Non-Text Content (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.1.1 Non-Text Content (2.0 A)

## In brief

A text alternative is available for visual and auditory content, most commonly images, for those who cannot see or hear content to understand it.

## Normative

> All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose, except for the situations listed below.
>
> - **Controls, Input**
>   - If non-text content is a control or accepts user input, then it has a name that describes its purpose. (Refer to Success Criterion 4.1.2 for additional requirements for controls and content that accepts user input.)
> - **Time-Based Media**
>   - If non-text content is time-based media, then text alternatives at least provide descriptive identification of the non-text content. (Refer to Guideline 1.2 for additional requirements for media.)
> - **Test**
>   - If non-text content is a test or exercise that would be invalid if presented in text, then text alternatives at least provide descriptive identification of the non-text content.
> - **Sensory**
>   - If non-text content is primarily intended to create a specific sensory experience, then text alternatives at least provide descriptive identification of the non-text content.
> - **CAPTCHA**
>   - If the purpose of non-text content is to confirm that content is being accessed by a person rather than a computer, then text alternatives that identify and describe the purpose of the non-text content are provided, and alternative forms of CAPTCHA using output modes for different types of sensory perception are provided to accommodate different disabilities.
> - **Decoration, Formatting, Invisible**
>   - If non-text content is pure decoration, is used only for visual formatting, or is not presented to users, then it is implemented in a way that it can be ignored by assistive technology.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Non-text content updates, but the accessible alternative does not update. A Sales chart is updated to October results, but the text alternative still displays September results. ([F20](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F20)) | When non-text content updates, the `alt` value should be updated too. |
| A GitHub logo has no accessible label. | A GitHub logo has `alt="GitHub"` set as its accessible name. |
| An NPM logo on a page is labeled with `alt="Page Logo"`, which doesn't accurately describe the image. | An NPM logo on a page has an accessible name provided using `alt="NPM"`. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Terminal animation on cli.github.com has no text alternative** [Issue 3921](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/3921)
  * In this issue, there is an animated image showing terminal output. No accessible label is provided for the image. As a result, screen reader users will not be informed of the image's content / purpose.
* **Insufficiently descriptive `alt` value for 'npm' logo as "Page Logo" is provided** [Issue 9247](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9247)
  * In this issue, the accessible description of the image doesn't properly describe what it is.
  * If it was just a logo image for NPM, it would be appropriate to have just `alt="npm"`.
  * If it is a linked image, you could also include a bit more detail to convey the purpose of the control (e.g., `alt="NPM home"`).
* **`<svg>` elements with an `img` role must have an alternative text** [Issue 9802](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9802)
  * In this issue, we have an `svg` element without a descriptive, accessible description, which would result in the meaning of the image not being communicated to screen reader users.
  * `svg` elements, that have a `role` of `image`, must be given an accessible descriptions just like other images.
* **`alt` text value is defined for decorative image** [Issue 10610](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10610)
  * In this issue, we have a decorative image that has an `alt` attribute with a value set instead of being null (`alt=""` or `alt`), or having a `role` attribute set to `presentation` to indicate that it is decorative and provides no information.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| An image with the text "Sale!" has an accessible name of "Sale!" via an `alt` attribute. Additionally, adjacent text "Sale!" is present. | The "Sale!" image programmatically indicates that it is decorative — such as with a null `alt` attribute — since the same information is contained in the adjacent text. |

## Additional guidance

* [Note on CAPTCHA as it relates to SC 1.1.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content#intent:~:text=the%20same%20language.-,Note%20on%20CAPTCHA,-CAPTCHAs%20are%20a)
* This success criterion passes if an image has no programmatic alternative text, but the exact content is available in text and is adjacent to the image.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Primer resources

* [Alternative text for images | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/alternative-text-for-images)
* [Icons | Primer accessibility patterns](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/icons)

## Other resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 1.1.1](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#111-non-text-content)
* [MAS 1.1.1: Non-text Content Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.1.1-Non-text-Content-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 1.1.1 Non-Text Content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content)
* [Images Tutorial | WAI | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/)

documents.title: 1.2.1 Audio-Only and Video-Only (Prerecorded) (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.2.1 Audio-Only and Video-Only (Prerecorded) (2.0 A)

## In brief

Provide an alternative for prerecorded media that is only perceivable with one sense (audio-only or video-only) to ensure users who cannot fully see or hear can understand it.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> For [prerecorded](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded#dfn-prerecorded) [audio-only](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded#dfn-audio-only) and prerecorded [video-only](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded#dfn-video-only) media, the following are true, except when the audio or video is a [media alternative for text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded#dfn-media-alternative-for-text) and is clearly labeled as such:
>
> - **Prerecorded Audio-only**
>   - An [alternative for time-based media](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded#dfn-alternative-for-time-based-media) is provided that presents equivalent information for prerecorded audio-only content.
> - **Prerecorded Video-only**
>   - Either an alternative for time-based media or an audio track is provided that presents equivalent information for prerecorded video-only content.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A silent video shows a man adding a conference session to his agenda for the conference. There are no audio descriptions of the visual content available. | The video has audio descriptions describing what actions the man is taking throughout the video. |
| An audio-only recording of a conference session has no accompanying captioning or transcript of the audio. | A transcript is provided for the audio content. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **There is no alternative way defined for the video only content to know the purpose of the video content** [Issue 6558](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/6558)
  * In this issue, there is a video on a page that features no audio or other alternative to help describe what is being shown in the video.
* **The audio description is not present for the video only content** [Issue 7882](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7882)
  * In this issue, there is a video on a page that features no audio or other alternative to help describe what is being shown in the video.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A tutorial video features a step by step set of text instructions underneath it that describes the steps shown in the video. | A video tutorial features a synchronized transcript that accurately describes each step being taken in the video as it plays. (See [General Guidelines for Transcripts | Content Creation : Create Accessible Captions and Transcripts | Section508.gov](https://www.section508.gov/create/captions-transcripts/#general-guidelines-for-transcripts)) |

## Additional guidance

* A text equivalent is not required for audio that is provided as an equivalent for video with no audio information. For example, it is not required to caption audio description that is provided as an alternative to a silent movie.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 1.2.1](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#121-audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 1.2.1 Audio-Only and Video-Only (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded.html)
* [Making Audio and Video Media Accessible | W3C Web Accessibility Initiative](https://www.w3.org/WAI/media/av/)
* Deque resources
  * [Captions are incorrect or inadequate | Deque Docs](https://docs.deque.com/issue-help/1.0.0/en/captions-inadequate)
  * [`<video>` elements must have captions | Deque University](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.7/video-caption)
* [Open vs. Closed Captions | Digital Accessibility | University of South Carolina](https://sc.edu/about/offices_and_divisions/digital-accessibility/toolbox/best_practices/captioning_transcripts/open-closed-captioning/index.php)
* [Captions vs. Subtitles: Breaking Down the Differences | 3PlayMedia](https://www.3playmedia.com/blog/closed-captioning-vs-subtitles/)
* [Open Captions vs. Closed Captions: What’s the Difference? | 3PlayMedia](https://www.3playmedia.com/blog/open-captioning-use/)
* [Subtitles, Closed Captions, and Open Captions: What's the Difference? | Ben Myers](https://benmyers.dev/blog/captions-and-subtitles/)

documents.title: 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (2.0 A)

## In brief

Ensure captions are available for audio content in videos so people who are deaf or hard of hearing can understand the audio content.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> [Captions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded#dfn-captions) are provided for all [prerecorded](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded#dfn-prerecorded) [audio](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded#dfn-audio) content in [synchronized media](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded#dfn-synchronized-media), except when the media is a [media alternative for text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded#dfn-media-alternative-for-text) and is clearly labeled as such.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A video tutorial on how to create a repo has someone speaking to describe the steps. No captions are available for users unable to hear the content. | Captions are included in the content that accurately reflect what is being said. |
| A video tutorial features captions that list the steps being performed, but not the actual content of what the speaker is saying (i.e. "Step 1: Navigate to your GitHub profile." instead of the actual words spoken by the presenter.). | The captions contain the words spoken by the presenter along with descriptions of any other relevant audio from the video. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Missing Human-Generated Captions for Video** [Issue 834](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/834)
  * In the case of this issue, there is a video hosted on YouTube.
  * The only captions available for the video are those automatically generated by YouTube, which unfortunately can be inaccurate.
  * By adding human generated captions, we ensure that users are able to accurately obtain the information from the video.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A video tutorial features Open captions which are embedded into the video and cannot be turned off by the user. | The video instead features closed captions which can be customized and can be turned on/off by the user. |

## Additional guidance

* Style guides for captions may differ among different languages.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

* [WCAG Helper 1.2.2](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#122-captions-prerecorded)

* [Understanding SC 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded)
* [Making Audio and Video Media Accessible | W3C Web Accessibility Initiative](https://www.w3.org/WAI/media/av/)
* **Deque resources**
  * [Captions are incorrect or inadequate | Deque Docs](https://docs.deque.com/issue-help/1.0.0/en/captions-inadequate)
  * [`<video>` elements must have captions | Deque University](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.7/video-caption)
* [Open vs. Closed Captions | Digital Accessibility | University of South Carolina](https://sc.edu/about/offices_and_divisions/digital-accessibility/toolbox/best_practices/captioning_transcripts/open-closed-captioning/index.php)

documents.title: 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (2.0 A)

## In brief

Provide [audio descriptions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded#dfn-audio-description) or [alternative media](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded#dfn-alternative-for-time-based-media), of video content to ensure users who cannot see the visual content can have it described.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> An [alternative for time-based media](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded#dfn-alternative-for-time-based-media) or [audio description](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded#dfn-audio-description) of the [prerecorded](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded#dfn-prerecorded) [video](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded#dfn-video) content is provided for [synchronized media](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded#dfn-synchronized-media), except when the media is a [media alternative for text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded#dfn-media-alternative-for-text) and is clearly labeled as such.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A video tutorial features audio descriptions that do not include all of the important visual information from the video. | The audio descriptions describe all important visual content found in the video. |
| A video tutorial's player doesn't provide a method to enable audio description and no alternative has been provided by the owner. | A text transcript is provided adjacent to the video or as a linked file. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Missing Audio Description for Video** [Issue 835](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/835)
  * In the case of this issue, we have a video with no audio.
  * The video has no alternative format for non-visual users to know what information is being conveyed.
  * In this case, an audio description track or text description could be a viable option to resolve the issue.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional guidance

* For 1.2.3, 1.2.5, and 1.2.7, if all of the information in the video track is already provided in the audio track, no audio description is necessary.
* 1.2.3, 1.2.5, and 1.2.8 overlap somewhat with each other. This is to give the author some choice at the minimum conformance level, and to provide additional requirements at higher levels. At Level A in Success Criterion 1.2.3, authors do have the choice of providing either an audio description or a full text alternative. If they wish to conform at Level AA, under Success Criterion 1.2.5 authors must provide an audio description - a requirement already met if they chose that alternative for 1.2.3, otherwise an additional requirement. At Level AAA under Success Criterion 1.2.8 they must provide an extended text description. This is an additional requirement if both 1.2.3 and 1.2.5 were met by providing an audio description only. If 1.2.3 was met, however, by providing a text description, and the 1.2.5 requirement for an audio description was met, then 1.2.8 does not add new requirements.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

documents.title: 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (2.0 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Captions are provided for audio content in real-time videos so it can be understood by people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> [Captions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live#dfn-captions) are provided for all [live](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live#dfn-live) [audio](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live#dfn-audio) content in [synchronized media](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live#dfn-synchronized-media).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A keynote is being broadcast live to virtual attendees. No captions are provided are provided. | Captions are provided to users on screen. |

# 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Provide a synchronized spoken description of the visual content in videos so the visual content can be understood by people who cannot see it.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> [Audio description](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-prerecorded#dfn-audio-description) is provided for all [prerecorded](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-prerecorded#dfn-prerecorded) [video](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-prerecorded#dfn-video) content in [synchronized media](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-prerecorded#dfn-synchronized-media).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| An onboarding video of an employee exploring an office area plays. The spoken content is available in captions, but there is visual information needed to understand the content that is not conveyed with audio descriptions.| Audio descriptions are provided that include information about the surroundings and actions occurring within the video. |
| A video tutorial features audio descriptions that do not include all of the visual information from the video. | The audio descriptions describe all visual content found in the video. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **The audio description is not present for the video only content** [Issue 7005](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7005)
  * In the case of this issue, there is a video with no audio description presented.
  * As a result, non-visual users, are not informed of the information presented by the video.
* **Missing Audio Description for Video** [Issue 835](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/835)
  * In the case of this issue, there is a video with no audio description presented.
  * As a result, non-visual users, are not informed of the information presented by the video.

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A physics professor gives a lecture and makes freehand sketches on the whiteboard. He speaks rapidly while drawing and when one problem is finished, he erases the drawing and begins another sketch while continuing to speak and gesture. There is not enough of a pause between problems for a sufficiently descriptive audio description. | The video is paused between problems, and extended audio description of the professor's drawings and gestures is provided; the video is then resumed. |

documents.title: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (2.0 A)

## In brief

Use semantic markup in a way that properly conveys meaning and relationships between content.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| An input has an error message and/or hint that is not programmatically associated to the input. As a result, it is not communicated to the user by assistive technologies in a way that clearly communicates the relationship between the elements. | Errors and hints should be programmatically associated with the respective inputs. For example, this can be done via an `aria-describedby` attribute. |
| Using changes in text presentation to convey information without using the appropriate markup or text ([F2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F2)). For example, in [issue #5992 comment](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/5992#issuecomment-2027534655), visually crossing out text without ensuring the added context is provided in an accessible format. | Ensure information conveyed visually is also available in an accessible format (i.e., plain text, `aria-label`). Reference WCAG [Technique G117](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/general/G117) for more context. |
| Structural markup being used for presentational effect rather than proper semantics ([F43](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F43)). For example, using headings to emphasize text rather than to convey logical heading structure, or using list elements (`ol`, `ul`, & `dl`) for non-list content. | Ensure semantic elements are used to communicate their intended purpose (i.e., Headings used to describe the content under them, lists for lists,blockquotes for quotes, and fieldsets for groupings of form inputs like a radio button group.) |
| Using `th` elements, `caption` elements, or non-empty `summary` attributes in layout tables ([F46](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F46)). | If a table is being used for presentation/layout purposes, rather than to display a data table, assign the table a `role` of `presentation` and do not use structural markup such as `<th>` or `<caption>` elements. |
| Not correctly marking up table headers ([F91](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F91)) by not using header elements (`th`), `headers` and `id` attributes, the `scope` attribute, or the ARIA roles (`columnheader`/`rowheader`) to make the headers programatically determinable from within table content. | Ensure that table headers are properly used and scoped. When screen reader users navigate through the table content horizontally or vertically, the headers that change can be read out to provide the necessary context for the information in the data cells. |
| Enclosing non-heading information in table headers. | Ensure that table headers only contain the header. Other information should be contained within other cells of the table. An example of this can be found in a [comment on Issue #5992](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/5992#issuecomment-2027545840). |
| Headings are visually defined, but not programmatically defined. | Heading structure should be programmatically defined so that users who do not perceive the visual context can still know and navigate the page structure. This can be achieved with appropriate semantics (`h1` - `h6`) or the ARIA role (`role="heading"`) and attribute (`aria-level="[1-6]"`) set. |
| Illogical heading structure does not accurately convey the structure of the page. | Heading structure should ideally follow an `h1` through `h6` structure that represents how the content is structured and related. |

### Guidance for severity level 3

A severity level of 3 should be applied when both of the following are true:

- A description for a form input is provided but is not programmatically associated with the input.
- The description is accessible to screen reader users in browse mode.

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Screen reader is not announcing the associated label for the radio controls** [Issue 11024](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11024)
  * In the case of this issue, the radio buttons are not programmatically grouped under their group label.
  * As a result, a screen reader will not communicate the primary question being asked to give context to why the option is being announced.
  * Additionally, the radio buttons will not be properly communicated as a group so the user knows they are all options for a single question.
* **Text -'GitHub Advanced Security' is not programmatically defined as heading** [Issue 10977](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10977)
  * In the case of this issue, we have text that is visually and functionally a heading, but has not been programmatically defined as such.
  * As a result, important structural information is lost to users of some assistive technologies, in addition to navigational functionality that would otherwise be available.
* **'--' is unnecessarily displayed as a heading** [Issue 10720](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10720)
  * In the case of this issue, heading semantics have been used on text that does not function as a heading in order to obtain certain aesthetics.
  * As a result, structural information will not be correctly communicated to users of certain assistive technologies.
* **Screen reader does not announce the required information for edit field** [Issue 10547](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10547)
  * In this instance, a field is required and visually this is communicated by the use of an asterisk. However, the field is not programmatically identified as required.
  * Punctuation marks, such as asterisks, don't typically get communicated by assistive technologies. As a result, non-visual users will not be informed that the field is required.
  * The field should be given the `required` and/or `aria-required` attribute, or should have the word "required" added to its label (e.g., "Name (Required)").

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| List semantics are not applied to a set of links within a navigation section. | List semantics are applied to a set of links within a navigation section. |

## Additional guidance

* The `role` of `presentation|none` should not be used on elements that provide semantic information ([F92](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F92)).
* Providing error messages when necessary falls under [3.3.1 Error Identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html), while the programmatic association of error messages to relevant inputs falls under [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* H1 not required on a page for compliance (it's usability).
  * For example, [Issue #7695](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7695) should not have been initially noted as a failure of WCAG 1.3.1, but instead recorded as a usability issue.
* Name-value pairs mustn't use headings. [Reference screenshot](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/33)
* Taglines mustn't be a heading; it's simply a P. [Reference screenshot](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/33)
* For social media link sections, text such as "Follow us on" may or may not be a heading; either way is acceptable. [Reference screenshot](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/33)
* The `role` of `presentation|none` must be used on layout tables. A screen reader announcing a layout table is a Severity 3 fail. Reference [issue 9653](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9653#issuecomment-2577839358).
* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Primer resources

* [Semantic HTML and ARIA | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/semantic-html-and-aria)
* [Headings | Primer accessibility patterns](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/headings)
* [FormControl accessibility | Primer](https://primer.style/product/components/form-control/accessibility)
* [DataTable accessibility | Primer](https://primer.style/product/components/data-table/accessibility)

## Other resources

* [WCAG Helper 1.3.1](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#131-info-and-relationships)
* **MAS content**
  * [MAS 1.3.1: Info and Relationships Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.3.1-Info-and-Relationships-Guide.aspx)
  * [Landmarks](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/ARIA-landmarks-for-web-developers.aspx): not normally visible with regular browsers, these document areas allow assistive technology to orient themselves, navigate, and skip parts of pages.
* **WCAG content**
  * [Understanding SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html)
  * [Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/) for form inputs
  * [Grouping controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/) for multiple associated inputs
  * [Instructions and hints](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/instructions/), where necessary
  * [Form validation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/validation/) should provide information directing the user to the form element that needs attention
  * [Headings](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/headings/) provide a document structure which benefits all users. In particular, screen reader users can open a list of headings.
  * [aria-label](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#aria-label): Defines a string value that labels the current element.
  * [aria-labelledby](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#aria-labelledby): Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
  * [aria-describedby](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#aria-describedby): Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.
  * [Tables Tutorial | W3C WAI](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/)

documents.title: 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (2.0 A)

## In brief

When read by assistive technologies, content should be read in an order that is accurate and makes sense to the user.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a [correct reading sequence](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence#dfn-correct-reading-sequence) can be [programmatically determined](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence#dfn-programmatically-determined).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| When reading through a page, a clear button is located after a line of text describing the content that will be cleared. Screen readers reads the clear button before reading the line describing what is being cleared with nothing to connect the 2. This results in confusion for the user on what they are clearing. | The screen reader should read the text that describes what is being displayed, and would be cleared by the clear button, before reading the clear button. ([See audit issue #9552](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9552)) |
| While moving through a page, a paragraph of text containing a link gains focus, but only part of it gets read. Upon advancing focus or using additional gestures, the remaining text and link does not get read. ([See audit issue #9548](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9548)) | Content should be read by the screen reader in a meaningful order that accurately conveys the information. |
| A drop-down menu's contents are being read off by a screen reader before the menu has been expanded. | The drop-down menu's content should be hidden from assistive technology while closed. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **In browse mode, screen reader focus land on the hidden content** [Issue 12042](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/12042)
  * In this case, when the screen reader is being used to browse the page, content that is not visible is in the sequence, which should not be.
* **Page Content is not Visible to Keyboard only Users** [Issue 11682](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11682)
  * In this instance, content is not in the sequence of content for users only using keyboard.
  * This results in the content being inaccessible to keyboard only users, and fully hidden from screen readers and other assistive technologies.
* **Voiceover is not announcing any information after selecting ‘login with browser’ control** [Issue 10978](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10978)
  * In the case of this issue, the screen reader is not announcing the additional content that gets displayed when the user select the "login with browser" control in the CLI.
  * In CLI, the focus is expected to move as content is displayed in the window. Therefore, it should be read as the content appears so that screenreader users are informed of what is expected of them next or of information provided.
* **VoiceOver does not navigate in a sequential manner over 'Up to 50 in Free' text** [Issue 11071](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11071)
  * In this case, when a screen reader navigates through the table, not all of the text within the cell is read. Only the bold text is read in the left most cell of each row.
  * Content within each cell of the table should be programmatically grouped, even if styled differently, so that it is all communicated to the screen reader.
* **Talkback focus does not navigate on the 'Tick, Sync and Minus' icons** [Issue 11079](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11079)
  * There are icons present on the page that convey information about what features each plan option has, but these are not accessible to screen readers. Thus they get skipped when a Voiceover user is navigating through the content.
  * Depending on how the icons are implemented, changes need to be made so they are in tab order regardless of whether the user is using a assistive technology, and have accessible labels that are also accessible to assistive technology.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A set of social media links is read off by a screen reader in a different order from the visual reading order. | The set of social media links is read by assistive technologies in the same order as the visual reading order. |
| A section of text contains a footnote number that indicates which of the footnotes in the footer it is referencing. The user has to scroll down to the footer to find the footnote. | The footnote number is a link to the respective footnote in the footer. |

## Additional guidance

* If line numbers of a code block are not output by the screen reader, this most likely should _not_ be reported. 
* Be careful when using CSS grid of flex to ensure that content structure doesn't change in a way that impacts the meaning of the content, particularly with regards to how assistive technology reading order.
  * The [Resources section](#resources) contains some helpful resources describing why source order, display/CSS order, and keyboard order are so vital to users being able to comprehend and interact with content.
* Assistive technologies typically read content based on its order within the DOM structure, which is why the visual structure may not match the reading order. As a result, it is important to take this into account to ensure that content is presented to users in a meaningful order regardless of how they reading it.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* In the event that content is not read out by a screen reader, it is to be reported under 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence.
  * Deque University [1.3.2.a Reading Order](https://dequeuniversity.com/class/wcag-conformance/interpreting/wcag/a/1.3.2/1.3.2.a) says:
    * > The meaning of the content is changed and there isn’t a programmatic way to understand the intended meaning OR
    * > Meaningful content is completely skipped by the screen reader OR
    * > Hidden content is read inappropriately
  * Example: [Issue 7691](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7691)
* [Guideline Alignment] Must code line numbers output by SRs? [#334](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/334)

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 1.3.2](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#132-meaningful-sequence)
* [MAS 1.3.2: Meaningful Sequence Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.3.2-Meaningful-Sequence-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 1.3.2: Meaningful Sequence](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence)
* Source order vs Display order vs Keyboard order
  * The following resources provide some helpful information related to why source order, display order, and keyboard order are so important:
    * [HTML Source Order vs CSS Display Order | Adrian Roselli](https://adrianroselli.com/2015/10/html-source-order-vs-css-display-order.html)
    * [Source Order Matters | Adrian Roselli](https://adrianroselli.com/2015/09/source-order-matters.html)
    * [Accessibility reading order VS DOM order in a list of events | Stack Exchange](https://ux.stackexchange.com/questions/148141/accessibility-reading-order-vs-dom-order-in-a-list-of-events/148146#148146)
    * [Source Order vs Display Order vs Keyboard Focus Order video | AccessibilityOz](https://www.accessibilityoz.com/resources/videos/source-order-vs-display-order-vs-keyboard-focus-order/_)
    * [Solving the CSS layout and source order disconnect | Rachel Andrew | Chrome for Developers Blog](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/reading-order)

documents.title: 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics (2.0 A)

## In brief

Ensure controls are described by name and not just by appearance or location for those who benefit from non-visual instructions.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Instructions provided for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, color, size, visual location, orientation, or sound.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Instructions for navigating the steps of a pull request are described as "To navigate to the next step, press the button to the right. To go back to previous page, press the button to the left." | The instructions instead state "To navigate to the next step, press the 'Next' step, or press the 'Previous' button to go back to the previous step." |
| The instructions for navigating through a set of recommended changes describes that you press the square button to accept the recommendation or the circle button to make your own edits. | The instructions provide the names of the button labels instead of the visual appearance of the buttons. |
| Instructions say: Read the green text above to learn more. | Instructions say: To learn more, read the section under the heading Further Info. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **An additional information is not defined for the 'Pencil shaped icon' i.e., present at the left side of the 'GitHub discussions homepage'** [Issue 3459](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/3459)
  * The pencil icon used to represent the ability to edit categories isn't accessibly labeled to help clarify to users what its purpose.
  * Due to this, its purpose depends on the user being able to see the symbol, recognize it, and make assumptions about it.
  * This results in users with visual or cognitive disabilities to struggle with understanding the purpose of the control.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional guidance

* For requirements related to color, refer to [Guideline 1.4](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#distinguishable).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* None at this time.

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 1.3.3](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#133-sensory-characteristics)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/sensory-characteristics)

documents.title: 1.3.4 Orientation (2.1 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.3.4 Orientation (2.1 AA)

## In brief

Content allows for the user to view the UI in portrait or landscape view without loss of information or functionality.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation, such as portrait or landscape, unless a specific display orientation is [essential](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/orientation#dfn-essential).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| The user moves their device in landscape view and part of a button gets clipped off resulting in its label appearing as "Watch" instead of "Watching" implying that the user is not currently watching it. | The user moves their device in landscape view all content is still available and readable including the button label "Watching". |
| The user rotates their view from portrait to landscape. However, the UI is locked in portrait view. | The user moves their devices between landscape and portrait view and the UI adjusts so that there is no loss of content or functionality. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Lost Information and Functionality with Larger Text Sizes and/or Landscape Orientation** [Issue 1549](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/1549)
  * In the case of this issue, functionality is lost when the viewport is switched from portrait to landscape.
  * Functionality should remain available regardless of the orientation of their device.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional guidance

* Examples where a particular display orientation may be essential are a bank check, a piano application, slides for a projector or television, or virtual reality content where content is not necessarily restricted to landscape or portrait display orientation.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 1.3.4](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#134-orientation)
* [MAS 1.3.4: Orientation Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.3.4--Orientation-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 1.3.4 Orientation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/orientation)

documents.title: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (2.1 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (2.1 AA)

## In brief

Ensure that the purpose of a form input collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined, so they can be conveyed to users using different browsers, assistive technologies, and input methods.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be [programmatically determined](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-input-purpose#dfn-programmatically-determined) when:
>
> - The input field serves a purpose identified in the [Input Purposes for user interface components section](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#input-purposes); and
> - The content is implemented using technologies with support for identifying the expected meaning for form input data.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A payment form has input fields for the user's name, address, phone number, but the user is unable to autofill them using the browser's auto fill functionality. | The user is able to autofill the name, address, and phone number input fields. |
| A shipping address form features input fields with their `tyoe` and `autocomplete` attributes set incorrectly or disabled (i.e., `autocomplete="family-name"` on a field labeled as "First Name" or `autocomplete="off"`. | The input fields have `autocomplete` and `type` attributes set based on their purpose and expected content. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Autocomplete attribute is not correct for the form field ‘Name on Card’** [Issue 2705](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/2705)
  * In this case, the `autocomplete` attribute is incorrect, which means users who use autocomplete to fill in fields and avoid errors in the information they enter, particularly fields that may show up repeatedly on a site, may enter incorrect information.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional guidance

* The HTML `type` attribute allows for input type to be broadly set. Then the `autocomplete` attribute allows a more fine-grained definition or identification of purpose than the `type` attribute due to its limited, specific, well-defined fixed values. As a result, you can use just the `type` attribute, or combine it with the `autocomplete` when appropriate.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 1.3.5](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#135-identify-input-purpose)
* [MAS 1.3.5: Identify Input Purpose Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.3.5--Identify-Input-Purpose-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-input-purpose)
* [`<input>` Types | `<input>`: The HTML Input element | Mozilla Developer Network](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#input_types)
* [HTML attribute: `autocomplete` | Mozilla Developer Network](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/autocomplete)
* [7. Input Purposes for User Interface Components | WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#input-purposes)

documents.title: 1.4.1 Use of Color (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.4.1 Use of Color (2.0 A)

## In brief

Color isn't the only way that information and actions are communicated.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 1**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Text links adjacent to regular text are identified using color alone. | Text links adjacent to regular text are underlined, unless set to not be underlined in the current user's GitHub accessibility settings. |
| An invalid form field is indicated using color alone. | In addition to any color treatment, an error message is displayed adjacent to the field. |
| A chart relies on users being able to match labels in a legend to data using color alone. | A chart uses other methods besides color to identify data. For example, text labels appear directly on the data without having to match colors to a separate legend. |
| Items in a list are color coded to indicate a particular state or purpose. | In addition to color, the difference between the items is communicated in some other visual way (such as text or an icon). |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Link 'Support' has insufficient color contrast 1.3:1 with the surrounding text** [Issue 11463](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11463)
  * The link text differs from surrounding text by color alone.
  * This will make it difficult for users who are colorblind or low vision to differentiate linked text from unlinked text.
  * The preferred resolution would be to let the links be underlined all the time.
* **Color is the sole medium to indicate level of contributions** [Issue 11202](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11202)
  * The contribution graph on a user's profile only differentiates the level of contribution by color.
  * As a result, users who are low vision or colorblind may struggle to interpret the contribution graph.
* **Color is the sole medium to indicate the progress bars** [Issue 10555](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10555)
  * The different sections of the progress bars are only differentiated from each other and in their meaning by color.
  * There should be a method other than color that can be used to differentiate between the sections of the progress bar.
* **Color is the sole medium to identify the 'partial outage' time on a particular date** [Issue 6091](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/6091)
  * The different bars representing uptime and various levels of outage are only differentiated from each other by color.
  * There should be a method other than color that can be used to differentiate between the bars.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Inline linked text has a 3:1 color contrast with surrounding text and has an underline on hover or focus. | Inline linked text has a 3:1 color contrast with surrounding text and is underlined at all times. |

## Additional guidance

* This should not discourage the use of color on a page, or even color coding, as long as it is also conveyed via text.
* Regarding text links, this success criterion mostly pertains to blocks of text. Isolated linked text within a design convention (such as a footer) or paired with an icon are an exception and not a violation.
* Regarding text links, instances of linked text appearing inline with other text of the same color, without any visual differentiation between the two, is a usability issue that creates an overall poor user experience. However, it does not fail this success criterion.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* Update guidance on 1.4.1 Use of Color to explicitly call out links presented in isolation [#266](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/266).

## Primer resources

* [Color considerations: don't rely on color alone | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/color-considerations#dont-rely-on-color-alone)

## Other resources

* [Understanding SC 1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [WCAG Helper 1.4.1](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#141-use-of-color)
* [WCAG 2.0 and Link Colors | WebAIM](https://webaim.org/blog/wcag-2-0-and-link-colors/)
* [WCAG Technique G183: Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text and providing additional visual cues on hover for links or controls where color alone is used to identify them](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/general/G183)
* [WCAG Technique F73: Failure of Success Criterion 1.4.1 due to creating links that are not visually evident without color vision](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/failures/F73)
* [Links must be distinguished from surrounding text in a way that does not rely on color | Deque University](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/html/4.4/link-in-text-block)
* [Designing for Web Accessibility | WAI | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tips/designing/)

documents.title: 1.4.10 Reflow (2.1 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.4.10 Reflow (2.1 AA)

## In brief

People with low vision need to enlarge text and read it in a single column.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions for:
>
> * Vertical scrolling content at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels;
> * Horizontal scrolling content at a height equivalent to 256 CSS pixels.
>
> Except for parts of the content which require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| When adjusting the viewport size, content becomes hidden / cut off. | Content is fully viewable even as it adjusts to different viewport sizes. |
| When adjusting the viewport size, content is overlapping which makes it unreadable. | Content does not overlap as it adjusts to different viewport sizes. |
| When adjusting the viewport size, two-dimensional scrolling is required to read content. | One-dimensional scrolling is required to read content even when adjusting to different viewport sizes. |
| Search autocomplete is not available on mobile web but is on desktop web. | Search autocomplete is available on both mobile and desktop web. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following issues are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Two-dimensional scrolling is required to read the contents of the page upon setting the viewport to 320*256 px accessibility-audits** [Issue 10962](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10962)
  * When the screen size is narrowed, the content is cut off in such a way that the user must scroll horizontally in order to view everything.
  * Content should instead reflow so that the user only has to scroll vertically.
* **On setting viewport to 320*256 pixel mode, left navigation is disappearing** [Issue 11490](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11490)
  * Navigation controls get cut off and become inaccessible to users on smaller displays.
  * Content should instead reflow and scale to still be accessible.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Upon adjusting to different viewport sizes, scrollbars appear but two-dimensional scrolling is not required to read the content. | No scrollbars appear. |
| Content is partially overlapping but still can be read. | Content does not overlap at all. |
| Data table displays via horizontal and vertical scrollbars. | Data table layout is responsive and understandable without requiring both horizontal and vertical scrolling. |

## How to test 1.4.10 Reflow

### Websites

1. Set the browser window size to 1280px width by 1024px height.
2. Adjust browser zoom to 400%.
3. Confirm the website content is visible when scrolling in a single direction.

### Desktop Applications (Windows/MacOS)

1. Set your screen resolution to 1280px width by 1024px height.
2. Maximize the application window.
3. Use OS zoom to increase the size of the application’s content by 400%.
4. Confirm the application scrolls in only a single direction.

### Android / iOS

Not applicable.

## Additional guidance

* Truncated text is generally a fail of this success criterion -- but it passes if the text is still available via either of these use cases:
  * is revealed via accessible controls on the same screen
  * is accessible via a link directly to the content
* Exceptions include the following as they may require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning: preformatted code, maps, diagrams, video, games, presentations, data tables, etc.
* For horizontal navigation menus, the menu bar may scroll horizontally, but each individual menu item must fit horizontally within the viewport.
* A carousel may scroll horizontally but each individual panel must fit horizontally within the viewport. Each panel may scroll vertically.
* When testing Reflow, if scrollable content is discovered and not accessible by keyboard, the issue is to be reported under 2.1.1 Keyboard.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When options of a select dropdown are wider than the viewport, report as a moderate usability issue — labels `A11yUsable` and `Severity-3`. The suggested fix is to switch to a radio list and/or shorten the option label text. See [#205](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/205).
* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

* [Understanding SC 1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow)
* [MAS 1.4.10: Reflow Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.4.10--Reflow-Guide.aspx)
* [WCAG Helper 1.4.10](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#1410-reflow)
* [Zooming and scaling must not be disabled | Deque University](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.4/meta-viewport)

documents.title: 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast (2.1 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast (2.1 AA) ## In brief Important graphical information needs to meet 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. > [!IMPORTANT] > When testing this SC on GitHub.com, the tester must turn on the "Increase contrast" setting. When logged in, the setting is located in the GitHub UI under [Settings > Appearance](https://github.com/settings/appearance) page. If logged out, after navigating to the page to be tested, select the settings button in the global nav and activate it in the dialog which appears. (Starting June 5, 2025) ## Normative This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion. > The visual [presentation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast#dfn-presentation) of the following have a [contrast ratio](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast#dfn-contrast-ratio) of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s): > > - **User Interface Components** > - Visual information required to identify [user interface components](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast#dfn-user-interface-component) and [states](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast#dfn-state), except for inactive components or where the appearance of the component is determined by the user agent and not modified by the author; > - **Graphical Objects** > - Parts of graphics required to understand the content, except when a particular presentation of graphics is [essential](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast#dfn-essential) to the information being conveyed. ## Examples of failures **Default severity level: 2** This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md). With each of these failures, you can view the [Visual Examples section](#visual-examples) to see them and other examples displayed. | Actual | Expected | |--------|----------| | A text input boundary has insufficient contrast with the adjacent background. | The text input boundary has sufficient contrast (3:1) with the adjacent background. | | A checkbox has a dark border that has sufficient contrast with the adjacent background. However, when checked, the check mark does not have sufficient contrast with the fill of the checkbox. | The checkmark inside the checkbox has at least 3:1 contrast with the fill of the checkbox. | | A button that is blue adjacent to a white background, gains a light yellow outline when it has keyboard focus. This outline has sufficient contrast with the adjacent blue button, but not with the adjacent white background. | The yellow outline is either placed just inside the blue of the button so it has blue on either side, which results in sufficient contrast (3:1). Alternatively, the yellow could be changed to a single or two tone outline coloration that gives sufficient contrast against both the adjacent button and background. | ### Example GitHub issues The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC. * **Luminosity contrast ratio of the focus indicator for 'Enterprise trial' control is 1.4:1** [Issue 11441](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11441) * The focus indicator around the "Enterprise trial" control is less than 3:1 with content on either side of it. * The focus indicator needs to have sufficient contrast with content inside and outside of it. * **Luminosity contrast ratio for the selected tab indicator(orange) is 2.3:1** [Issue 11199](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11199) * The underline that is meant to show which tab is currently selected is less than 3:1 with the background. * This could make it difficult for low vision or colorblind users to perceive it. ## Examples of usability issues and best practices **Default severity level: 4** These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG. | Actual | Preferred | |--------|-----------| | A button does not have a visual boundary to indicate the hit area and better identify the control location/type. | Give the button a visual border that has at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent backgrounds. | | An icon has sufficient contrast with its accompanying text label, but not against the adjacent background. | The icon has at least 3:1 contrast with the background. | ## Visual Examples | Insufficient Contrast | Sufficient Contrast | |:---------------------:|:-------------------:| | | | | | | | | | | |

| | | | ### Boundaries The following two images are an example of how 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast does not require a button to have a border with sufficient contrast if the text has sufficient contrast and the border is not the only way to identify it as a button. Both of these images would be passing since the text within them has sufficient contrast with the background, as long as they are still identifiable from surrounding text as buttons. However, the second image is the best practice since it has both the border and text of sufficient contrast, which allows the user to more clearly identify the hit area of the button. This does not apply to the focus state of the button, which still must maintain proper contrast. ## Additional guidance * If a button, input, etc. DOES NOT have a visual border, but still has text to identify it, then [1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum) applies. * When the button does have a border, and the border does not meet the 3:1 contrast ratio requirement of the 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast SC, it can still be passing if it has a text label that meets the 4.5:1 contrast ratio of the 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) SC. * This success criterion DOES NOT require that controls have a visual boundary indicating the hit area, but if the visual indicator of the control is the only way to identify the control, then that indicator must have sufficient contrast (3:1). * This success criterion is heavily related to [1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color) because of how the appearance of a component changes to indicate a change in state (hover, active, unselected, keyboard focus, etc) or value. * This success criterion is heavily related to [2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible) since the visual focus indicator needs to have sufficient contrast with surrounding content so that a keyboard user can identify where focus is. * Issues discovered via Windows high-contrast themes in OS/device settings are not WCAG violations. * As a result, there are a limited scope of situations where we still report these issues. * For more details, refer to the [Severity 4 Issue Reporting doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/sev-4-issue-reporting.md). * Issues discovered involving the Light and Dark GitHub themes should be `Severity-2`. ## Accessibility Council decisions * When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md). ## Resources This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it. * [WCAG Helper 1.4.11](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#1411-non-text-contrast) * [MAS 1.4.11: Non-Text Contrast Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.4.11-Non-Text-Contrast-Guide.aspx) * [Understanding SC 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast) * **Primer Components** * [Checkbox Group Component](https://primer.style/components/checkbox-group) * [Form Control Component](https://primer.style/components/form-control) * [Radio Component](https://primer.style/components/radio) * [Radio Group Component](https://primer.style/components/radio-group) * [Tab Component](https://primer.style/components/tab-panels) * [Toggle Switch Component](https://primer.style/components/toggle-switch)

documents.title: 1.4.12 Text Spacing (2.1 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.4.12 Text Spacing (2.1 AA)

## In brief

When a user adjusts text spacing, the content is still readable and functional.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> In content implemented using markup languages that support the following text style properties, no loss of content or functionality occurs by setting all of the following and by changing no other style property:
>
> - Line height (line spacing) to at least 1.5 times the font size;
> - Spacing following paragraphs to at least 2 times the font size;
> - Letter spacing (tracking) to at least 0.12 times the font size;
> - Word spacing to at least 0.16 times the font size.
>
> - Exception: Human languages and scripts that do not make use of one or more of these text style properties in written text can conform using only the properties that exist for that combination of language and script.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| While viewing a list of Branches in a Repo Pull Request window, a user adjusts the text spacing for easier reading. Upon doing so, the text is truncated so that a user is unable to read all the content. | The text and its container is developed so that the content is able to reflow without loss of content or functionality when spacing is overridden by the user. |
| A user attempts to adjust the spacing of text for improved readability while reviewing an Issue that was submitted. However, the text is set to a fixed width that prevents overriding spacing. | Text spacing is able to be overridden by users as needed without the loss of content or functionality. (See [Technique C36](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C36)) |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Upon applying text spacing, 'Source repository' text is getting cutoff** [Issue 11101](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11101)
  * Upon adjusting text spacing, the options in the "Source" repo drop-down menu get cut off.
  * They should instead resize so that the user can read all the options.
* **Upon applying text spacing, 'Choose a JSON File to upload' text is getting truncated** [Issue 11048](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11048)
  * Upon adjusting text spacing, the "Choose a JSON File to upload" option is truncated so a user may not be able to properly read the option.
* **Upon applying text spacing, controls are getting overlapped** [Issue 10446](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10446)
  * Upon adjusting text spacing, controls end up overlapping so a user may have difficulty reading the labels or activating the correct control.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None

<!-- | Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | -->

## Additional guidance

* Truncated text is generally a fail of this success criterion -- but it passes if the text is still available via either of these use cases:
  * is revealed via accessible controls on the same screen
  * is accessible via a link directly to the content
* Content is not required to use these text spacing values. The requirement is to ensure that when a user overrides the authored text spacing, content or functionality is not lost.
* An embedded code block is an exception; if the code doesn't wrap but a scrollbar is provided, it is conformant as the formatting is required to preserve its meaning.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* In cases where meaningful content is truncated, or otherwise hidden visually, but is still announced by screen reader, [1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence) applies.
* Per [WCAG Technique C35](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C35), where text is not intended to wrap, authors should either:
  * size containers to a have a value greater than the default width of the text, or
  * allow the containers to expand in the direction of text.
* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).
