documents.title: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (2.1 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (2.1 AA)

## In brief

Ensure content that becomes visible or hidden based on mouse hover or keyboard focus is perceivable and predictable.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Where receiving and then removing pointer hover or keyboard focus triggers additional content to become visible and then hidden, the following are true:
>
> - **Dismissible**
>   - A [mechanism](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus#dfn-mechanism) is available to dismiss the additional content without moving pointer hover or keyboard focus, unless the additional content communicates an [input error](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus#dfn-input-error) or does not obscure or replace other content;
> - **Hoverable**
>   - If pointer hover can trigger the additional content, then the pointer can be moved over the additional content without the additional content disappearing;
> - **Persistent**
>   - The additional content remains visible until the hover or focus trigger is removed, the user dismisses it, or its information is no longer valid.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A tooltip on a button displays upon mouse hover or keyboard focus. The tooltip blocks other content on the page when it displays and can only be dismissed by tabbing off the control or moving the mouse off the control. | The tooltip can be dismissed by pressing the Escape key without moving the mouse or keyboard focus off the control. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Copilot Chat UI gets closed upon closing the time stamp tooltip of the generated codeblock** [Issue 7967](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7967)
  * Upon placing focus on the timestamp, a tooltip appears. However, that tooltip cannot be closed by using an expected control, the <kbd>Esc</kbd> key.
* **Hovercards can't be dismissed without moving mouse/pointer** [Issue 7797](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7797)
  * The hovercards can be invoked by giving the triggering content keyboard of mouse focus.
  * However, they then are unable to be collapsed with the expected keyboard control, <kbd>Esc</kbd> key.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional guidance

* Exception: The visual presentation of the additional content is controlled by the user agent and is not modified by the author.
  * Examples of additional content controlled by the user agent include browser tooltips created through use of the HTML [`title` attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#the-title-attribute).
* Custom tooltips, sub-menus, and other nonmodal popups that display on hover and focus are examples of additional content covered by this criterion.
* This criterion applies to content that appears in addition to the triggering component itself. Since hidden components that are made visible on keyboard focus (such as links used to skip to another part of a page) do not present additional content they are not covered by this criterion.
* Modal dialogs are out of scope for this criterion because they must take keyboard focus and thus should not appear on hover or focus. Refer to [Success Criterion 3.2.1, On Focus](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#on-focus).
* Content which can be triggered via pointer hover should also be able to be triggered by keyboard focus. Refer to [Success Criterion 2.1.1, Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#keyboard).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

* [MAS 1.4.13: Content on Hover or Focus Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.4.13-Content-on-Hover-or-Focus-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus)

documents.title: 1.4.2 Audio Control (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.4.2 Audio Control (2.0 A)

## In brief

If you play audio content automatically, let people turn it down or off.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> If any audio on a Web page plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, either a [mechanism](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-control#dfn-mechanism) is available to pause or stop the audio, or a mechanism is available to control audio volume independently from the overall system volume level.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Music begins playing when a page loads. It plays for longer than 3 seconds and there is no mechanism present within the page to allow the user to stop the content. | No audio automatically plays without the user initiating it. (See [Technique G171](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/general/G171)) |
| An audio clip of a keynote speech automatically begins playing when the user loads an event page. There is no mechanism present within the page to allow the user to stop the audio content. | A control is present near the top of the page that allows a user to stop the audio content. (See [Technique G170](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/general/G170)) |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* None
<!--
* **placeholder** [Issue NUMBER](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/NUMBER)
  * Description
-->

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| An audio clip automatically begins playing when a user loads a page. The audio clip plays for longer than 3 seconds, but a control at the top of the page allows the user to stop the audio. | Audio content on a page that plays for longer than 3 seconds only plays when the user initiates it. |

## Additional guidance

* Playing audio automatically when landing on a page may affect a screen reader user's ability to find the mechanism to stop it because they navigate by listening and automatically started sounds might interfere with that navigation. Therefore, we discourage the practice of automatically starting sounds (especially if they last more than 3 seconds), and encourage that the sound be started by an action initiated by the user.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

documents.title: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (2.0 A)

## In brief

Text must have a color contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for large text (3:1), inactive or decorative text, and text in logos or brand names, which have no contrast requirement.

> [!NOTE]
> Large text is defined as 24px for regular text and 19px for bold text.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for the following:
>
> ### Large Text
>
> Large-scale text and images of large-scale text have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1;
>
> ### Incidental
>
> Text or images of text that are part of an inactive user interface component, that are pure decoration, that are not visible to anyone, or that are part of a picture that contains significant other visual content, have no contrast requirement.
>
> ### Logotypes
>
> Text that is part of a logo or brand name has no contrast requirement.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Regular text has a color contrast ratio of less than 4.5:1 against its background. | Regular text has a color contrast ratio of 4.5:1 or higher against its background.|
| Large text has a color contrast ratio of less than 3:1 against its background. | Large text has a color contrast ratio of 3:1 or higher against its background. |

### Guidance for severity level 3

A severity level of 3 should be applied to regular text (not large text) which has a color contrast ratio greater than 4.2:1 and less than 4.5:1.

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Luminosity ratio for the 'String' link is less than 4.5:1** [Issue 11479](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11479)
  * If it was due to it having insufficient contrast with surrounding unlinked text, it would fall under 1.4.1 Use of Color.
  * However, since it is due to insufficient contrast with the background, it falls under 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) instead.
  * All text needs to have at least 4.5:1 contrast with the background.
* **The luminosity ratio of the placeholder text 'Query Name' is 3.5:1, which is less than 4.5:1** [Issue 5020](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/5020)
  * The placeholder text has less than 4.5:1 contrast with the background.
  * It needs to be darkened so that it has 4.5:1 contrast with the background.
* **Luminosity contrast ratio for 'Search references' placeholder text is 4.3:1** [Issue 7202](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7202)
  * The placeholder text has less than 4.5:1 contrast with the background.
  * The ratio is 4.3:1 so it is labeled severity 3.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- | Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | -->

## Additional guidance

* Issues discovered via Windows high-contrast themes in OS/device settings are not WCAG violations.
   * As a result, there are a limited scope of situations where we still report these issues.
   * For more details, refer to the [Severity 4 Issue Reporting doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/sev-4-issue-reporting.md).
* Issues discovered involving the Light and Dark GitHub themes should be `Severity-2`.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply unless additional non-ANSI colors have been added.
  * See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Primer resources

* [Color considerations | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/color-considerations)

## Other resources

* [MAS 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum) Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.4.3-Contrast-(Minimum)-Guide.aspx)
* [WCAG Helper 1.4.3](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#143-contrast-minimum)

documents.title: 1.4.4 Resize Text (2.0 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.4.4 Resize Text (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Text can be enlarged up to 200% without loss of content or functionality.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Except for [captions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text.html#dfn-captions) and [images of text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text.html#dfn-image-of-text), [text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text.html#dfn-text) can be resized without [assistive technology](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text.html#dfn-assistive-technology) up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Content is truncated when zooming in with browser functionality to 200% to the point that some instructional text is no longer visible resulting in loss of information to the user. | By using responsive content and container sizing, the content is able to resize and reflow in such a way that content remains visible up up to 200% through the use of responsive sizing. |
| A form control disappears when zooming in with browser functionality to 200% to the point that the control can not be viewed or used. This results in a loss of functionality. | By using responsive content and container sizing, the content is able to resize and reflow in such a way that control remains visible up up to 200% through the use of responsive sizing. |
| The label on a button disappears or runs behind other content when the user zooms in up to 200%. As a result the user cannot read the label for the control and understand its purpose. | Through the use of responsive techniques the label, its container, and the control all resize in such a way that they are still readable and functional up to 200% browser zoom. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **'Load 151 More Items' gets truncated in larger accessibility sizes** [Issue 11504](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11504)
  * When text is resized, content gets truncated so the user is unable to read it anymore.
  * Text and surrounding content/controls should resize and reflow so that users can zoom in if needed without having to scroll horizontally and without loss of information or functionality.
* **Filter buttons are not adapting to larger accessibility sizes** [Issue 11246](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11246)
  * Controls and content get cut off when the user uses larger text scaling settings on their device because it does not properly resize and reflow.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A small portion of text is obscured when the user zooms in up to 200% and is still easily readable. | Text is not obscured at all when the user zooms in up to 200%. |

## How to test 1.4.4 Resize Text

When testing the 1.4.4 Resize Text SC, it is important to verify the following rules:

- Ensure all visible text is resized as per applied level.
- Ensure text is readable and reflows to new lines. When reflowing is not possible, ensure text can be read even with characters clipped at the end.
- Ensure scrollbars are provided whenever text is resized to accommodate the set level.
- Ensure if user is navigating through keyboard only then auto scroll should be implemented and work according to set level.

### Desktop Applications

For all testing of this SC on Desktop applications, you will first need to:

1. Go to Settings > System > Display.
2. To ensure consistent testing,
   1. Set your system resolution to 1280px width by 1024px height.
   2. Set the scaling to 100%.

#### Option 1: Testing resize Text via OS Zoom

Go to Settings > System > Display and, using Custom Scaling, set the Scale size to 200%.

#### Option 2: Testing Resize Text via “Make text bigger” (Windows 10 October 2018 Update and beyond)

The October 2018 Update introduced a new feature labelled “Make text bigger.”  

1. Press <kbd>Windows</kbd> and <kbd>U</kbd> to open the Accessibility settings.
2. Select "Text size" from the displayed options.
3. Adjust the text size preview slider to 200% and select "Apply".

### Websites

For all testing of websites in a desktop browser:

- Set your browser dimensions to 1280px width by 1024px height.
- Set the browser's zoom setting to 200%. On most browsers the zoom can be activated with either:
   - <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Plus</kbd> (Mac)
   - <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Plus</kbd> (Windows)

### Android

#### Option 1: Testing Resize text in Android applications

Go to Settings -> Accessibility -> Font size -> Set the slider to max value.

#### Option 2: Testing Resize text in Android websites and webapps in Chrome

In Chrome, go to Settings -> Accessibility -> Increase Text scaling to 200%.

#### Option 3: Testing Resize text in Android websites and webapps in Edge

In Edge, go to Settings -> Accessibility -> Increase Text scaling to 200%.

### iOS

#### Option 1: Testing Resize text in iOS applications

Go to Settings -> Accessibility -> Display & Text Size -> Larger Text -> Set the slider to max value.

#### Option 2: Testing Resize text in Safari websites and webapps

Select the page settings button and interact with the Page Scale Control to adjust zoom to 200%.

## Additional guidance

* Truncated text is generally a fail of this success criterion -- but it passes if the text is still available via either of these use cases:
  * is revealed via accessible controls on the same screen
  * is accessible via a link directly to the content
* The intent of this Success Criterion is to ensure that visually rendered text, including controls and labels using text, can be made larger so that it can be read more easily by people with milder visual impairments, without requiring the use of assistive technology (such as a screen magnifier). Users may benefit from scaling all content on the Web page, but text is most critical.
* Images of text do not scale as well as text because they tend to pixelate, and therefore we suggest using text wherever possible. It is also harder to change foreground and background contrast and color combinations for images of text, which are necessary for some users. See [1.4.5 Images of Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/images-of-text).
* As with most other Success Criteria, this criterion applies to each variation of the page that is automatically presented for various screen sizes (e.g. media query variations in a responsive site). In an implementation where text does not consistently increase its size as people zoom in (such as when it is transformed based on a media query to adapt to small-screen usage), it must still be possible to get to 200% enlargement in order to satisfy the criterion.
* For development on iOS, it is strongly recommended to support [dynamic type and text scaling](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/scaling-fonts-automatically) to the fullest extent possible.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

* [WCAG Helper 1.4.4](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#144-resize-text)
* [MAS 1.4.4: Resize Text Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.4.4-Resize-Text-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 1.4.4 Resize Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text.html)
* [Zooming and scaling must not be disabled | Deque University](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.4/meta-viewport)

documents.title: 1.4.5 Images of Text (2.0 AA)
documents.content:
# 1.4.5 Images of Text (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Text should be presented as text instead of as an image unless it is necessary (i.e., logos).

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> If the technologies being used can achieve the visual presentation, text is used to convey information rather than images of text except for the following:
>
> * **Customizable**
>   * The image of text can be visually customized to the user's requirements;
> * **Essential**
>   * A particular presentation of text is essential to the information being conveyed.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A banner of text is presented as an image with alt text that matches the content of the image. | CSS is used to style the text in HTML instead of using an image. ([C22](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C22)) |
| A list of statistics are displayed as an image rather than as text. | Use sematic HTML list elements and CSS to display the information as text. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* None available at this time.

documents.title: 2.1.1 Keyboard (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.1.1 Keyboard (2.0 A)

## In brief

A user can access all content and functionality with a keyboard (except features explicitly based around freehand movements; for example, drawing with a mouse).

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement and not just the endpoints.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 1**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Link or button cannot be activated by keyboard. | Link or button receives keyboard focus and can be activated by keyboard. |
| Selecting an option is not accessible by keyboard. | Option can be selected by keyboard. |
| Tooltip does not open by keyboard. | Tooltip appears and remains visible while the associated element has keyboard focus. |
| Scrollable content is not accessible by keyboard. | Content inside a scrolling container can be revealed using the keyboard. |
| Draggable column separator control is not accessible using the keyboard. | Draggable column separator control can be manipulated using the keyboard. |
| Controls are accessible while navigating in a forward direction (Tab), but not by going backward (Shift + Tab) | It is possible to move both forwards (Tab) and backwards (Shift + Tab) though focusable elements. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Timestamp is not accessible via keyboard** [Issue 11505](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11505)
  * The user is unable to activate the timestamp control when using a keyboard.
  * This is important for users who may need to use a keyboard or navigate through controls using swipes and gestures commonly used with a screen reader.
* **Content which appears after invoking 'Show more details' control is not accessible via keyboard** [Issue 11482](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11482)
  * The "Show more" control, indicated by an ellipses icon, is not able to be invoked by keyboard.
  * This is important for users who may need to use a keyboard or navigate through controls using swipes and gestures commonly used with a screen reader.
* **Unable to adjust the recommended size after uploading the image.** [Issue 11354](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11354)
  * The controls to resize uploaded images cannot be used by a keyboard user.
  * They are only accessible when using a mouse.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Dialog has an explicit close button but doesn't close when pressing Esc on the keyboard. | Dialog closes when the Esc key is pressed, returning focus to the original location. |
| Keyboard interaction doesn’t follow the platform/user agent conventions. For example, if a custom button only fires via Enter (or another key) and not Spacebar. | Keyboard interaction follows platform/user agent conventions. |

## Additional guidance

* If the Loom extension is installed, it can interfere with testing for this success criterion, and the [2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts) criterion. As described in a [comment from `@JoyceZhu`](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/3110#issuecomment-2599064096), the extension overrides some keyboard shortcuts within the browser. Thus, it is recommended that the extension be disabled prior to testing.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* None

## Resources

* [Understanding SC 2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html)
* [MAS 2.1.1: Keyboard Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-2.1.1-Keyboard-Guide.aspx)
* [WCAG Helper 2.1.1](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#211-keyboard)
* [I Used The Web For A Day With Just A Keyboard | Chris Ashton | Smashing Magazine](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2018/07/web-with-just-a-keyboard/)

documents.title: 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (2.0 A)

## In brief

Ensure users are able to use a keyboard to navigate throughout the UI and not get trapped.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> If keyboard focus can be moved to a component of the page using a [keyboard interface](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap#dfn-keyboard-interface), then focus can be moved away from that component using only a keyboard interface, and, if it requires more than unmodified arrow or tab keys or other standard exit methods, the user is advised of the method for moving focus away.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A user tabs into a form control and then is unable to tab forward or backwards to get back out. | A user tabs into a form control and is able to tab forward or backwards to get back out. |
| A user's keyboard focus is trapped and cannot be exited with typical keyboard functions (commonly the tab key). There is a custom key that can be used, but it is not communicated to the user. | Ensure that the keyboard function for advancing focus, if something other than standard controls, is documented in an accessible manner prior to where the user would enter the content. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Keyboard focus gets trapped on slider** [Issue 11469](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11469)
  * In this issue, when the user is navigating the page via keyboard, keyboard focus gets trapped in the slider and so the user cannot navigate further.
* **Keyboard focus gets trapped inside the 'Terminal' tab** [Issue 10860](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10860)
  * Upon navigating to the Terminal tab on the page via keyboard, the user's focus gets stuck in that tab preventing them from navigating to other content or further down the page.
* **Keyboard focus gets trapped inside the multiline edit field** [Issue 9666](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9666)
  * When the user tabs into the multiline edit field, they are then unable to exit the field to interact with other content on the page.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional guidance

* Since any content that does not meet this success criterion can interfere with a user's ability to use the whole page, all content on the Web page (whether it is used to meet other success criteria or not) must meet this success criterion. See [Conformance Requirement 5: Non-Interference](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#cc5).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* None

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 2.1.2](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#212-no-keyboard-traps)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap)
* [Technique G21: Ensuring that users are not trapped in content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/general/G21)

documents.title: 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (2.1 A)
documents.content:
# 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (2.1 A)

## In brief

Ensure single character shortcut keys can be turned off or modified to reduce accidental activation of keyboard shortcuts.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> If a [keyboard shortcut](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts#dfn-keyboard-shortcut) is implemented in content using only letter (including upper- and lower-case letters), punctuation, number, or symbol characters, then at least one of the following is true:
>
> - **Turn off**
>   - A [mechanism](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts#dfn-mechanism) is available to turn the shortcut off;
> - **Remap**
>   - A mechanism is available to remap the shortcut to include one or more non-printable keyboard keys (e.g., Ctrl, Alt);
> - **Active only on focus**
>   - The keyboard shortcut for a [user interface component](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts#dfn-user-interface-component) is only active when that component has focus.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| An application uses the single key shortcut S to bring up a search popup. There is no setting available to turn off or modify the shortcut. (See [WCAG Failure 99](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/failures/F99)) | A mechanism is provided to disable or remap the shortcut keys. |
| In an email application, a user can press X to delete an email. This keyboard shortcut works even when the user's keyboard focus is outside the email list grid. | The keyboard shortcut only functions when the user's keyboard focus is on one of the emails inside the email list grid. |
| Keyboard shortcuts are provided in Visual Studio Code to activate certain features with no option to remap them when they interfere with other applications, including assistive technologies. | An option is provided to allow a user to remap a keyboard shortcut. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following issues are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Single shortcut is defined for the Send button** [Issue 10987](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10987)
  * A single shortcut is set for the send button. The shortcut cannot be disabled or remapped.
  * This could cause conflict with other applications or extensions the user uses.
  * Users with fine motor control impairments, low vision, and more may also be at risk of inadvertently triggering the shortcut if they cannot disable or remap it.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->

## Additional guidance

* If the Loom extension is installed, it can interfere with testing for this success criterion, and the [2.1.1 Keyboard Accessible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard) criterion. Thus, it is recommended that the extension be disabled prior to testing.
  * As [identified by an Accessibility engineer](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/3110#issuecomment-2599064096), the Loom is auto-installed on some user machines, and takes over some keyboard shortcuts, including the <kbd>Shift+Alt+C</kbd> shortcut, which cause the browser to misinterpret the hotkeys pressed by the user.
* The Success Criterion also applies to situations where a shortcut is based on a sequence of printable character keys – for example, pressing G and then A in quick succession to trigger an action since they still rely on printable character keys.
  * If instead of a sequence, a shortcut consists of a chord of one non-printable keyboard key (e.g., Ctrl, Alt) pressed in conjunction with a printable character key, then this is allowed (e.g., <kbd>Alt+F</kbd> to open a Find menu).
* This success criterion doesn't affect components such as listboxes and drop-down menus. Although these components contain values (words) that may be selected by one or more character keys, the shortcuts are only active when the components have focus.
* [Accesskeys](https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/single-page.html#the-accesskey-attribute) are also not affected because they are generally (depending on the user agent) activated using modifier keys.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [GitHub's engineering guidance on turning off character key shortcuts](https://thehub.github.com/epd/engineering/dev-practicals/frontend/keyboard-shortcuts/#character-key-shortcuts)
* [WCAG Helper 2.1.4](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#214-character-key-shortcuts)
* [MAS 2.1.4: Character Key Shortcuts Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-2.1.4--Character-Key-Shortcuts-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts)
* [Understanding WCAG SC 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts | DigitalA11y](https://www.digitala11y.com/understanding-sc-2-1-4-character-key-shortcuts/)
* [Success Criterion 2.1.4 − Character Key Shortcuts | Hong Kong Digital Policy Office](https://www.digitalpolicy.gov.hk/en/our_work/digital_government/digital_inclusion/accessibility/promulgating_resources/handbook/new_success_criteria/wcag_214.html)

documents.title: 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (2.0 A)

## In brief

Applications that feature a timeout allow the user to adjust, turn off, or extend the timeout.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> For each time limit that is set by the content, at least one of the following is true:
>
> * **Turn off**
>   * The user is allowed to turn off the time limit before encountering it; or
> * **Adjust**
>   * The user is allowed to adjust the time limit before encountering it over a wide range that is at least ten times the length of the default setting; or
> * **Extend**
>   * The user is warned before time expires and given at least 20 seconds to extend the time limit with a simple action (for example, "press the space bar"), and the user is allowed to extend the time limit at least ten times; or
> * **Real-time Exception**
>   * The time limit is a required part of a real-time event (for example, an auction), and no alternative to the time limit is possible; or
> * **Essential Exception**
>   * The time limit is essential and extending it would invalidate the activity; or
> * **20 Hour Exception**
>   * The time limit is longer than 20 hours.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A user is filling out a form and stops for a break. The form times out without providing any warning. | The form provides a warning before timing out so that a user can reset the timeout timer without losing any entered information. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **There is no alternative way to adjust the time for auto updating content** [Issue 7908](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7908)
  * On the page, there is a section where a series of VS Code images are shown.
  * There is no mechanism given to adjust how fast it goes through the images or stop the content.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional guidance

* This success criterion helps ensure that users can complete tasks without unexpected changes in content or context that are a result of a time limit. This success criterion should be considered in conjunction with [SC 3.2.1 On Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-focus.html), which puts limits on changes of content or context as a result of user action.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* None

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 2.2.1](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#221-timing-adjustable)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable)

documents.title: 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (2.0 A)

## In brief

Allow users to pause, stop, or hide content that auto-updates, moves, blinks, or scrolls automatically to decrease distraction.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> For moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating information, all of the following are true:
>
> - **Moving, blinking, scrolling**
>   - For any moving, [blinking](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide#dfn-blinking) or scrolling information that (1) starts automatically, (2) lasts more than five seconds, and (3) is presented in parallel with other content, there is a mechanism for the user to [pause](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide#dfn-paused), stop, or hide it unless the movement, blinking, or scrolling is part of an activity where it is [essential](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide#dfn-essential); and
> - **Auto-updating**
>   - For any auto-updating information that (1) starts automatically and (2) is presented in parallel with other content, there is a mechanism for the user to pause, stop, or hide it or to control the frequency of the update unless the auto-updating is part of an activity where it is essential.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A banner across the top of the page displays notifications that automatically scroll between notifications with no option to stop the scrolling. | The notification banner doesn't auto-scroll. Instead the banner has controls that allow the user to manually switch between notifications. |
| An interactive element has an animated behavior that begins automatically when the user scrolls to it with no option to pause, stop, or hide the animation. (See the example displayed in the following [comment on Issue #9788](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9788#issuecomment-2500172042).) | The element doesn't begin moving automatically. Instead the element has controls allow the users to start/stop the movement. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **No mechanism to pause/stop/hide the auto-scrolling content** [Issue 11012](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11012)
  * There is no mechanism provided to stop the scrolling business icons on the page.
  * This could cause some users with cognitive conditions or using various assistive technologies to be disoriented or miss content.
* **No mechanism is provided to pause, stop or hide the animation** [Issue 9965](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9965)
  * The rotating animated cube at the bottom of the page cannot be paused or stopped.
  * Additionally, the way the image is built is very disorienting, creating a bit of an optical illusion.
* **There is no mechanism to pause/stop/hide the auto updating carousel images present under the 'Bored of boards? Switch to tables and roadmaps.' heading** [Issue 7911](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7911)
  * The carousel of project board images rotates through images with no mechanism available to pause or stop it.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None

## Additional guidance

* For requirements related to flickering or flashing content, refer to [Guideline 2.3](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#seizures-and-physical-reactions).
* An animation that occurs as part of a preload phase or similar situation can be considered essential and therefore is an exception (not a fail).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* [[Guideline Alignment] SC 2.2.2 and prefers-reduced-motion #36](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/36) concluded that we consider `prefers-reduced-motion` to be an example of "a mechanism for the users to pause, stop, or hide" moving content.

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 2.2.2](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#222-pause-stop-hide)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide)
* [Designing With Reduced Motion For Motion Sensitivities | Smashing Magazine](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2020/09/design-reduced-motion-sensitivities/)
* [Creating Accessible UI Animations | Smashing Magazine](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2023/11/creating-accessible-ui-animations/)
* [Accessible Web Animation: The WCAG on Animation Explained | CSS-Tricks](https://css-tricks.com/accessible-web-animation-the-wcag-on-animation-explained/)
* [Understanding SC 2.3.3: Animation from Interactions (Level AAA)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html)
* [Building Accessible Animations with prefers-reduced-motion | Dev.to](https://dev.to/ibn_abubakre/building-accessible-animations-with-prefers-reduced-motion-280a)
* [Creating Accessible UI Animations | Oriana Garcia | Smashing Magazine](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2023/11/creating-accessible-ui-animations/)

documents.title: 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (2.0 A)

## In brief

Avoid content that flashes, or keep it under WCAG-defined flashing thresholds due to the risk of it causing migraines, dizziness, nausea, and seizures. The exception allows flashing content to pass if the relative size of the flashing area is small enough (i.e. less than 25% of 10 degrees of visual field). See [WCAG Technique G176](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/general/G176) for more details on this exception.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> [Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold#dfn-web-page) do not contain anything that flashes more than three times in any one second period, or the [flash](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold#dfn-flash) is below the [general flash and red flash thresholds](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold#dfn-general-flash-and-red-flash-thresholds).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A video features a strobing background effect that flashes more than 3 times per second. | The video is swapped with a version that does not feature a strobing light. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* None
<!--
* **placeholder** [Issue NUMBER](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/NUMBER)
  * Description
* **placeholder** [Issue NUMBER](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/NUMBER)
  * Description
-->

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A video features a strobing effect that has been designed to meet the 3 or below per second threshold. | The strobing effect is removed from the video altogether. |

## Additional guidance

* It is advised to avoid large swaths of bright/vibrant color or repetitive pattern. Due to the way content loads in and refresh rates on screens, these can create a pseudo-flashing effect or cause discomfort. This is particularly noticeable on mobile screens.
  * A good example of this can be found in [History of the Disability Pride Flag](https://www.weinberg.cuimc.columbia.edu/news/history-disability-pride-flag).
* Since any content that does not meet this success criterion can interfere with a user's ability to use the whole page, all content on the Web page (whether it is used to meet other success criteria or not) must meet this success criterion. See [Conformance Requirement 5: Non-Interference](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#cc5).
* The specification cannot account for the actual viewing distance that a person chooses. Users that are closer to their screens than the idealized viewing distance will be affected by flashing areas that normatively pass. The same problem applies to users who rely on zoom or screen magnification. Conversely, users who are further away from the screen than the idealized distance should be able to tolerate flashing areas that are larger than the threshold.
  * The terms "blinking" and "flashing" can sometimes refer to the same content.
  * "Blinking" refers to content that causes a distraction problem. Blinking can be allowed for a short time as long as it stops (or can be stopped)
  * "Flashing" refers to content that can trigger a seizure (if it is more than 3 per second and large and bright enough). _This cannot ever be allowed or it could cause a seizure._ And turning the flash off is also not an option since the seizure could occur faster than most users could turn it off.
  * Blinking usually does not occur at speeds of 3 per second or more, but it can. If blinking occurs faster than 3 per second, it would also be considered a flash.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* None

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 2.3.1](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#231-three-flashes-or-below-threshold)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold)
* [IRIS | EA Games | GitHub](https://github.com/electronicarts/IRIS)
  * IRIS is a solution created by EA to identify video footage that could potentially cause photosensitive epileptic risks. IRIS is not intended to guarantee, certify or otherwise validate visual content's compliance with legal, regulatory or other requirements.
  * IRIS detects the following issues:
    * Luminance flashes
    * Red saturation flashes
    * Spatial patterns (with clear contrast and regularity between pattern components)
* [The Ganzflicker experience: High probability of seeing vivid and complex pseudo-hallucinations with imagery but not aphantasia | Science Direct](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0010945221001957)
* [Avoid contrasting patterns | Uexcel](https://app.uxcel.com/courses/design-accessibility/designing-for-epilepsy-677/avoid-contrasting-patterns-9991)
* [Web accessibility for seizures and physical reactions | Mozilla Developer Network](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/Seizure_disorders)
* [Avoid flickering images and repetitive patterns | Game accessibility guidelines](https://gameaccessibilityguidelines.com/avoid-flickering-images-and-repetitive-patterns/)
* [23. No blinking/No flickering | Pearson Accessibility Guidelines](https://ux.pearson.com/prototypes/accessibility-guidelines/patterns/pag/g23/)

documents.title: 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (2.0 A)

## In brief

Provide a means of skipping repeating content so users can more easily navigate by screen reader or keyboard.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> A [mechanism](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks#dfn-mechanism) is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple [Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks#dfn-web-page).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A site has a header section, which features identical content on every page. There is no skip link, heading structure, main landmark, or other means of quickly bypassing the section. | A "skip to main content" link at the top of the page allows the user to bypass the header and access the main content of the page. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **No mechanism to bypass the repetitive blocks of content.** [Issue #10609](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10609)
  * In this example, there is no mechanism available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple web pages.
  * This can be remediated through the use of a heading structure, skip links, and landmark regions.
  * You are not required to use a specific method, though a combination of them is considered best practice.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A site features a "Skip to main" link at the top of each page that allows the user to quickly bypass the header section. | Additionally, each page provides a top level heading (`<h1>`), and the main content of the page is contained within a `<main>` element. |

## Additional guidance

* Although this Success Criterion deals with blocks of content that are repeated on multiple pages, we also strongly promote structural markup on individual pages as per Success Criteria 1.3.1.
* Even for web pages that are not in a set, if a web page has blocks of text that are repeated within the page it may be helpful (but not required) to provide a means to skip over them. For example, a filters sidebar.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 2.4.1](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#241-bypass-blocks)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks)

documents.title: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (2.2 AA)
documents.content:
# 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (2.2 AA)

## In brief

Ensure when an item receives keyboard focus, it is at least partially visible.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A web page has a "sticky" footer (fixed to the bottom of the viewport) which completely covers the element in focus when the user tabs down the page. | A web page has a sticky footer and the element in focus always remains visible to the user (via [scroll padding](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-scroll-snap/#propdef-scroll-padding)) |
| A non-modal dialog opens and obscures the control which opened it; the only method to close it is with an X control in the dialog. | A non-modal dialog opens and obscures the control which opened it; pressing the Escape key closes the non-modal dialog. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **'Edit Fields' controls are not visible with keyboard focus** [Issue 10907](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10907)
  * Controls that gain focus are not being made visible to the user.
  * If content isn't visible when it gains focus it could make it difficult for users to know where they are in the page's content. This could result in confusion or unintended activation of a control.
  * Content that gains keyboard focus should become visible upon gaining focus, if it was not already.
* **'Search suggestion lists' are not visible with keyboard focus** [Issue 11187](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11187)
  * When the user inputs a valid search, the results display and can be navigated through with the keyboard.
  * However, as the user moves down the list, visible focus does not move as well.
  * As a result, the user is unable to see the results lower on the list unless they can use a mouse.
* **Comments sidesheet does not receive initial focus, does not retain focus** [Issue 7791](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7791)
  * When the comment side panel displays over the main content of the page, the user is able to tab out of it and back to the content behind it.
  * However, the side panel does not close and so the current item in focus is obscured from the users view unless they get back into the side panel and close it manually.
  * Focus should remain in the comment side panel until the user closes it, and then should go to the element that triggered its opening.
  * This could be seen as a combination of 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) and [1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence](./1.3.2%20Meaningful%20Sequence.md).

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A website design includes overlapping content such as a sticky header. | A website design has no overlapping content. | 
| When additional content appears, existing content is not displaced nor does it reflow. | When additional content appears, it displaces existing content (such as an accordion pattern) or existing content reflows. |

## Additional guidance

* Exceptions:
  * If users can move content (like draggable cards and toolbars) such that they obscure a focusable element, then it's not a fail because the user caused that state. Only the initial position of the moveable content is considered.
  * Content opened by the user may obscure a focused element if the user can reveal the focused element without advancing the keyboard focus. For example, a user opens a non-modal dialog and is able to close it with the Escape key.
* A properly constructed modal dialog will always pass this SC because the dialog takes focus when it opens and maintains focus until dismissed.
* Where content in a configurable interface can be repositioned by the user, then only the initial positions of user-movable content are considered for testing and conformance of this Success Criterion.
* Content opened by the user may obscure the component receiving focus. If the user can reveal the focused component without advancing the keyboard focus, the component with focus is not considered visually hidden due to author-created content.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

* [Understanding SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [WCAG Helper 2.4.11](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#2411-focus-not-obscured-minimum)
* [Sticky elements: functionality and accessibility testing (UK Gov)](https://technology.blog.gov.uk/2018/05/21/sticky-elements-functionality-and-accessibility-testing/)

documents.title: 2.4.2 Page Titled (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.4.2 Page Titled (2.0 A)

## In brief

The page's `title` element should describe the topic and/or purpose of the page.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> [Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/page-titled#dfn-web-page) have titles that describe topic or purpose.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| The page title stays the same between different PRs or Repos. (i.e. All the page titles are just "GitHub".) | The page's `title` element changes to be descriptive of the fact the user is on a different PR or Repo. (i.e., "Accessibility Repo - GitHub - GitHub" or "PR #2022 - Accessibility Repo - GitHub") |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Title remains same on all PR subpages** [Issue 7718](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/7718)
  * The page title remains the same for all the PR subpages.
  * This could make differentiating tabs apart difficult for users who have multiple ones open or are using some assistive technologies (e.g., voice control applications like Dragon Naturally Speaking or Screen readers).
  * Each page should have a different page title that is descriptive of its purpose to help users differentiate them apart.
* **Application title is not present for the application.** [Issue 4462](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/4462)
  * There is no page title set for the pages of the application.
  * The only identifier for the pages is their respective first level heading.
  * Each page should have a different page title that is descriptive of its purpose to help users differentiate them apart.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A page title starts with the site name and followed by the name of the page. | A page title starts with the page and followed by the site name. For example, the page title for a PR request is `PR Title · Pull Request #### · repo name` instead of `repo name · Pull Request #### · PR Title`. |

## Additional guidance

* None

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 2.4.2](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#242-page-titled)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 2.4.2 Page Titled](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/page-titled)

documents.title: 2.4.3 Focus Order (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.4.3 Focus Order (2.0 A)

## In brief

The order of focusable elements makes sense, particularly to sighted keyboard users.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> If a Web page can be navigated sequentially and the navigation sequences affect meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A control is not visible in the UI but the focus is landing on that control. | Visually hidden controls must not be keyboard focusable. |
| Keyboard focus moves out of a modal dialog to the underlying content. | Keyboard focus must be maintained within a modal dialog. Note that when pressing tab, it's acceptable for the focus to move to the browser controls and return back to the modal dialog. |
| Focus is lost when a user adds/removes an element from a list.  | The focus remains in the list and goes to the newly added list item. ( Ex. [Issue #2538](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/2538)) |
| Upon closing a modal window a user opened, focus goes back to the top of the page. | The focus returns to the element that originally triggered the modal to open. (Ex.[Issue #2467](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/2467)) |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Keyboard focus is not in sequential order in Hamburger menu** [Issue 11296](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11296)
  * In this issue, the user opens the hamburger menu. It opens in a modal format where the background is blurred.
  * Initially, the tab focus order is logical going through all the options.
  * However, upon getting to the end of the hamburger menu options, the focus goes to the hidden content behind the hamburger menu.
  * As a result, the user is unable to see where their focus is.
  * The expected behavior is that the focus should go back to the top of the hamburger menu modal.
  * The user should be able to either close the modal by selecting the close control, or by pressing the <kbd>Esc</kbd> key.
  * Then focus should return to the hamburger menu button.
* **Focus does not retain on the copy button in the code snippet** [Issue 11426](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11426)
  * In this issue, when the user activates the copy button to copy the code snippet, the keyboard focus jumps to the top of the page.
  * The expected behavior is that it should instead stay on the copy button.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Tabbing past an open control does not need to close it. | Tabbing past an open control closes it. |
| Keyboard focus occurs on non-interactive elements (such as regular text). | Keyboard focus doesn’t land on non-interactive elements (such as regular text). |
| Keyboard focus is moving to the same control twice (two tab stops) and its functionality is the same. | Keyboard focus lands on a control once (one tab stop). |

## Additional guidance

* Bugs involving screen reader reading order (i.e. hidden content still being announced or revealed content not being announced) are to be filed under 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

* [Understanding SC 2.4.3 Focus Order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order)
* [MAS 2.4.3: Focus Order Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-2.4.3-Focus-Order-Guide.aspx)
* [WCAG Helper 2.4.3](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#243-focus-order)

documents.title: 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (2.0 A)

## In brief

Provide descriptive names or context for all links so users can understand what each link will do.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> The [purpose of each link](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context#dfn-link-purpose) can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text together with its [programmatically determined link context](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context#dfn-programmatically-determined-link-context), except where the purpose of the link would be [ambiguous to users in general](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context#dfn-ambiguous-to-users-in-general).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A linked image has no accessible name or link text to identify it. | The image within the link has alternative text that describes the target of the link. |
| Link text is "Learn more" under a "GitHub pricing plans" heading. | Link text instead reads "Learn more about GitHub pricing plans." |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **'History' links present on the Page does not have discernible text** [Issue 11179](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11179)
  * The accessible labels for the history link doesn't provide sufficient context.
  * It would be better if the accessible label for the link was made more descriptive, or linked to other text that can provide the extra context with something like `aria-describedby`.
* **'See More' link is not descriptive** [Issue 11512](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11512)
  * Each of the login sessions has a "See more" link beside it.
  * However, because all the links say "See more", they don't provide sufficient context for individuals unable to view the visual layout or if the layout doesn't load properly.
  * It would be better if the accessible label for the link was made more descriptive, or linked to other text that can provide the extra context with an `aria-describedby` or `aria-label`.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A link's visible text is "Learn more", and it has `aria-label="Learn more about GitHub pricing plans."`. | The visible link text is "Learn more about GitHub pricing plans". As a result, the `aria-label` is no longer necessary. |

## Additional guidance

* There may be situations where the purpose of the link is supposed to be unknown or obscured. For instance, a game may have links identified only as door #1, door #2, and door #3. This link text would be sufficient because the purpose of the links is to create suspense for all users.
* In some cases, `aria-describedby` can also be used to provide additional context to an otherwise ambiguous link.
  * For example, a "Learn more" link is located under a "GitHub Pricing Plans" heading. Using `aria-describedby` set to an ID on the heading, assistive technology will be able to provide that added context to non-visual users who navigate through the links.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Primer resources

* [Links and buttons: guidance on naming controls | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/links-and-buttons#guidance-on-naming-controls)
* [Links | Primer accessibility patterns](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/links)
* [Link accessibility | Primer](https://primer.style/product/components/link/accessibility)

## Other resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 2.4.4](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#244-link-purpose-in-context)
* [MAS 2.4.4: Link Purpose (In Context) Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-2.4.4-Link-Purpose-In-Context-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context)
* [Avoid generic link text | `erblint-github` repo](https://github.com/github/erblint-github/blob/main/docs/rules/accessibility/avoid-generic-link-text.md)
* [Link and Button guidance | GitHub Accessibility Playbook](https://accessibility-playbook.github.com/link-and-button-guidance)
* [Functional Images | W3C WAI Tutorials](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/functional/)
* [Designing Better Links For The Web | Slava Shestopalov | Smashing Magazine](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2021/12/designing-better-links-websites-emails-guideline/)
* [Why Your Links Should Never Say “Click Here” | Anthony T | Smashing Magazine](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2012/06/links-should-never-say-click-here/)
* [Voice Control Usability Considerations For Partially Visually Hidden Link Names | Eric Bailey | Smashing Magazine](https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2022/06/voice-control-usability-considerations-partially-visually-hidden-link-names/)

# 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Provide at least 2 ways for users to reach the same content since not all users can navigate content the same way.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> More than one way is available to locate a [Web page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/multiple-ways#dfn-web-page) within a [set of Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/multiple-ways#dfn-set-of-web-pages) except where the Web Page is the result of, or a step in, a [process](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/multiple-ways#dfn-process).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| The only way to access the repos of a user is by the links on the user's profile page. | Repos can be reached by the user's profile and by search functionality. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.
