documents.content:
# 2.4.6 Headings and Labels (2.0 AA)

## In brief

A page's content is described by its headings and labels. Content should be sufficiently described by headings and labels so users can understand and use the content.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Headings that do not adequately describe the content under them. For example, two headings that are both "Recipe", but one heads a risotto recipe and the other heads up a French onion dip recipe. | Headings should sufficiently describe the content under them. Better headings in the aforementioned example could be "Risotto Recipe" and "French Onion Dip Recipe", which differentiates their content. |

> [!NOTE]
> Failure to programmatically define heading structure that is visually defined is considered a failure of 1.3.1 Info and Relationships.

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Descriptive aria label is not defined for the 'Edit' control** [Issue 10643](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10643)
  * The "Edit" label for the control is not sufficiently descriptive enough to help a user understand what the button is meant to edit without the visual layout. This poses a problem for those who use screen readers.
  * Instead, it would be best to either use `aria-label="Edit Meet the Team (optional)"` or associate it with the "Meet the Team (optional)" text with `aria-describedby`.
* **Descriptive group label is not defined for the 'combo boxes'** [Issue 10644](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10644)
  * There are multiple issues with the labeling of the "Expiration Date" group of fields.
    * The visual group label for the Expiration Date drop-downs meant to select the month and year says "Expiration Date (YYYY)", which leaves out the month field like it is not a part of the group. It should be "Expiration Date (MM/YYYY)".
      * Additionally, there is a second `legend` element label for the fields, but this one doesn't include the month or year context that the visual label does.
      * It would be better to just have one group label that says "Expiration Date (MM/YYYY)" and that is programmatically linked to the group of drop downs via being the `legend` element for the fieldset or through `aria-describedby`. Having 2 labels the way they are currently will always risk one not being as up to date as the other.
    * The drop-downs both say "Select One" instead of "Select Month" and "Select Year" respectively.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional guidance

* In some cases, a visible label can be an icon rather than text because they have become universally recognized for having certain meanings. For details, reference the [Additional guidance](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/web/WCAG/3.3.2%20Labels%20or%20Instructions.md#additional-guidance) in 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions.
* Ideally, all interactive elements' labels should be distinct so that they are descriptive of their individual purpose. The exception to this rule is when multiple elements perform _identical_ actions.
  * For example, it is okay for multiple links to be labeled "Home" if they all take you to the Home page. Additionally, it may make sense for the visible labels of buttons to all match, if there is additional visible context that differentiates them (e.g., each "copy code block" button is visually next to and programmatically associated with the code block it copies and there is sufficient visible separation for the buttons and their associated code blocks to reasonably not be confused.).
* It is important to ensure that the accessible labeling is such that the buttons can be differentiated without the visual context (e.g., There are 3 copy buttons, which each copy a different type of content. An `aria-label` or `aria-describedby` is used to provide the additional context that is otherwise only visually available.).
  * An example can be seen in [[WCAG Audit] [Usable-GHModels3.4] A descriptive aria-label is not defined for the copy button #9972](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9972).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* None

## Resources

* [WCAG Helper 2.4.6](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#246-headings-and-labels)
* [MAS 2.4.6: Headings and Labels Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-2.4.6--Headings-and-Labels-Guide.aspx)
* [Understanding SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/headings-and-labels)
* [Heading off confusion: When do headings fail WCAG? | TPGi](https://www.tpgi.com/heading-off-confusion-when-do-headings-fail-wcag/)
  * This article lists a few instances where Heading issues do not count as failures necessarily, and a few instances where they count as failures of either [2.4.6 Headings and Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/headings-and-labels.html) or [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html).
* [Headings | Office for Digital Accessibility (ODA) | University of Minnesota](https://accessibility.umn.edu/getting-started/learn-7-core-accessibility-skills/headings)
* [Headings Tutorial | Page Structure | W3C WAI](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/headings/)
* [Writing for Web Accessibility | WAI | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tips/writing/)

documents.title: 2.4.7 Focus Visible (2.0 AA)
documents.content:
# 2.4.7 Focus Visible (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Keyboard focusable elements should provide a visible focus indicator to help sighted keyboard users navigate content.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Visual focus indicators are removed through improper use of styling. | Elements that gain keyboard focus should display a visible focus indicator. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Keyboard focus indicator is not visible on the link 'Just for testing'** [Issue 10194](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10194)
  * The focus indicator is not visible when the focus is on the "Just for testing" link text.
  * This could make it difficult for some users to know what is/isn't an interactive component, and lead to the unintended activation of some controls.
* **Keyboard focus indicator is not visible on progress bars** [Issue 10542](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10542)
  * The keyboard focus indicator is not visible when focus is on the sections of the progress bars.
  * This could make it difficult for some users to know what is/isn't an interactive component, and lead to the unintended activation of some controls.
* **Keyboard focus indicator is not visible on 'Play/Pause' control** [Issue 11116](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11116)
  * The keyboard focus indicator is not visible when focus is on the video controls.
  * This could make it difficult for some users to know what is/isn't an interactive component, and lead to the unintended activation of some controls.
  * In this particular case, this could also cause problems if the user needs to navigate through the video or adjust video settings, like play speed or captions.
  * It could also cause trouble if the user encounters a section of video they need to skip due to trauma, epilepsy, or other cognitive conditions.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| When a new screen/page opens via a single page app, the H1 heading is focused and there is no visible focus indicator. | When a new screen/page opens via a single page app, the H1 heading is focused and a visible focus indicator is provided. |
| When a skip-to-main link is activated, the H1 heading is focused and there is no visible focus indicator. | When a skip-to-main link is activated, the H1 heading is focused and a visible focus indicator is provided. |
| The visible focus indicator is not visible when using a Windows or Mac system High Contrast mode. | It is preferred that the visible focus indicator remain visible with sufficient contrast. However, these are marked as `a11yUsable` instead of 2.4.7 failures. |

## Additional guidance

* There are nuances to this Success Criterion when it applies to programmatic focus of non-interactive items, so WCAG conformance may need to be decided on a case-by-case basis. See Examples of usability issues and best practices above. 
* If focus indicator contrast is less than 3:1, report under 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.
* If the browser is forcing keyboard focus on an iFrame when navigating by tab key, and there's no visible focus indicator, the bug is not required to be reported. If it is reported, it should be labeled as a [user-agent issue](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/user-agent-bug-issues.md). 

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).
* [Guideline Alignment] focus ring on iframe [#329](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/329)
* [Guideline Alignment] keyboard focus indicator on static content [#337](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/337)

documents.title: 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (2.1 A)
documents.content:
# 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (2.1 A)

## In brief

Provide single-point operation for all functionality so users who cannot perform complex and multi-touch gestures may still access all features using one finger on touchscreens.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> All [functionality](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-gestures#dfn-functionality) that uses multipoint or path-based gestures for operation can be operated with a [single pointer](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-gestures#dfn-single-pointer) without a path-based gesture, unless a multipoint or path-based gesture is [essential](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-gestures#dfn-essential).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A web application implements an interface where drawing a "Z" on the screen undoes the last action. There is no other way to undo the action. | A button is available for undoing the last action (See [Technique F105](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F105)).|
| An image gallery requires the user to swipe left/right to navigate between images with no single point alternative available. | The image gallery can be navigated by swiping left/right, or by tapping/clicking on next and previous buttons located on either side of the currently displayed image. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Use of Path-Based Gesture to Horizontally Scroll Repositories** [Issue 1159](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/1159)
  * In the case of this issue, the "Pinned" section uses a path-based swipe gesture to horizontally scroll the repositories in view.
  * No alternative is available, potentially making it difficult or impossible for users relying on pointer devices to navigate.
  * Instead, the user should be able to use one finger, reduced gesture options.
  * Often, mobile devices have built in gestures that can be utilized.
* **Use of Path-Based Gesture for Operation of Sign Out Option** [Issue 1622](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/1622)
  * To sign out of an account, a path-based swipe gesture is required to cause the appropriate button to appear.
  * For users relying on pointing devices, keyboards and/or other input methods, it can be very difficult or impossible to execute the gesture accurately.
  * If the first swipe to the left isn't carried out in a direct horizontal line, the screen will scroll instead of revealing the control.
  * Users may not even realize that this gesture is available in the first place, making sign out difficult.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->
## Additional guidance

* This requirement applies to web content that interprets pointer actions (i.e., this does not apply to actions that are required to operate the user agent or assistive technology).
* Any movement of a pointer could be difficult or impossible to use for someone who cannot perform precise movements, therefore alternative forms of interaction are always recommended.
* This success criterion is scoped to *path-based gestures* as it may be difficult or impossible to provide an alternative for *free-form gestures*.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

documents.title: 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation (2.1 A)
documents.content:
# 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation (2.1 A)

## In brief

Make pointer cancellation predictable and consistent to reduce accidental activation of controls by mouse or touch.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> For [functionality](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-cancellation#dfn-functionality) that can be operated using a [single pointer](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-cancellation#dfn-single-pointer), at least one of the following is true:
>
> - **No Down-Event**
>   - The [down-event](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-cancellation#dfn-down-event) of the pointer is not used to execute any part of the function;
> - **Abort or Undo**
>   - Completion of the function is on the [up-event](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-cancellation#dfn-up-event), and a [mechanism](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-cancellation#dfn-mechanism) is available to abort the function before completion or to undo the function after completion;
> - **Up Reversal**
>   - The up-event reverses any outcome of the preceding down-event;
> - **Essential**
>   - Completing the function on the down-event is [essential](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-cancellation#dfn-essential).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A submit button is activated on the mouse down, which means the user cannot prevent accidental submission.  | The submit button is activated on the `onclick` event instead so that it activates when the user releases the click, which allows the user to cancel the action by moving the cursor focus before releasing (See [Technique F101](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F101)). |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

documents.content:
# 2.5.3 Label in Name (2.1 A)

## In brief

Ensure the accessible names for interface components contain any text visually presented and associated with those components so they are easier for users who depend on voice activation.

## Normative

> For [user interface components](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name#dfn-user-interface-component) with [labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name#dfn-label) that include [text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name#dfn-text) or [images of text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name#dfn-image-of-text), the [name](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name#dfn-name) contains the text that is presented visually.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A form has a "First Name" field and "Last Name" field. The accessible labels that are read by assistive technologies only read "First" and "Last". | The accessible labels contain the visible label (in this case, both "First Name" and "Last Name"). |
| A button with a visible speech bubble icon with the number 8 inside it, has a visible tooltip label that reads "8 comments". The accessible label that is read by assistive technologies only reads "Comments". | The accessible label contains the visible label (in this case, "8 comments"). |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Information about enabling 'Mark as resolved' control is not provided to the user** [Issue 9670](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9670)
  * In the case of this issue, the label isn't entirely incorrect, but it is incomplete.
  * It is okay for an accessible label to provide additional context that may be available to a visual user, such as tooltip text in this case, but it also needs to contain the visual label.
  * In this case, the accessible label needs to be "Mark as resolved. Remove all conflict markers to resolve this file."
* **Visual name and aria-label are different for the 'Organization naming pattern' edit field** [Issue 11076](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11076)
  * In this case, the accessible label is entirely different from the visual label. The label should be `Organization naming pattern`.
  * That said, if the additional instruction above the edit field is not programmatically connected to the field in some way, then it may be a good idea to also have an `aria-describedby` attribute on the field that links to an ID on a div around the instructional text, "Organizations that match the matching pattern will be targeted by this ruleset.", that comes before it as this provides important context that a non-visual user may miss.
* **Visual label and aria label is different for the 'Essentials' control** [Issue 11491](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11491)
  * In this case the accessible label does not contain the visual label and instead contains unnecessary context.
  * The `aria-label` just needs to be `Essentials`.
  * If the button is given an `aria-expanded` attribute that updates properly, the the user will be informed that it can be expanded to view additional content without the need for extra wording in the label. This would also help the element meet [4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](./4.1.2%20Name,%20Role,%20Value.md).

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |

## Additional guidance

* While the accessible label needs to contain the visible label, it does not have to be an exact match.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

documents.title: 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (2.1 A)
documents.content:
# 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (2.1 A)

## In brief

Don't rely solely on device motion to control page content so that content is not dependent on a user's ability to move a device since some people cannot hold or move a device steadily.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> [Functionality](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/motion-actuation#dfn-functionality) that can be operated by device motion or user motion can also be operated by [user interface components](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/motion-actuation#dfn-user-interface-component) and responding to the motion can be disabled to prevent accidental actuation, except when:
>
> - **Supported Interface**
>   - The motion is used to operate functionality through an [accessibility supported](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/motion-actuation#dfn-accessibility-supported) interface;
> - **Essential**
>   - The motion is [essential](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/motion-actuation#dfn-essential) for the function and doing so would invalidate the activity.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A control can only be activated by tilting the device. | The control can be activated by tilting the device and also by an alternate method such clicking/tapping a button. |
| In various Pokemon games, the Pokemon [Malamar](https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Malamar_(Pok%C3%A9mon)) requires users to rotate their device upside down. There is no alternative provided. | There is a method to turn off motion actuation and an alternative method is available to activate the evolution. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

documents.title: 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (2.2 AA)
documents.content:
# 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (2.2 AA)

## In brief

For any action that involves dragging, provide an alternative requiring only a single mouse click/tap because some people cannot use a mouse to drag items.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential or the functionality is determined by the user agent and not modified by the author.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A user is unable to reorganize items in a sortable list because the only method provided requires dragging. | The user is also able to reorganize items by clicking the element to be moved and then clicking arrows or buttons to position it within the list. |
| A linear slider control widget can only be set by dragging the visual indicator (thumb). | The widget allows tapping or clicking on any point of the slider track to change the value and set the thumb to that position. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Single pointer alternative is not provided for the graph** [Issue 11401](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11401)
  * Currently, a dragging movement with the mouse is required to rotate the rendered stl file preview.
  * This will be difficult for users who cannot operate a mouse.
  * A single pointer alternative needs to be provided.
  * For example, a set of controls that allows the user to rotate and move the preview in a manner similar to how a mouse user would be able to.
* **Single pointer alternative is not provided for the maps** [Issue 11222](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11222)
  * Currently, a dragging movement with the mouse is required to move the map.
  * This makes navigating the map difficult or impossible for someone who cannot use a mouse.
  * Including arrow controls that would allow someone to move in a similar fashion would be ideal.
* **No alternative is provided to reorder the columns** [Issue 10254](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10254)
  * Currently, reordering the columns in a project board requires the user to use a mouse to drag them.
  * Adding an option to reorder them with a menu or button controls would be ideal for users who cannot use a mouse.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None

|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |

## Additional guidance

* Keyboard accessibility does not meet this guideline.

## Accessibility Council decisions

documents.title: 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (2.2 AA)
documents.content:
# 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (2.2 AA)

## In brief

Ensure targets meet a minimum size or have sufficient spacing around them so users can easily and accurately activate the target.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except where:
>
> * **Spacing**: Undersized targets (those less than 24 by 24 CSS pixels) are positioned so that if a 24 CSS pixel diameter circle is centered on the bounding box of each, the circles do not intersect another target or the circle for another undersized target;
> * **Equivalent**: The function can be achieved through a different control on the same page that meets this criterion;
> * **Inline**: The target is in a sentence or its size is otherwise constrained by the line-height of non-target text;
> * **User agent control**: The size of the target is determined by the user agent and is not modified by the author;
> * **Essential**: A particular presentation of the target is essential or is legally required for the information being conveyed.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Three buttons have a target size of 20 by 20 CSS pixels and there are adjacent buttons on each side. | Three buttons have a target size of 20 by 20 CSS pixels and there are no adjacent buttons for at least 4 pixels on each side. |
| A set of buttons are 24 by 24 pixels, but formatted such that their the target areas overlap. | A set of buttons are 24 by 24 pixels and target areas do not overlap. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Target height size for 'Links' is 18 Display Pixels** [Issue 9993](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9993)
  * The spacing around the links is insufficient.
  * There are multiple links too close together.
  * As a result, users may have difficulty accurately activating the intended link.
* **Touch Target for 'Avatar' is 20 Pixels** [Issue 9880](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9880)
  * The spacing between the avatar and other controls, like the back button, is insufficient.
  * As a result, the user could inadvertently activate the wrong control.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A set of buttons do not meet the minimum size requirements, but do have the minimum spacing. | Buttons have both the minimum spacing and size requirements met. |
| A checkbox is smaller than 24 by 24 CSS pixels, but has sufficient spacing around it so that there is no overlap with a 24 pixel circle drawn around it and any adjacent targets. | The checkbox is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or is paired with a label that increases the overall target size. |

## Additional guidance

* It's highly recommended to review the [examples in the W3C Understanding](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum#examples) document.
* Targets that allow for values to be selected spatially based on position within the target are considered one target for the purpose of the success criterion. Examples include sliders, color pickers displaying a gradient of colors, or editable areas where you position the cursor.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

* [Understanding SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [WCAG Helper 2.5.8](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#258-target-size-minimum)
* [Bookmarklets | Accessibility and inclusive design manual | UK Department of Education](https://accessibility.education.gov.uk/knowledge-hub/tools-testing/bookmarklets)
* [Target size bookmarklets by David Cox | accessibility-tools](https://accessibility-tools.github.io/target-size-highlighter/)
* [How to test 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) | TPGi](https://www.tpgi.com/how-to-test-2-5-8-target-size-minimum/)
* [Understanding WCAG SC 2.5.8 – Target Size (Minimum) | DigitalA11y](https://www.digitala11y.com/understanding-sc-2-5-8-target-size-minimum/)

documents.title: 3.1.1 Language of Page (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 3.1.1 Language of Page (2.0 A)

## In brief

Every page should have a programmatically set primary language set for the page (i.e., `<html lang="en">`)

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> The default [human language](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page#dfn-human-language) of each [Web page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page#dfn-web-page) can be [programmatically determined](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page#dfn-programmatically-determined).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A page has no `lang` attribute programmatically set. | The `lang` attribute is set for the page based on the primary language of the page. |
| A page has a `lang` attribute set to `lang="fr"` for French when the page is in English.| The page's `lang` attribute is instead set to `lang="en"` so it matches the primary language of the page. |
| The UI allows the user to change the language of the page. The `lang` attribute does not change to match the current language of the page. | The `lang` attribute dynamically adjusts to match the current page language. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Page does not have lang attribute defined** [Issue 10688](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10688)
  * The page does not have a language attribute defined.
  * This could cause issues for translation applications, screen readers, and other applications that may depend on that attribute to identify how to pronounce or translate content on the page.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->

## Additional guidance

* [HTML page lang attribute has valid language tag | ACT Rules](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/act/rules/bf051a)
  * This rule assumes that only [known primary language tags](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/act/rules/bf051a/#known-primary-language-tag) are enough to satisfy Success Criterion 3.1.1 Language of Page; this notably excludes [grandfathered tags](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5646.html#section-2.2.8) and [ISO 639.2](https://www.loc.gov/standards/iso639-2/php/code_list.php) three-letters codes, both having poor support in assistive technologies.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)

* [HTML page lang attribute has valid language tag | ACT Rules | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/act/rules/bf051a/)
* [On Use of the Lang Attribute | Adrian Roselli](https://adrianroselli.com/2015/01/on-use-of-lang-attribute.html)
* [Accessibility Bookmarklets by Paul J Adam](https://pauljadam.com/bookmarklets/)
  * Has a useful `lang` bookmarklet and a demo page you can use to better see how a page's language should be marked up and how content that differs from the page language should be marked up.

documents.content:
# 3.1.2 Language of Parts (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Ensure that text on a page that differs from the main page language is marked up so text-to-speech software can more accurately pronounce the text.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> The [human language](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-parts#dfn-human-language) of each passage or phrase in the content can be [programmatically determined](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-parts#dfn-programmatically-determined) except for proper names, technical terms, words of indeterminate language, and words or phrases that have become part of the vernacular of the immediately surrounding text.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A page is in English primarily, but has an article about Dia de los Muertos. Words in the article that are Spanish, including "Dia de los Muertos" are not programmatically identified as being Spanish. This results in assistive technologies mispronouncing these words. | The parts of the article that are in Spanish, are programmatically marked up as such (i.e., `<span lang="es">Dia de los Muertos</span`) and thus pronounced properly by screen readers. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Incorrect lang value is defined for the page** [Issue 11377](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11377)
  * In the case of this issue, the page `lang` attribute is set the `en` for English, which is correct.
  * However, there is not a separate `lang` attribute provided for the Ukranian (`uk`) content.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->

## Additional guidance

* Exception: the lang attribute is not required on user-generated content in non-English languages.
* Exception: the lang attribute is not required on [filler text](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/general-guidance/sample-content-policy.md#filler-text).
* Identifying changes in language is important for a number of reasons:
  * It allows braille translation software to follow changes in language.
  * Screen readers will pronounce words with the appropriate pronunciation, ensuring more accurate communication of information.
  * Marking changes in language can benefit future developments in technology, for example users who are unable to translate between languages themselves will be able to use machines to translate unfamiliar languages.
  * Marking changes in language can also assist user agents in providing definitions using a dictionary.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

* [3.2.6.2 The lang and xml:lang attributes | HTML Standards](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#attr-lang)
* [Language tags in HTML and XML | W3C Internationalization](https://www.w3.org/International/articles/language-tags/index.en)
* [On Use of the Lang Attribute | Adrian Roselli](https://adrianroselli.com/2015/01/on-use-of-lang-attribute.html)
* [Accessibility Bookmarklets by Paul J Adam](https://pauljadam.com/bookmarklets/)
  * Has a useful `lang` bookmarklet and a demo page you can use to better see how a page's language should be marked up and how content that differs from the page language should be marked up.

documents.content:
# 3.2.1 On Focus (2.0 A)

## In brief

Do not change a user's context when items get focus so content can be navigated more predictably.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> When any [user interface component](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-focus#dfn-user-interface-component) receives focus, it does not initiate a [change of context](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-focus#dfn-changes-of-context).

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| Moving focus to a form control results in the page unexpectedly refreshing. | Unexpected page refreshes don't occur without warning. (Ex. [Issue #3825](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/3825)) |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Control automatically gets selected when navigating with Tab key** [Issue 11172](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11172)
  * In this issue, the user types a forward slash to open the Slash Commands menu.
  * When the user presses the tab key to navigate, the currently highlighted menu item is activated, moving the user to the next menu instead of going down the list of command options.
  * This is unexpected and could be disorienting for users.
  * For screen reader users, it could also result in confusion about the menu's structure.
* **Checkbox automatically gets selected when navigating with Tab key** [Issue 10946](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10946)
  * When the user tabs through the page and lands on a checkbox, pressing tab again to go to the next checkbox instead activates the current checkbox.
  * This is not expected behavior and will make the form more difficult for some users to use.
* **New page is getting displayed automatically while invoking the 'disable delete' menu control** [Issue 10298](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10298)
  * Upon activating the "Delete Configuration" control, the user is taken to another page about the element they were trying to delete rather than being asked to confirm deletion or the page updating to show the option removed.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->

## Additional guidance

* What is meant by "component" here is also sometimes called "user interface element" or "user interface component".
* A change of content is not always a [change of context](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-focus#dfn-changes-of-context). This success criterion is automatically met if changes in content are not also changes of context.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

documents.content:
# 3.2.2 On Input (2.0 A)

## In brief

Forewarn users if their context will change based on their input so content can be operated more predictably.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Changing the setting of any [user interface component](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-input#dfn-user-interface-component) does not automatically cause a [change of context](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-input#dfn-changes-of-context) unless the user has been advised of the behavior before using the component.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/Level%20of%20severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| While focused on an option within a select dropdown, pressing Escape unexpectedly results in the option getting selected. | While focused on an option within a select dropdown, pressing Escape closes the select dropdown with no change in selection. (See [Issue #9113](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9113)) |
| Upon activating a checkbox option, the focus unexpectedly moves to another form control. | The focus remains on the selected checkbox after checking it. (See [Issue #2725](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/2725)) |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **The list item is getting selected automatically upon invoking the 'ESC' key** [Issue 9113](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/9113)
  * In this issue, an option is being selected when the user uses the Escape key, which is not an expected reaction.
  * The Escape key is used for predominantly closing modals, exiting processes, etc.
  * By having this behave in such a manner, users will be very likely to inadvertently select the wrong option and result in errors in information they enter.
* **"Search syntax tips" link in the QueryBuilder modal opens in a new tab** [Issue 4932](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/4932)
  * With this issue, the link opens in a new window/tab unexpectedly upon activation.
  * Users typically expect links within a site to open in the same window/tab by default, unless otherwise indicated.
  * This allows them to easily use the typical browser / system options to go back to the previous page.
  * The link needs to either have an accessible indication that it will open in a new window/tab or needs to open in the same window/tab.
* **After activating ‘Save my info…checkout’ checkbox, keyboard focus does not stay on the same control** [Issue 2725](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/2725)
  * In this issue, the keyboard focus automatically moves to a different control upon checking the "Save my info..." checkbox.
  * This could cause problems, particularly for users with low vision or who use a screen reader.
  * Focus should remain on the checkbox after it is checked/unchecked.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->

## Additional guidance

* This Success Criterion covers changes in context due to changing the setting of a control. Clicking on links or buttons is activating a control, not changing the setting of that control.
* A change of content is not always a [change of context](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-input#dfn-changes-of-context). This success criterion is automatically met if changes in content are not also changes of context.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

documents.title: 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (2.0 AA)
documents.content:
# 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Consistently order navigation that repeats across multiple pages so content can be navigated more predictably.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Navigational mechanisms that are repeated on multiple [Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-navigation#dfn-web-page) within a [set of Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-navigation#dfn-set-of-web-pages) occur in the [same relative order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-navigation#dfn-same-relative-order) each time they are repeated, unless a change is initiated by the user.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A site features a navigation bar at the top of every page that provides the following links: Home, Products, Contact. But on one page the links are in a different order: Home, Contact, Products. | The navigation bar provides the links in the same order consistently: Home, Products, Contact. | 
| A site features a skip-to-main link located at the top of every page so it is first in tab order. However, it is fourth in the tab order on a couple of pages. | A site features a skip-to-main link located at the top of every page so it is first in tab order on every page. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Inconsistent VoiceOver Swipe Order on Home Screen** [Issue 1096](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/1096)
  * The way in which Voiceover navigates across the home screen when the user is navigating via swiping is inconsistent, which could cause the user to struggle to access the content they intend to.
* **Confusing Change of Context when Language is Changed** [Issue 1605](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/1605)
  * With other settings, the user stays within the settings menu, and in the section of the settings they were in before activating the setting.
  * However, this is not the case with the language setting.
  * After activating the "App Language" button, they get taken to a new screen with focus placed on the "Back" button by default. The parent/previous screen is also called "Settings", so users will hear "Settings, Back button".
  * This is especially problematic because the "Settings" menu they are now in is the System Settings and not the GitHub app Settings.
  * Users could be confused and have trouble getting back to where they were.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->

## Additional guidance

* None

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 3.2.3](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#323-consistent-navigation)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-navigation)

documents.title: 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (2.0 AA)
documents.content:
# 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Identify repeating functions consistently so actions are more predictable across related pages.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Components that have the [same functionality](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-identification#dfn-same-functionality) within a [set of Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-identification#dfn-set-of-web-pages) are identified consistently.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/Level%20of%20severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A speech bubble icon is used primarily to indicate comments on an article, comment, etc. On one page, the speech bubble is instead used to trigger an audio file. | The speech bubble icon is only used to indicate comments and a different icon is used to indicate an audio file that can be played so users can consistently identify the meaning for each icon. |
| Two search buttons that have the same search functionality and same visual, text label, but different `aria-label` values. | Controls that have the same functionality are labeled the same with regards to both their visual label and accessible label so they can be consistently announced and identified by users. |
| The main content of a page contains numerous links. These links have varying appearances with some being underlined and some just being a different color. | The links have a consistent appearance across the page so they can be consistently identified by users. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Inconsistent roles are defined for the control named "newer" while in disable/enable state** [Issue 2885](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/2885)
  * The visual state and programmatic state of controls that are disabled/enabled is not consistent.
  * This can cause some users to not know the current state of the control.
  * If the control is disabled it should be consistently communicated as disabled, and the same when it is enabled.
* **Appearance of links are not consistently thorough as present under ‘Upgrade’ page** [Issue 2609](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/2609)
  * Links are not consistently styled across the page.
  * This can cause users to visually have trouble identifying the links across the page.
* **On the secret scanning page, consistent identification is not defined for the copy secret to clipboard button i.e by pressing spacebar key on the control no copied information is visible** [Issue 2209](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/2209)
  * The behavior of the copy buttons after activation is inconsistent.
  * This can cause users to have trouble identifying whether the control is functional.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

None at this time.
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->

## Notes

This section is used to highlight notes from the Success Criterion and its associated Understanding document.

* Text alternatives that are "consistent" are not always "identical." For instance, you may have a graphical arrow at the bottom of a Web page that links to the next Web page. The text alternative may say "Go to page 4." Naturally, it would not be appropriate to repeat this exact text alternative on the next Web page. It would be more appropriate to say "Go to page 5". Although these text alternatives would not be identical, they would be consistent, and therefore would satisfy this Success Criterion.
* A single non-text-content-item may be used to serve different functions. In such cases, different text alternatives are necessary and should be used. Examples can be commonly found with the use of icons such as check marks, cross marks, and traffic signs. Their functions can be different depending on the context of the Web page. A check mark icon may function as "approved", "completed", or "included", to name a few, depending on the situation. Using "check mark" as text alternative across all Web pages does not help users understand the function of the icon. Different text alternatives can be used when the same non-text content serves multiple functions.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* None

## Resources

This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it.

* [WCAG Helper 3.2.4](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#324-consistent-identification)
* [MAS Liquid Collection (see Table of Contents)](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [Understanding SC 3.2.4 Consistent Identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-identification)

documents.content:
# 3.2.6 Consistent Help (2.2. A)

## In brief

Place links to help-related resources in the same location in the UI so people who need help can find it easily.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> If a Web page contains any of the following help mechanisms, and those mechanisms are repeated on multiple Web pages within a set of Web pages, they occur in the same order relative to other page content, unless a change is initiated by the user:
>
> * Human contact details;
> * Human contact mechanism;
> * Self-help option;
> * A fully automated contact mechanism.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A contact support link is repeated on every page of a website, but sometimes in the header, sometimes in the footer, and sometimes in a sidebar. | A contact support link is the second link in the footer on every page of a website. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* None

## Additional guidance

* Help mechanisms may be provided directly on the page, or may be provided via a direct link to a different page containing the information.
* For this Success Criterion, "the same order relative to other page content" can be thought of as how the content is ordered when the page is serialized. The visual position of a help mechanism is likely to be consistent across pages for the same page variation (e.g., CSS break-point). The user can initiate a change, such as changing the page's zoom or orientation, which may trigger a different page variation. This criterion is concerned with relative order across pages displayed in the same page variation (e.g., same zoom level and orientation).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

documents.title: 3.3.1 Error Identification (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 3.3.1 Error Identification (2.0 A)

## In brief

When form input errors are identified, error messages must be provided in text and must indicate which field has an error.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> If an [input error](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification#dfn-input-error) is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| An error in a form is only indicated with a red border around the field with invalid input. | The field with an invalid input also has a text error message that indicates the error and the name of the input. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **On providing invalid input on the email control no error message displayed** [Issue 10713](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10713)
  * Upon providing invalid input to the email control and tabbing out of the field, no error message is displayed to help the user identify their mistake.
* **"Finish your review" form is not identified as required; error feedback not presented directly to user** [Issue 6294](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/6294)
  * Failure to fill out required fields causes the form to fail to submit.
  * However, upon this failure, the user receives a generic error that doesn't indicate which fields do not have valid content.
  * Additionally, these fields are not visually indicated as required prior to, or after failed submission.
  * This is inconsistent with other forms on the site.
* **Screen reader is not announcing the error message information for 'Expiration Date' control** [Issue 5287](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/5287)
  * The visual error message for the field is not announced by the screen reader.
  * As a result, visual users and screen reader users are not receiving a consistent experience.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!-- 
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder | 
-->

## Additional guidance

* If a user enters a value that is too high or too low, and the coding on the page automatically changes that value to fall within the allowed range, the user's error would still need to be described to them as required by the success criterion. Such an error description telling the person of the changed value would meet both this success criterion (Error Identification) and [3.3.3 Error Suggestion](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-suggestion).
* This criterion does not mandate any particular way in which errors should be displayed such as listed at the start of a form; show errors inline; or in an alert or a dialog.
* This success criterion does not mean that color or text styles cannot be used to indicate errors. It simply requires that errors also be identified using text.
* To indicate the input that has an error, the input name is included within the text of the error message itself. For example: "First name is required." or "Policy start date is invalid." Or, the error message is programmatically associated with the field (typically via `aria-describedby` but can also be via the form or `aria-label`.).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* None

documents.title: 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (2.0 A) ## In brief Provide labels or instructions for inputs so users understand what they need to enter. ## Normative This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion. > [Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions#dfn-label) or instructions are provided when content requires user input. ## Examples of failures **Default severity level: 2** This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels. | Actual | Expected | |--------|----------| | A form where some inputs are required has no visible labeling or instruction provided to visually identify required fields. | An asterisk is included on required fields, and text at the start of the form indicates its meaning. | | A drop-down, select input has no visible label nor visual context to identify its purpose. | The input has a visible text label to help users identify the input's purpose. | | A telephone number field requires that the user enter the number in a particular format, but the format is not indicated to the user. | The text label includes the required format, such as "Birth date (mm/dd/yyyy)". | ### Example GitHub issues The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC. * **On the 'Blog' page, placeholder visual label disappears upon providing any input** [Issue 10351](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10351) * Because placeholder text has been used as the sole visual label for the field, it disappears upon the user adding any input to the field. * The user can only check the label of the field by removing their input. * The placeholder also does not get identified as a label by assistive technologies. * A separate, persistent, visual label should be available for the field. * **No visual label is defined for 'Start date and End date' edit field** [Issue 11285](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11285) * No visual labels are provided for the start and end date fields in the date picker. * This makes their purpose unclear to some users. ## Examples of usability issues and best practices **Default severity level: 4** These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG. | Actual | Preferred | |--------|-----------| | A search field features just a magnifying glass icon as its visible label. | The magnifying glass is further supported by a text label, such as "Search GitHub" or other wording that identifies the purpose of the field. | | An expandable menu is represented by a standard hamburger menu icon. | An additional, accessible tooltip is added to explain what the menu is for. | | A required field in a form is indicated by an asterisk. | A required field's label contains "(Required)" instead so it is read with the label and is clearer to all with/without a legend. | ## Additional guidance * This Success Criterion covers if a visible label exists. It also covers whether the visible and/or accessible label is descriptive. * If there is a visible label but no accessible name is provided, this falls under [4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value). * If an asterisk is included on required fields, but text at the start of the form indicating its meaning is missing, it must be reported as a WCAG violation with Severity 3. * In some cases, a visible label can be an icon rather than text because they have become universally recognized for having certain meanings. * Some examples include: * A magnifying glass for a search field * A funnel for a filter button * Three stacked horizontal lines for a "hamburger" menu button * Gear for preferences or settings * Trash can for delete * Star for favorite/save * Examples within GitHub: * Eye for Watch * Branch diagram for Fork



* The label and descriptive text should be in close proximity to the associated control. For instance, a magnifying glass icon next to a text input field could be interpreted as a search field, but that same icon next to an image could imply the ability to zoom in/out on the image. * Including text labeling can still help in cases where there could be confusion caused by multiple similar controls/inputs. For instance, * If you have multiple search fields on a page, but one searches the whole site while the other just searches within a subset of information. * If you have multiple filters, but each filters a different set of values. * A required field must have both a visual and a non-visual indication that it is required before the user attempts to submit the form. * In cases where all fields are required, the inclusion of a line at the start of the form indicating such could serve as a visual indication as long as all fields are also set to required. * Exceptions may be recognized for situations in which the user would reasonably assume that all fields are required, such as a login form, as long as validation explains the input being required if left out on submission. * In [Primer forms](https://primer.style/ui-patterns/forms/overview#required-field-indicator) using the [form control component](https://primer.style/components/form-control#required-fields), required fields are indicated by an asterisk (`*`). It is possible to specify a different indicator (such as 'Required') by passing a string to `requiredText`. * When using a symbol, such as `*`, [Primer recommends](https://primer.style/components/form-control#required-fields) that the meaning of the symbol be defined at the top of the form, but it won't be inserted automatically. * The rationale for flexibility here is that the `*` symbol is assumed to be a widely recognized convention that doesn't necessarily need to be explained. * Please review [Required Form Input Use Cases](general-guidance/required-input-use-cases.md) for additional guidance related to this SC and required form inputs. ## Accessibility Council decisions * When a `button` element is used to open a set of options, like `select` element functionality, a visual label must be provided (a non-visible accessible name alone such as `aria-label` is not sufficient). Reference [issue 272](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/issues/272). * When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md). ## Primer resources * [Forms | Primer UI patterns](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/forms) * [FormControl accessibility | Primer](https://primer.style/product/components/form-control/accessibility) * [Placeholders | Primer accessibility patterns](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/placeholders) ## Other resources This section contains various resources that could be helpful in understanding this success criterion or resolving issues related to it. * [WCAG Helper 3.3.2](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#332-labels-or-instructions) * [MAS 3.3.2: Labels or Instructions Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-3.3.2-Labels-or-Instructions-Guide.aspx) * [Understanding SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions) * [Icon Usability | Nielsen Norman Group](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/icon-usability/) * [Technique H90: Indicating required form controls using label or legend](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H90) * [Doing what’s required: Indicating mandatory fields in an accessible way | TPGi](https://www.tpgi.com/doing-whats-required-indicating-mandatory-fields-in-an-accessible-way/) * [Writing for Web Accessibility | WAI | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tips/writing/) * [Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions | ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/names-and-descriptions/)

documents.title: 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (2.0 AA)
documents.content:
# 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Where errors are detected, suggest ways to correct them to help guide users on how to fix errors.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> If an [input error](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-suggestion#dfn-input-error) is automatically detected and suggestions for correction are known, then the suggestions are provided to the user, unless it would jeopardize the security or purpose of the content.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A user enters a phone number in a form and receives an error upon submitting. The error simply says the entry was invalid, but provides no guidance on how to correct it. | The phone field error provides a suggestion for what format is being looked for (**e.g.,** `Telephone entry is invalid. Expected format: ###-###-####`). |
| A password creation field fails to submit. The error simply says invalid entry. | The password error lists the required criteria for the password (**e.g.,** `Password requires at least 1 capital letter, 1 lower case letter, 1 number, 1 of the following special characters (#&@!-+/?), and be a minimum of 8 characters.`). |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **No error suggestion appears by providing invalid input on the 'Contact email' control** [Issue 11546](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11546)
  * Upon entering an invalid format entry for the email field, no suggestion for what is wrong is provided.
  * Suggestions about format or if there is no email matching that one in the system would help users to know what they need to do to correct the issue.
* **On invoking, 'continue to shipping method' button, the displayed error message is not descriptive enough for the edit fields** [Issue 4289](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/4289)
  * The error message displayed when invalid input is entered into the form does not help the user identify what fields they need to fix or what they need to do to fix them.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None

documents.title: 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (2.0 AA)
documents.content:
# 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (2.0 AA)

## In brief

Provide ways for users to confirm, correct, or reverse important submissions so users can avoid submitting incorrect important information.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> For Web pages that cause legal commitments or financial transactions for the user to occur, that modify or delete user-controllable data in data storage systems, or that submit user test responses, at least one of the following is true:
>
> - **Reversible**
>   - Submissions are reversible.
> - **Checked**
>   - Data entered by the user is checked for input errors and the user is provided an opportunity to correct them.
> - **Confirmed**
>   - A mechanism is available for reviewing, confirming, and correcting information before finalizing the submission.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue. Reference the [Severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md) labels.

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A user makes a change to their GitHub account that will result in a charge. The change is submitted as soon as they select the option and provide payment information, with no chance to review what is being changed first. | Prior to finalizing the user's selections, a page displays the user's information, payment information, and an itemized list of what changes are being made. The user must confirm them prior to the changes being processed. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Upon invoking 'remove' control, the custom name domain is getting deleted without an error preventive dialog being populated** [Issue 3903](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/3903)
  * Upon removing a domain, no mechanism for the user to confirm the decision before it actually takes place is provided.
  * This means that, if a user misclicks they can lose a custom domain entry without being given a chance to prevent the data loss.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practice that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

documents.content:
# 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (2.2. A)

## In brief

Minimize the need for users to enter the same information repeatedly unless necessary for security, confirmation, or updating information.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> Information previously entered by or provided to the user that is required to be entered again in the same process is either:
>
> * auto-populated, or
> * available for the user to select.
>
> Except when:
>
> * re-entering the information is essential,
> * the information is required to ensure the security of the content, or
> * previously entered information is no longer valid.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| In a checkout flow, the user is asked for their shipping address and then asked for their billing address (which is often the same). | In a checkout flow, for billing, users can select a "same as shipping address" option. |
| In the first step of a registration flow, the user is asked for their phone number; in the last step, they are asked to confirm the phone number.  | In the last step to confirm the phone number, the phone number field is pre-populated with the number previously entered. |

documents.title: 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (2.2 AA)
documents.content:
# 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (2.2 AA)

## In brief

Make logins possible with less mental effort. Don't make people solve, remember, or transcribe something to log in.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> A cognitive function test (such as remembering a password or solving a puzzle) is not required for any step in an authentication process unless that step provides at least one of the following:
>
> * **Alternative**
>   * Another authentication method that does not rely on a cognitive function test.
> * **Mechanism**
>   * A mechanism is available to assist the user in completing the cognitive function test.
> * **Object Recognition**
>   * The cognitive function test is to recognize objects.
> * **Personal Content**
>   * The cognitive function test is to identify non-text content the user provided to the Web site.
> 
> **Note**
>
> "Object recognition" and "Personal content" may be represented by images, video, or audio.
> 
> **Note**
> 
> Examples of mechanisms that satisfy this criterion include:
>   1. support for password entry by password managers to reduce memory need, and
>   2. copy and paste to reduce the cognitive burden of re-typing.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| User cannot paste a password into the input. | User is able to paste a password into the input (and use a password manager to populate). |
| User is required to perform a math test during a login process. | User is not required to perform a math (nor any "cognitive function test") test during a login process. |
| User is required to transcribe graphical text or audio during a login process. | User is required to identify objects during a login process. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* None

-->

|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
