## Additional guidance

* If there is a multi-factor authentication process (MFA), all steps need to comply with this Success Criterion to pass.
* Acceptable alternative authentication methods, usually use for MFA, may include:
  * Entering a verification code generated or received on a device.
  * Biometrics such as fingerprint scanning and facial recognition.
* Evaluating whether or not a verification code can be seamlessly transferred from a secondary device to a primary device is outside of the scope for this SC.
* A test to recognize objects passes this SC, but there still may be a usability/culture problem with this type of test. This is outside of the scope of WCAG. Note that the AAA version of this SC — 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)— does not allow this technique.

documents.title: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (2.0 A)
documents.content:
# 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (2.0 A)

## In brief

All UI components have an accessible name, role, value, state and properties (if applicable).

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> For all user interface components (including but not limited to: form elements, links and components generated by scripts), the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes to these items is available to user agents, including assistive technologies.

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 1**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A `div` or `span` is used to recreate a UI control without specifying its role and name. | A standard HTML control, such as a `button`, is used since it has built-in role and name. |
| A form input does not have an accessible name. | All form inputs have an accessible name, normally given by a programmatically associated `label` element. |
| An invalid ARIA attribute is used. | Only ARIA attributes that are valid for a given HTML element are used. |
| A link does not have an accessible name. | All links have an accessible name, which may or may not be visible such as a linked logo image. |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Send button is not programmatically defined as disabled 'User Message' edit field** [Issue #10982](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10982)
  * The button isn't programmatically identified as disabled. As a result, screen reader users will not be notified that the control is disabled.
  * This could cause them to think something is wrong if they attempt to interact with the control, but nothing happens.
* **'Contribution activity in 2025' control is incorrectly defined as link** [Issue 11415](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11415)
  * Buttons and links are expected to serve different purposes.
  * Buttons are expected to perform an action (e.g., expand a section, switch between tabs of content on a page, open a drop-down menu, submit a form).
  * Links are expected to navigate to different locations within the page, across the site, or to external site locations.
  * In this case, the various buttons representing different years the GitHub account contributed are programmatically assigned the role of links even though they do not navigate the user to different locations at all.
  * These buttons act like tabs by swapping out the information under the Contributions section of the user's profile with the relevant content for the selected year.
  * Having these as links could cause the user to expect their focus to be moved elsewhere on the page or taken to a different page, when that is not what is happening.
* **Screen reader does not announce the state information** [Issue 11595](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11595)
  * The selected/unselected state is not announced by screen readers.
  * As a result, screen reader users will be unable to tell what options they have selected/unselected.
* **Screen reader does not announce the value information for the 'QTY' control** [Issue 11611](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11611)
  * Upon navigating to the "QTY" control with a screen reader, the current value is not announced.
  * As a result, screen reader users will have difficulty confirming whether they selected the correct quantity is listed.
* **Label is not defined for checkbox control** [Issue 11383](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11383)
  * In this case, there is a visible label for the checkbox, but that label is not programmatically linked with its respective checkbox.
  * There is an empty `aria-describedby` attribute on the label, which is serving no purpose, even though the label is supposed to be describing the checkbox.
  * Both need to be programmatically linked, and the whole checkbox group should additionally be programmatically linked to a group label so that the information is conveyed to assistive technologies like screen readers.
* **Interactive controls are nested together** [Issue 11381](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11381)
  * When interactive controls are nested within one another, they may behave in unexpected ways with assistive technologies that could cause information and functionality to not be clearly communicated.
  * Ensure interactive controls don't have focusable descendants by separating nested interactive components.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| A control has a role of button but functions as a link. | A control has a role of link and functions as a link. |
| A control has a role of link but functions as a button. | A control has a role of button and functions as a button. |

## Additional guidance

* A common issue seen reported under 4.1.2 is ARIA roles being misspelled, resulting in axe DevTools reporting an [ARIA roles used must conform to valid values](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.2/aria-roles) issue (e.g., [Issue #12599](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/12599)).
   * Double-check that the ARIA attribute value is valid.
   * A common example is `role="image"` instead of `role="img"` ([ARIA: img role | MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/img_role)).
   * [WAI-ARIA Roles | MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles) provides information on valid values and uses for individual ARIA roles.
* Please review [Required Form Input Use Cases](general-guidance/required-input-use-cases.md) for additional guidance related to this SC and required form inputs.

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Primer resources

* [Semantic HTML and ARIA | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/semantic-html-and-aria)
* [Descriptive buttons | Primer accessibility patterns](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/descriptive-buttons)
* [Links and buttons | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/links-and-buttons)

## Other resources

* [Understanding SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value)
* [MAS 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-4.1.2-Name-Role-Value-Guide.aspx)
* [WCAG Helper 4.1.2](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#412-name-role-value)
* [`nested-interactive` | Info and Examples for Accessibility Insights for Web](https://accessibilityinsights.io/info-examples/web/nested-interactive/)
* [Nested interactive controls are not announced by screen readers | axe Rules | Deque University](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.2/nested-interactive)
* [Basics of event handling in the DOM | GitHub Accessibility Repo](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/c03200e31ec29449695db7583a4f69646c07cf39/docs/wiki/javascript_events.md#basics-of-event-handling-in-the-dom)
* [Short Note on: Button or Link? | TPGi](https://www.tpgi.com/short-note-on-button-or-link/)
* [Link and Button guidance | GitHub Accessibility Playbook](https://accessibility-playbook.github.com/link-and-button-guidance)
* **ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG)**
  * **APG Practices**
    * [Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/names-and-descriptions/)
    * [Developing a Keyboard Interface](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/)

documents.title: 4.1.3 Status Messages (2.1 AA)
documents.content:
# 4.1.3 Status Messages (2.1 AA)

## In brief

Users of assistive technology are made aware of important changes in content.

## Normative

This is the actual text from the WCAG Success Criterion.

> In content implemented using markup languages, [status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages#dfn-status-message) can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.

> [!NOTE]
> A status message is defined as:
>
> change in content that is not a [change of context](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages#dfn-changes-of-context), and that provides information to the user on the success or results of an action, on the waiting state of an application, on the progress of a process, or on the existence of errors

## Examples of failures

**Default severity level: 2**

This is the recommended severity level for this SC. Please change accordingly depending on the circumstances of each bug issue.
Reference the [Severity level labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/estimation/severity.md).

| Actual | Expected |
|--------|----------|
| A search returns zero results and a message displays informing the user. Asistive technologies are unable to inform users of the status change. | A search returns zero results and a message displays informing the user. Asistive technologies inform users of the status change. |
| After a user selects a "recalculate" button, an icon symbolizing 'busy' appears on the screen but a screen reader announces nothing. | After a user selects a "recalculate" button, an icon symbolizing 'busy' appears on the screen and a screen reader announces "application busy". |

### Example GitHub issues

The following are a selection of GitHub issues that were failures of the relevant SC.

* **Screen reader does not announce the search result information on providing invalid input** [Issue 11464](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11464)
  * When a search query that provides no results is submitted, a status message informing the user that no results were found is displayed, but is not announced by the screen reader unless the user navigates downwards.
  * This adds extra effort for the screen reader user that requires them to navigate down and back up repeatedly while trying to search.
  * Instead, an `aria-live="polite"` or `role="status"` should be used so that this information is announced to the user when it appears, thus giving them a more uniform experience regardless of whether they are using a screen reader.
  * Do not use a `role="alert"` or `aria-live="assertive"` as these will interrupt the screen reader as soon as they appear rather than allowing it to first finish its current announcement to avoid causing the user to miss information.
* **Screen reader does not announce displayed status message** [Issue 11553](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/11553)
  * When the user provides an invalid webhook, a status message informing them of the error appears, which is not announced by screen readers.
  * As a result, a screen reader user may be entirely unaware of the error and not know why their submission was not successful, or not even be informed that it was unsuccessful.
  * In addition to the usual `aria-live` or `role="status"` methods, if the error is persistant, `aria-describedby` should be used to link the error to its field so it is read off if the user enters the field again.

## Examples of usability issues and best practices

**Default severity level: 4**

These are examples of usability issues and best practices that wouldn't necessarily fail WCAG.

* None
<!--
| Actual | Preferred |
|--------|-----------|
| Placeholder | Placeholder |
-->

## Additional Guidance

* **Dynamically generated search results**
  * Dynamically generated search results are not status messages, but if there is brief text provided that conveys the completion of the search, then that is a status message.
  * Per the [Understanding SC 4.1.3: Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages):
  > Information can be added to pages which does not meet the [definition of a status message](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html#dfn-status-message). For example, the list of results obtained from a search are not considered a status update and thus are not covered by this Success Criterion. However, brief text messages displayed about the completion or status of the search, such as "Searching...", "18 results returned" or "No results returned" would be status updates if they do not take focus. Examples of status messages are given in the section titled Status Message Examples below.
* **New page loads in**
  * When a new page loads dynamically, and that change is not announced, this does not fall under 4.1.3 Status Message because it is a change in content which by definition is a change of context.
  * For example, with [issue 8210](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/8210), a user logins and the screen reader does not announce anything about the new page.
    * This falls under [2.4.3 Focus Order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order.html) as the focus is not managed when the content changes. In this case, the focus should go to the top of the page or top of the main content (i.e., the "Registration" heading).
    * If the change in content or context happens unexpectedly, then this could fall under one of the [Guideline 3.2: Predictable](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/predictable) success criterion.
* **Informational text that can become status messages**
  * In [Issue #6630](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/8607), a user can preview a pull-request. In doing so, a message displays at the bottom of the window indicating whether or not this pull request would be able to merge without conflicts.
  * While this is the current status of the pull request, it is currently just providing general information that isn't a change of context for the user. When a user initially opens a pull request, they expect it be displayed as either able to be merged or as having conflicts. Thus, it does not need to be announced, *yet*.
  * In this particular instance, if the user could make further changes in the window that would cause that message to update from what it initially displayed as, then it would be considered a status message and users would need to be informed of the change.
* **Context changes that occur as a result of a full page refresh**
  * When a context change occurs as a result of a full page refresh, then it does not need to be announced.
  * By virtue of the page fully refreshing, the user reasonably expects that the content will change.
  * However, it is important to ensure that the action that triggered the page refresh would be reasonably expected by the user to do so. If it wouldn't, then that could count as a failure of success criteria [3.2.1 On Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-focus) or [3.3.2 On Input](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-input).

## Accessibility Council decisions

* When auditing CLI, this SC does not apply. See [CLI-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Resources

* [Understanding SC 4.1.3 Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages)
* [MAS 4.1.3: Status Messages](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-4.1.3-Status-Messages-Guide.aspx)
* [WCAG Helper 4.1.3](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/wcag-helper.md#413-status-messages)
  * **APG Patterns**
    * [Alert Pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/)
* [The Complete Guide to ARIA Live Regions for Developers | A11y Collective](https://www.a11y-collective.com/blog/aria-live/)

documents.title: Process for Audit Request Extensions
documents.content:
# Process for Audit Request Extensions

This document outlines the process for extending a deadline for an accessibility audit for a project. We have two terms for this which are used interchangeably: "audit extension" and "audit exception". This is different from an exception request which asks for an extension on bug issues rather than an audit.

This Audit Request Extensions process should be used for annual audit exceptions, not for initial accessibility audits. It pertains to both strategic and non-strategic services. It does NOT apply to feature audits nor GA audits. 

Audit Request Extensions are managed by @weboverhauls within CELA Accessibility.

## Creating an Audit Request Extension

1. The service owner [requests an audit extension](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/issues/new?template=audit-request-extension.yml) for a project audit.
1. The request issue is added to the project board [Accessibility audit extension requests](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/20362/views/1).
1. The extension request is reviewed by CELA Accessibility.
1. If the extension request is denied:
    1. Reviewer enters a comment and closes the extension request.
    2. In the project board, reviewer marks the extension request as Done. 
1. If the extension request is accepted:
    1. Reviewer adds the `exception-audit` label to the request.
    1. Reviewer enters a comment to the extension request to accept the request and to confirm the date.
    1. In the project board, reviewer marks the extension request as In Progress. 
    1. Reviewer comments on the audit request issue and includes: confirmation of the extension; the expiration date; a link to the extension request issue. 

NOTES:
- The extension request issues are to remain open until extension period is completely over.
- A programmatic solution was begun but not completed; [see issue #2170](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/issues/2170)

## Ending an Audit Request Extension

1. Remove the `audit-extension` label from the audit request issue and add a comment.
1. Close the extension request issue and add a comment.
1. In the project board, mark the extension request as Done.

## References:

- [Policy for audit request exceptions](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/audit-request-exceptions.md)
- [Overview of the audit process](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/FAQs.md#how-does-the-process-work)
- [How to get to MAS C](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/governance/how-to-get-to-MAS-C.md)
- Origination of auto-generated audit requests: [Request] Automation: Open Audit Requests [#2876](https://github.com/github/accessibility-scorecard/issues/2876)

documents.title: Audit Flowchart
documents.content: # Audit Flowchart [The Accessibility Audit Flowchart via Figma](https://www.figma.com/board/pVc93Zbe20hePF1WANyEfa/A11y-Gov-Flows?node-id=1-530&p=f&t=3ctmgUn4BnNFRdzg-0) Text version: 1. Start 1. Is the service team in the a11y scorecards? - If yes, continue to next step. - If no, Service team creates a [request to add service to a11y scorecards](https://github.com/github/accessibility-scorecard/issues/new?template=add-service-to-scorecard.yml). CELA A11y [adds service](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/governance/service-updates/adding-services.md) to the a11y scorecards. 1. Does the service team need a [feature audit](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/FAQs.md#my-project-is-large-and-complex-can-i-test-only-the-new-functionality-or-feature-we-are-adding)? - Note: This should be rare. A feature audit request should only be requested for a subset of a project — relatively small updates that do not warrant the full re-auditing of an entire project. [Feature audit example](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/7342) - If no, continue to next step. - If yes, Service team manually [creates an audit request](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/new?template=a11y-audit-request.yml) for the feature. Go to step 5. 1. Audit request issues automatically created for each project; message posted to [#accessibility-reminders](https://github-grid.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C053TD6K0RZ). - Note: An audit request is generated for each project listed under a service (see [SLA data](https://github.com/github/accessibility-scorecard/tree/main/service-level-agreements/data)). They are due to be opened 9 months after the previous audit was completed (1-year requirement minus 3-month lead time). 1. Tester confirms and modifies audit details and [applies corresponding labels](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/instructions-for-auditors.md#adding-labels). 1. Tester schedules a [demo meeting](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/process.md#3-demo-meeting). 1. Tester drafts scenarios. 1. Service team approves scenarios. - Note 1: Per the [Scenario SLA](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/audit-scenarios.md), if two weeks pass without this step completed, CELA A11y will move the audit to the next step. - Note 2: The [Scenario Framework](https://github.com/github/scenarios) has great info to help with this step. Ideally, use of the scenario framework would replace this step (and has other benefits too!). 1. Testers perform audit and create GitHub issues for problems found. 1. CELA A11y [refines issues](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/triage-process.md). 1. CELA A11y [creates an audit hand-off issue](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/handoff-process.md) to service team. 1. Service team replies via comment in the hand-off issue. 1. Does the service team request a handoff meeting? - If yes, CELA A11y schedules and conducts handoff meeting with service team. - If no, continue to next step. 1. CELA A11y completes hand-off to service team and closes audit. 1. End For more info on the accessibility audit process: - [Audit Process](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/process.md) - [Audit FAQs](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/FAQs.md) - [How to get to MAS C](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/governance/how-to-get-to-MAS-C.md)

documents.title: Governance Escalations
documents.content:
# Governance Escalations Created: January 2026 ## Problem statement The accessibility auditing and governance programs experience major delays in auditing and service maintenance. This is primarily caused by lack of response from service owners, and sometimes due to lack of clarity about ownership. Activities where we have to get people to communicate include: * Getting information when adding a service or a project. * Identifying audit test scenarios. * Scheduling audit onboarding meetings. * Getting assistance when testers are blocked by incorrectly documented / communicated UI, access issues, etc. * Handing off audit findings. * Following up when audits or bug issues fall out of SLA. * Adding, removing, or modifying services in the accessibility scorecards. Over the last 10 months, approximately 11% of audit requests were blocked. (See the [Blocked Audits](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/20994/) project board for history.) This is significant number, especially considering that this does *not* consider: * Multiple reminders that were already communicated before blocked status was applied. Many delayed audits were never reported as blocked. * Service requests that were blocked (only audits were considered in the stat). ## Problems with the current escalation steps Problems with the current escalation steps (see “Current escalation steps“ below) include: * The process is not well documented. * Jurisdiction for EPD Staff Program Manager is limited to EPD. \ For example: * OCOO / Kyle’s org: zendesk, lumos, github-stars, github-blog, github-swag-shop * HR: fragomen * Revenue: HelpHub * See the table below for more details * No time periods identified for the next step. * Sometimes the escalation steps are not effective. ## Goals We need a plan for escalating a lack of response from service owners in audit requests or when there’s a lack of clarity about ownership. In addition to audit requests, the new path will also cover lack of response from service owners in service requests (particularly when adding a service) and other related tasks. The new escalation steps will: * Be approved by the Head of Accessibility * Be documented * Implement automation and AI as much as possible ## Current escalation steps When service owners do not respond to an audit request issue, the auditing team reminds the service owners in the following ways. 1. HCL Lead asks for action from service owners via a comment in the audit request issue. 2. HCL Lead comments with a reminder. 3. HCL Lead monitors and comments again and tags CELA if no reply. 4. CELA Accessibility Specialist comments on the issue (and ensures all service owners are tagged). 5. CELA Accessibility Program Manager comments on the issue (and ensures all service owners are tagged). 6. CELA Accessibility Specialist direct messages service owners via Slack. 7. CELA Accessibility Specialist emails service owners. 8. CELA Accessibility escalates to EPD Staff Program Manager via the Slack #accessibility-sponsors channel. ## Revised escalation steps Below are the steps for reminders for ALL audit types (GA, Annual, Feature) when the DRI is not responding. ### Definitions * CELA PM - CELA Senior Accessibility Program Manager * FAM DRI = Functional Area MAS compliance DRI * Project board = [Accessibility WCAG Audit Testing Schedule (HCL)](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/5332/) ### Revised steps Step 0: No action needed. HCL Lead makes an initial ask for action from service owners in the audit request issue. 1. **Awaiting response**. HCL Lead comments with a reminder which sets expectations for response (within working 3 days) and tags CELA Accessibility Specialist. - CELA Accessibility Specialist modifies the audit request issue in project board: - Apply the “1. Awaiting response” state to the “Requested Info” column in the project board. - Add date to “Response due date” column in the project board (set date to 3 working days ahead). - CELA Accessibility Specialist comments on the issue; ensures all service owners are tagged. - Automation: none 2. **Reminded**. After 3 working days, CELA Accessibility Specialist direct messages all service owners via Slack. - CELA Accessibility Specialist comments in the audit request issue that a Slack message was sent and in the comment tags the FAM DRI (see table below). - CELA Accessibility Specialist applies the “2. Reminded” state to the “Requested Info” column in the project board. - Automation: TBD 3. **Blocked**. After 3 working days, CELA PM escalates. - CELA PM adds to the [blocked audits project board](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/20994/). - CELA PM applies the “3. Blocked” state to the “Requested Info” column in the project board. - CELA PM contacts FAM DRI via a Slack DM. (If EPD, contact Janice first.) - CELA PM comments on the issue. - Automation: TBD 4. **Escalated**. After 3 working days, CELA PM notifies FAM DRI via the [#fundamentals](https://github-grid.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C011ZHR7QP9) Slack channel and copies Fundamentals Lead (Deepthi). - CELA PM applies the “4. Escalated” state to the “Requested Info” column in the project board. - CELA PM comments on the issue. - Automation: TBD 5. **Top escalation**. The Fundamentals Lead escalates. - Fundamentals Lead further escalates to Fundamentals-LT Slack channel, CTO (Vlad), and/or monthly Fundamentals meeting. - This step is expected to be rare. - Automation: none ### Supporting resources * Table version of revised steps: [Escalations steps for A11y Audits](https://microsoft-my.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/personal/dlembree_microsoft_com/Documents/Governance/Escalations%20steps%20for%20A11y%20Audits.xlsx?d=w6d0e9d8d60fd5486f6fcb24b6e04f395&csf=1&web=1&e=KdhPBE) * [Requested info](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/5332/views/21) tab in the HCL audit board ## Important notes * CELA manages the “Requested Info” and “Response due date” values in the project board. * If the service owner responds adequately, the “Requested Info” column in the project board is returned to the default state of “0. No info needed”. * Scenarios: If the request is for approving an audit scenario, the approval is waived after 2 weeks and the audit moves to the next stage. See the [Scenario Policy](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/audit-scenarios.md). * Hand-off: If the request is for accepting an audit hand-off, the audit hand-off and audit request issues may be closed after 2 weeks (1 week if no Sev 1-2 issues). See the [Hand-off Policy](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/audit-handoff.md). ## Misc ideas and enhancements * Use automation for steps 2-4. * Consider the individual team's Slack channel for escalation messages. * Consider for FAM DRI reminder; could work well with automation (like the Remediation workflow). * Improve language for reminders. * Create MD report or Slack message listing audits at risk; post to #fundamentals. ## Reports TBD ## Resources & related policies * [Functional Area via the CRM board](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/21486/views/22) * [Audit Scenario Policy](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/audit-scenarios.md) * [Audit Handoff Policy](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/audit-handoff.md) * [Service Request Policy](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/service-requests.md) * [Blocked Audits](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/20994/) project board for history ## Sample messages * [https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/9502#issuecomment-3407706574](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/9502#issuecomment-3407706574) * [https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/9186#issuecomment-3259463696](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/9186#issuecomment-3259463696) * [https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/8792#issuecomment-2981437066](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/8792#issuecomment-2981437066) ## Management escalation path Last update: November 20, 2025

documents.title: handoff-process
documents.content: To complete the handoff, the service owners must comment on this ticket to indicate whether they prefer to schedule a meeting to discuss these steps or if an asynchronous handoff is acceptable. The governance team prefers a "manual" handoff so that an actual person on the team acknowledges the audit which provides accountability.# Handoff Process ## Background After the refining of issues is completed for an audit, the results of the audit need to be handed off to the service team for remediation. A handoff issue is created which includes pertinent links, SLA information, and tips for remediation. To complete the handoff, the service owners must comment on this ticket to indicate whether they prefer to schedule a meeting to discuss the audit or if an asynchronous handoff is acceptable. The governance team prefers this "manual" handoff process so that a person on the team acknowledges the completion of the audit which provides accountability. Note that if the service owners do not reply within 1-2 weeks, the handoff will be closed. ## Handoff Instructions 1. Create an issue using the [Audit Issues Handoff template](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/new?template=audit_issues_handoff.md). 1. Complete the template. - Update the subject with the name of project. - `[Handoff Request]` should be at the front of the title. - This should be automatically added if you use the template. - If not, clearing your session cookies may resolve this. - Address the pertinent Hubbers via their handles (typically found in the description of the audit request or the service's tracking/CRM issue). - Link the audit request, its project board, and the refining request. - If refinement was not necessary: 1. Replace the placeholder for the "Refining Request" link with: `*N/A - No refinement necessary*` 2. Remove `Note: only Severity 1/2/3 WCAG issues have been refined. While higher severity issues should take precedence over lower severity ones, all accessibility audit issues must be addressed to ensure the inclusivity of your service.` 3. Replace the first sentence with the following: `Your team's accessibility audit has been successfully refined! This issue serves as a handoff, providing instructions for the next steps. There were no Severity 1/2/3 WCAG issues identified during the audit.` - Ask requestor and DRI if they prefer to schedule a meeting to review or if an asynchronous handoff is suitable. 1. Submit the issue. 1. Update the relevant fields for the issue in the [Accessibility Audit Handoff Tracking board](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/22816/). - The issue should be automatically added to this board as long as it has the `audit-handoff` label. - For more details on the field options for the board, view the [Accessibility Audit Handoff Tracking Board Explained](#accessibility-audit-handoff-tracking-board-explained) section of this page. 1. Add the handoff issue as a sub-issue of the corresponding audit request issue. 1. In both the audit request issue and in the refining request issue, create a comment stating that the refining request is complete and include a link to the handoff issue. ([sample copy](handoff-process.md#handoff---refining-request-completion)) 1. If refinement was not necessary, ensure the comment reflects that. 1. Close the refining request issue. 1. Move the audit request issue to Step 7 “Ready for Handoff”. 1. If a meeting is requested: - Schedule a 30-minute meeting with the audit requestor and DRI. - Conduct the meeting and explain the results of the audit, next steps, and answer any questions. - As talking points you can use the information in the MAS Grade Audit Process document starting at the section [Issues are handed off to the feature team](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/process.md#8-issues-are-handed-off-to-the-feature-team). - Update the [relevant fields of the Accessibility Audit Handoff Tracking Board](#accessibility-audit-handoff-tracking-board-explained): - **Handoff Type**: Set to "Meeting Requested" / "Meeting Scheduled" - **Meeting Scheduled**: Set to the date the meeting is scheduled for. 1. After handoff is approved by the audit requestor or DRI: - Close the handoff issue. - Comment on the audit issue and include a link to the handoff issue. ([sample copy](handoff-process.md#audit---when-handoff-is-complete)) - Close the audit request issue. - Move the audit request issue to Step 8 “Done”. [This step is automated now.] - Update the relevant [fields in the Accessibility Audit Handoff Tracking Board](#accessibility-audit-handoff-tracking-board-explained). ## Closing Handoff when no response Usually, we close due to no response after 2 weeks if no response is received from commenting a reminder, Slack DMs, and/or emailing to contact the service contacts (exact combination may depend on the team since we find some methods work better than others for some teams). With handoffs where there are no Severity 1/2 issues, we will instead wait just 1 week, but still try to contact the team via Slack and/or email first. The following are examples of general contact timelines: - General contact timeline for issues with Severity 1/2 issues: - 2 to 3 days after handoff creation of handoff - add reminder comment to issue - 5 days after handoff creation of handoff - Send email reminder - 10 days after handoff creation of handoff - Send slack reminder - General contact timeline for issues without Severity 1/2 issues: - 2 to 3 days after handoff creation of handoff - Send email/slack reminder - Close with comment about no response and there being no Severity 1/2 issues. Timings can vary slightly based on weekends and holidays. View the [Audit Handoff policy](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/audit-handoff.md) for more details. You can use some of the reminder status options and the "Last Reminder" field for the handoff issue in the Accessibility Audit Handoff Tracking board to keep track of when and what reminders reminders you last sent. Additionally, if you close the audit with no response, set the status on the Handoff tracking board to either "Closed, no response received", or "Closed, response N/A" as relevant. See the [Accessibility Audit Handoff Tracking Board Explained](#accessibility-audit-handoff-tracking-board-explained) section of this page for more details on when to use either status. ## Example text for comments ### Handoff - Instructions [Moved to the [handoff template](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/new?template=audit_issues_handoff.md)] ### Handoff - Refining Request completion ``` Refinement is complete! Please refer to the [handoff instructions](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/NUMBER) for more information on next steps. ``` ### Handoff - Refining Request completion when no refinement necessary ``` Refinement is not necessary due to zero Severity 1/2 issues, congrats! Audit ready for handoff. Please refer to the [handoff instructions](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/NUMBER) for more information on next steps. ``` ### Handoff - Reminder ``` @handle(s) Please let me know if you prefer to schedule a meeting to discuss the audit results or if an asynchronous handoff is suitable for you. Thank you! ``` ### Audit - when handoff is complete ``` [Handoff is complete](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/NUMBER)! Feel free to reach out if you have any further questions on the [audit process](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/process.md), [exceptions](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/exceptions.md), or [MAS grading](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/MAS-grades.md). ``` ## Accessibility Audit Handoff Tracking Board Explained The [Accessibility Audit Handoff Tracking board](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/22816/), offers a way to track the progress of handoffs, keep a record of reminders sent, and identify potential areas for improvement within the handoff process. Fields currently found in the board include: - **Status**: Current status of the handoff. Options include: - **In Progress** - **Issue comment reminder** / **Slack reminder** / **Email reminder**: A reminder was sent to the service owners. - **Meeting Requested** / **Meeting Scheduled**: Service owners requested a meeting or one has been scheduled. - **Closed, with response**: Closed after receiving confirmation of an async handoff or after completing a handoff meeting. - **Closed, no response received**: Closed after receiving no response from the service team in over a week. - **Closed, response N/A**: Closed without waiting a week for a response or because it was determined a response was not needed. (i.e., service deprecated, no severity 1 or 2 issues found, end of quarter / fiscal year cleanup, etc.). - **Open Date**: Date the handoff was opened. - **Date Completed**: The date that one of the following occurred: - received confirmation of an async handoff from service owners - completed a handoff meeting - the handoff was closed as no response received or response N/A - **Last Reminder**: The date you last sent out a reminder. - **Meeting Scheduled**: Date a handoff meeting was scheduled, if applicable. - **GA Audit?**: Indicate if the handoff was part of a GA audit. **Yes** if it was a GA audit and **No** if it was any other kind of audit. - **Handoff Type**: Select what kind of handoff occurred, options include: - **Async Handoff** - **Handoff Meeting** - **No Response**: Use if you waited at least a week for a response but did not receive one. - **N/A**: Use if it was determined a response was not needed. - This typically occurs if there were no severity 1/2 issues, if we are closing out handoffs at the end of a quarter, if the handoff was a duplicate (that couldn't be deleted), or if the service was deprecated and so we decided to not do a handoff.

documents.title: Examples for WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels compliance in CLIs
documents.content:
# Examples for WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels compliance in CLIs

The "headings and labels" [WCAG criteria
](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#headings-and-labels) requires that when there
is content inside a heading, it should be descriptive of how content is
organized. It does _not_ mandate creating headings.

## Definition of "heading" in a CLI context

Unlike with web pages, where authors may use heading HTML tags or the `role="heading"`
attribute combined with the `aria-level` attribute,
**there is no way to create a semantic heading in a CLI application**.

However, certain text may be emphasized in a CLI application's output by
surrounding it with other characters and/or a large amount of white space to visually separate it from the rest of
the output. As an example from the [delta git pager](https://github.com/dandavison/delta):

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
commit <commit hash>                               ┃
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┻━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Author: author name
Date:   date

    commit message
```

We treat these visually-separated snippets of text as headings in a CLI context, as they are
decorated in a way which implies the CLI application author intends them to help
structure the contents of the output, just like semantic headings in a web
context.

The exact character(s) used to create the visual separation don't
matter as the end effect is the same.

## Evaluating success for this criteria in CLIs

If there are no implied headings in the output, the application passes.

If there are implied headings in the output, the application only passes if the
text of those headings is descriptive of the structure of the output's content.

### Example of Success

```
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                          SEARCHING

  /pattern          *  Search forward for (N-th) matching line.
  ?pattern          *  Search backward for (N-th) matching line.
  n                 *  Repeat previous search (for N-th occurrence).
  N                 *  Repeat previous search in reverse direction.
  ESC-n             *  Repeat previous search, spanning files.
```

The implied heading ("Searching") is descriptive of the following content and
structure (a list of commands related to searching).

### Example of Failure

```
Installing library X
Installing library Y

------------------
| Almost there!! |
------------------

Installing library Z
Authenticating user
```

The implied heading ("Almost there!!") is _not_ descriptive of the structure of
the preceding or following content.

documents.title: How to apply an SLA extension
documents.content:
# How to apply an SLA extension 

This file defines how to apply an SLA extension to one or more audit issues. 

## Ensure the extension has been approved 

There is an approvals process that must be completed before an SLA extension can be applied to audit issues. 
We're still building that approvals process. 
So, for the time being we will indicate that approval is complete by manualy adding the exception request issue to the board where @alexandra-tashjian tracks labelling work.


## Applying the extension 

1. Review the exception request issue. That issue should contain a list of the audit issues that need an extension and the date for the extension.
2. Open the [accessibility scorecard project board](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/10080/).
3. Add the audit issues to the accessibility scorecard project board and  insert the extension date on the "exception granted" view.
4. Add the "sla-extension" label to the audit issues in the accessibility-audits repo.

documents.title: Mobile-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA)
documents.content:
# Mobile-WCAG Mapping (WCAG 2.2 AA) This table defines which WCAG Success Criterion (SC) apply to native mobile applications (iOS and Android apps) for accessibility audits. In general, all SC are applied directly as written, and as described in intent from their [WCAG 2.2 Understanding document](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/). Some wording is just altered to better reflect the differences between mobile and desktop environments, which may limit or alter how developers can support WCAG SC. These differences are covered by notes linked under some SC, which come from the: - [Guidance on Applying WCAG 2 to Non-Web Information and Communications Technologies (WCAG2ICT)](https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag2ict-22/) - [Guidance on Applying WCAG 2.2 to Mobile (WCAG2Mobile)](https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag2mobile-22/) by the W3C's Mobile Accessibility Task Force (MATF) It is recommended that you review the notes on individual SC found within those documents when in doubt for further guidance. Additional resources related to the differences in SC interpretation between mobile and desktop environments can be found after the [WCAG Mobile to Web Mapping Table](#wcag-mobile-to-web-mapping-table) section of this page. ## WCAG Mobile to Web Mapping Table | WCAG SC | Applicable to Mobile?
(Yes / No / Partial) | Notes | |:--------|:----------------------------------------------:|:------| | **Perceivable** | | | | **1.1 Text Alternatives** | | | | 1.1.1 Non-text Content | Yes | | | **1.2 Time-based Media** | | | | 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) | Yes | | | 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) | Yes | The WCAG 2 definition of "captions" notes that in some countries, captions are called subtitles. | | 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) | Yes |
  • The WCAG 2 definition of “audio description” says that "audio description" is "also called ‘video description’ and ‘descriptive narration’”.
  • Secondary or alternate audio tracks are commonly used for this purpose.
| | 1.2.4 Captions (Live) | Yes | | | 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) | Yes | | | **1.3 Adaptable** | | | | 1.3.1 Info and Relationships | Yes | In software, programmatic determinability is best achieved through the use of [accessibility services provided by platform software](https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag2ict-22/#accessibility-services-of-platform-software) to enable interoperability between software and assistive technologies and accessibility features of software. | | 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence | Yes | Grouping related elements in a way that helps ensure meaningful reading sequence and that hidden elements are not announced. | | 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics | Yes | | | 1.3.4 Orientation | Yes | Mobile applications should support both portrait and landscape orientations unless a specific orientation is essential (e.g., a game or medical app requiring a fixed orientation). Fixed display orientation hardware exceptions may still apply. Refer to the [WCAG 2.2 Understanding document for Orientation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/orientation.html) for more details. | | 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose | Yes | For non-web software and non-web documents that present input fields, the terms for the input purposes would be the equivalent terms to those listed in the [WCAG 2.2 section Input Purposes for User Interface Components](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#input-purposes) that are supported by the technology used.| | **1.4 Distinguishable** | | | | 1.4.1 Use of Color | Yes | | | 1.4.2 Audio Control | Yes | | | 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) | Yes | | | 1.4.4 Resize Text | Yes | For how to test on iOS and Android, refer to the Validation section of the [MAS 1.4.4: Resize Text Guide](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/MAS-1.4.4-Resize-Text-Guide.aspx#a37695de-2552-4f85-9529-c9275c5fb997) | | 1.4.5 Images of Text | Yes | | | 1.4.10 Reflow | Partial | The WCAG2ICT Task Force made changes to give additional guidance around how 1.4.10 Reflow should be applied to non-web software in response to public comments. Refer directly to the WCAG2ICT documentation: [Applying SC 1.4.10 Reflow to Non-Web Documents and Software](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#applying-sc-1-4-10-reflow-to-non-web-documents-and-software). | | 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast | Yes | | | 1.4.12 Text Spacing | Partial | Applies only to a WebView. | | 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus | Yes | | | **Operable** | | | | **2.1 Keyboard Accessible** | | | | 2.1.1 Keyboard | Yes |
  • Keyboard interface does not refer to a physical device but to the interface between the software and any keyboard or keyboard substitute (i.e., the interface where the software accepts text or other keystroke input from the platform which may come from a keyboard or from a keyboard alternative).
  • This success criterion does not imply that software always needs to directly support a keyboard or “keyboard interface”. Nor does it imply that software always needs to provide a virtual keyboard.
| | 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap | Yes |
  • All views must meet this SC since failure to do so can interfere with a user's ability to use the full view.
  • Standard exit methods may vary by platform. For example, on many desktop platforms, the Escape key is a standard method for exiting.
  • This criterion applies when focus can be moved using a keyboard interface. Some software may accept input from a keyboard, keypad, or controller, yet not offer any mechanism for focus; for example, the keys are mapped directly to functions without moving focus between on-screen controls. In this case, there is no concept of focus, and therefore keyboard traps cannot exist and this success criterion would be satisfied.
| | 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts | Yes | Exception: Long presses and other accessibility features provided by the platform do not meet the WCAG definition of a keyboard shortcut. | | **2.2 Enough Time** | | | | 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable | Yes | | | 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide | Yes | | | **2.3 Seizures and Physical Reactions** | | | | 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold | Yes | | | **2.4 Navigable** | | | | 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks | Partial | This does not apply within an app, but may apply across a set of related apps. | | 2.4.2 Page Titled | Partial |
  • [Appears to apply to whole applications](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#applying-sc-2-4-2-page-titled-to-non-web-documents-and-software) rather than individual screens. Although the [implementation advice available](https://appt.org/en/guidelines/wcag/success-criterion-2-4-2#solution) appears to provide individual screen level methods.
  • Also see [Issue #437](https://github.com/w3c/wcag2ict/issues/437) and Mobile Content Accessibility Guidelines (MCAG) [3.1.1 Screen Titled](https://getevinced.github.io/mcag/#screen-titled).
| | 2.4.3 Focus Order | Yes | | | 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) | Yes | In software, a "link" is any text string or image in the user interface outside a user interface control that behaves like a hypertext link. **This does not include general user interface controls or buttons. (An OK button, for example, would not be a link.)** | | 2.4.5 Multiple Ways | Partial | See set of documents and set of software programs in the [Key Terms section of the WCAG2ICT document](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#key-terms) to determine when a group of documents or software is considered a set for this success criterion. (Sets of software that meet this definition appear to be extremely rare.) Those implementing the WCAG2ICT will need to consider if this success criterion is appropriate to apply to non-web documents and software. See the [Interpretation of Web Terminology in a Non-web Context](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#interpretation-of-web-terminology-in-a-non-web-context). | | 2.4.6 Headings and Labels | Yes | | | 2.4.7 Focus Visible | Yes | | | 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) | Yes | | | **2.5 Input Modalities** | | | | 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures | Yes | | | 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation | Yes | | | 2.5.3 Label in Name | Yes | | | 2.5.4 Motion Actuation | Yes | | | 2.5.7 Dragging Movements | Yes | | | 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) | Yes |
  • Targets that allow for values to be selected spatially based on position within the target are considered one target for the purpose of the success criterion. Examples include sliders, color pickers displaying a gradient of colors, or editable areas where you position the cursor.
  • In technologies where CSS is not used, the definition of 'CSS pixel' applies as described in [Applying “CSS pixel” to Non-Web Documents and Software](https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag2ict-22/#applying-css-pixel-to-non-web-documents-and-software).
| | **Understandable** | | | | **3.1 Readable** | | | | 3.1.1 Language of Page | Partial | Applies to application as a whole rather than individual screens. | | 3.1.2 Language of Parts | Partial | Examples of programmatic identification include language metadata or markup. In software and non-web document technologies where there is no assistive technology supported method for marking the language for the different passages or phrases in the non-web document or software it would not be possible to meet this success criterion. | | **3.2 Predictable** | | | | 3.2.1 On Focus | Yes | | | 3.2.2 On Input | Yes | | | 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation | Yes | See set of documents and set of software programs in the [Key Terms section of the WCAG2ICT document](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#key-terms) to determine when a group of documents or software is considered a set for this success criterion. (Sets of software that meet this definition appear to be extremely rare.) Those implementing the WCAG2ICT will need to consider if this success criterion is appropriate to apply to non-web documents and software. See the [Interpretation of Web Terminology in a Non-web Context](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#interpretation-of-web-terminology-in-a-non-web-context). | | 3.2.4 Consistent Identification | Yes | See set of documents and set of software programs in the [Key Terms section of the WCAG2ICT document](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#key-terms) to determine when a group of documents or software is considered a set for this success criterion. (Sets of software that meet this definition appear to be extremely rare.) Those implementing the WCAG2ICT will need to consider if this success criterion is appropriate to apply to non-web documents and software. See the [Interpretation of Web Terminology in a Non-web Context](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#interpretation-of-web-terminology-in-a-non-web-context). | | 3.2.6 Consistent Help | Yes | | | **3.3 Input Assistance** | | | | 3.3.1 Error Identification | Yes | | | 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions | Yes | | | 3.3.3 Error Suggestion | Yes | | | 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) | Yes | | | 3.3.7 Redundant Entry | Yes | | | 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) | Partial |
  • Any passwords used to unlock underlying platform software (running below the non-web software) are out of scope for this requirement since these are not under control of the non-web software’s author. For example, if the user can login with their Google account but Android forces them to use the Android interface separate from the app's interface to do so.
  • There are cases where non-web software has an authentication process and no alternative or assistance mechanism is feasible, for example when entering a password when starting, powering on / turning on an ICT (device or otherwise). In such situations, it may not be possible for the non-web software to meet this success criterion.
| | **Robust** | | | | **4.1 Compatible** | | | | 4.1.1 Parsing (Obsolete and removed) | No | | | 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | Yes | This applies directly as written, and as described in [Intent from Understanding Success Criterion 4.1.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value#intent), replacing the note with: "This success criterion is primarily for software developers who develop or use custom user interface components. For example, standard user interface components on most accessibility-supported platforms already meet this success criterion when used according to specification.” | | 4.1.3 Status Messages | Yes | | ## Success Criteria Problematic for Closed Functionality **Closed Functionality** is a property or characteristic that prevents users from attaching, installing, or using assistive technology. Some ICT limit the ability for users to use assistive technology, which results in some SC being more problematic than others in mobile or other ICT. More details, including the list of impacted SC, can be found in the [Success Criteria Problematic for Closed Functionality](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#success-criteria-problematic-for-closed-functionality) and [Comments on Closed Functionality](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#comments-on-closed-functionality) sections of the WCAG2ICT. ## Words Swapped in SC Intents While the Intent sections of each [SC's Understanding document](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/) are typically applied as is, there are some phrases that get swapped when discussing a mobile environment. Refer to the [Key Terms of the WCAG2ICT](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#key-terms) for clarification. ## Resources - [Does WCAG 2.2 apply to native apps](https://tetralogical.com/blog/2024/07/18/wcag2ict/) by TetraLogical - [Guidance from the Mobile Accessibility Task Force (MATF) Repo Issues](https://github.com/w3c/matf/issues/) — issues related to the WCAG2Mobile document that represent ongoing W3C discussions related to the application of WCAG SC to mobile environments. - [Does WCAG 2.2 apply to native apps - Tetralogical](https://tetralogical.com/blog/2024/07/18/wcag2ict/) - [Key Terms of the WCAG2ICT](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#key-terms)

documents.title: Re-Audits
documents.content:
# Re-Audits

## Definition

A "re-audit" or "reaudit" commonly refers to an accessibility audit of a project after an initial audit has been completed.

## Re-Audit Process Overview

- Feature team requests an audit under the [usual process](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/FAQs.md#how-does-the-process-work).
- Apply _one_ "audit-type" label:
  - The label `audit-type:re-audit` is applied to the audit request ticket.
  - For Fast-Pass audits (see below), the label `audit-type:fast-pass` is applied to the audit request ticket.
- The testers perform the audit and compare discovered issues against the previous audit — and are not to create duplicate issues.
- If the tester rediscovers an issue (an identical issue from a previous audit):
  - The tester adds the current audit label to the original issue.
  - The tester adds the `previously-discovered` label to the original issue.
  - Note: If this process wasn't followed, then the new audit may supersede the previous audit and the previous audit issues may be [marked stale](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/stale-issues.md).
 
## Scenarios to Test

For strategic and non-strategic services, all scenarios will be tested during re-audits. (For a period previously, only core scenarios were tested in some cases.) Read more info on [scenarios in the Audit Process document](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/process.md#4-approval-of-the-accessibility-user-scenarios).

## Fast-Pass Audit

> [!CAUTION]  
> Use of the Fast-Pass audit type is currently suspended for regular use (starting March 26, 2025). It will still be applied judiciously in special circumstances.

For a Re-Audit, if the user scenarios are not changed, and the functionality and content is virtually the same, then a less extensive audit may be completed instead of a regular audit. We call this a Fast-Pass Audit. For web-based products, this requires only the following:

- Automated test (such as with axe or Accessibility Insights)
- Keyboard testing (SC 2.1.1)

Requirements for mobile fast-pass testing:
- iOS: VoiceOver
- Android: TalkBack and automated test (such as Accessibility Scanner or axe Accessibility Analyzer)

The Fast-Pass Audit applies to both strategic and non-strategic services.

## Tips

- The "audit label" is a unique label for all audits. It contains the project and the month-year that the audit is conducted (such as "HCL-GHCodeScanning-Mar2024"); this label can be used to discern between multiple audits for the same project.
- To prevent your service from regressing to MAS Grade F, a service must be audited every 365 days. 
For more, reference the [MAS Grade Audit Process](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/process.md).

documents.title: Testing Guidelines for the GH Command Line Interface (CLI)
documents.content:
# Testing Guidelines for the GH Command Line Interface (CLI)

## Background

Accessibility audits are periodically conducted on GitHub CLI applications. Because WCAG is based on the web, there is confusion as to what portions are pertinent. This document defines the accessibility checkpoints for CLI applications. It is a revision of a document originally written by a vendor (HCL). 

Also reference the [CLI-WCAG Mapping table](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).

## Configuration for testing

### macOS

* Terminal app: Terminal
* Settings: Use default
* Default theme name: Basic (light)

### Windows

* Terminal app: Windows Terminal
* Settings: Use default
* Default theme name: Dark

### Accessibility features must be enabled 

> [!IMPORTANT] 
> The GitHub CLI must be tested with accessibility features enabled. You can read about those settings in `gh help accessibility`.

For convenience, these are the commands that must be run before testing:

```
# Display color using customizable, 4-bit accessible colors
$ gh config set accessible_colors enabled

# Use input prompts without redrawing the screen
$ gh config set accessible_prompter enabled

# Disable motion-based spinners for progress indicators in favor of text
$ gh config set spinner disabled
```

## Checkpoints

### Reading Order

Ensure that the meaning of content as output by a screen reader is the same as for a visual user. The sequence of text and other content must be consistent for visual and non-visual users. 

### Data Tables

Content that emits linear text in a tabular format should use a separator like tab or | or comma (not just spaces) to format the content. This allows the user to send the output to a file and open the tabular data excel where the tabular data may be easier to consume such as for a person using a screen reader.

Example:

```
+--------+--------------+---------------------+----------+-----------+
| USERID | NAME         | EMAILID             | PASSWORD | USER_TYPE |
+--------+--------------+---------------------+----------+-----------+
|    137 | X            | b@cc.com            | #        | ADMIN     |
|    138 | Kshitiz      | ksharma@aaa.com     | asdf     | ADMIN     |
+--------+--------------+---------------------+----------+-----------+
```

### Sensory

Ensure that instructions provided for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, color, size, visual location, or sound.

### Color

#### Color Contrast

If non-ANSI colors have been set, ensure that there is sufficient color contrast between text and background to accommodate users with visual impairments.

#### Color for Meaning

Verify that color is not the only means of conveying information. For example, cannot say "the green text means…".

Regarding linked text (namely URLs), the link functionality is created by the terminal emulator. Therefore the visual treatment is out of the CLI application author's control. Only color contrast requirements must be met.

### Keyboard

Ensure that all functionality can be accessed and operated using only the keyboard.

### Timing

#### Timing Adjustable

For each time limit that is set by the CLI, ensure that the user can turn off, adjust, or extend it.

#### Pause, Stop, Hide

Moving, blinking, or scrolling content is very much discouraged. If it exists, starts automatically, and lasts more than five seconds, there must be a mechanism for the user to pause, stop, or hide it (unless it is essential).

Example of failure: [YouTube of Terminal Animation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WvIQ95CbsTI)

### Flashes

Flashing content is very much discouraged. There must not be any flashing of more than 3 times per second that is larger than 25% or more of the screen size.

Example of failure: [YouTube of Terminal Animation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WvIQ95CbsTI)

### Headings

Ensure that text used as headings are descriptive and clear. See the [Headings CLI page](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/heading_criteria_examples.md) for further information and examples.

### Identification

Components that have the same functionality within the CLI are identified consistently.

### Error Handling

If an input error is detected:

* The item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
* Suggestions to correct the error are provided to the user, unless it would jeopardize the security or purpose of the content.

### Authentication

A cognitive function test (such as remembering a password or solving a puzzle) is not required for any step in an authentication process unless that step provides an alternative authentication method that does not rely on a cognitive function test. Reference the lesser-known WCAG success criterion [WCAG SC 3.3.8](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/accessible-authentication-minimum.html).

### Screen Reader

Test with a popular screen reader (such as JAWS, NVDA, or Voiceover) to ensure that the screen reader reads out all relevant information, including prompts, responses, and any error messages.

### Documentation Accessibility [[MAS 10.2](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/accessibility/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B6DBB1C72-86F7-4BA0-81D7-E9BF14A13522%7D&file=MAS%2010.2%20%E2%80%93%20Product%20Documentation%20Format.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true)]

If product documentation is provided, it must be accessible in an electronic format. Documentation also must be provided upon request in alternate formats (for example, Braille, audio) at no additional cost to the customer.

## What Not to Test

* Keyboard access to URL text is not expected (nor to anything else in the CLI output). Any interaction of the URL is enhanced behavior provided by the Terminal app and not the CLI.
* Images and multimedia are not included in CLI output therefore any of the related WCAG Success Criteria do not need to be checked.
* CLI is not web-based, so many WCAG Success Criteria do not apply. For example, 2.5.3 Label in Name, 3.1.2 Language of Parts, and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. Reference the [CLI-WCAG Mapping table](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/cli/cli-wcag-map.md).


## Best Practices for CLI Developers

### Color

* Do not customize colors; best to use default settings.
* Reference this engineering issue: [Epic] Core GitHub CLI Accessibility Audit [#339](https://github.com/github/cli/issues/339)

### Motion

* Do not implement flashing or animation.

### Use Linear Output

* Implement linear output.
* Avoid table layouts.
* Avoid pagination.

## Related Resources

* [Building a more accessible GitHub CLI](https://github.blog/engineering/user-experience/building-a-more-accessible-github-cli/) -- GitHub blog post, May 2025
* For Window 11: HCL follows the process as mentioned in [Contrast themes - Windows apps | Microsoft Learn](https://nam06.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Flearn.microsoft.com%2Fen-us%2Fwindows%2Fapps%2Fdesign%2Faccessibility%2Fhigh-contrast-themes&data=05%7C02%7Cv-prahu%40microsoft.com%7Cd58e189d56154d4b495108dd31940de0%7C72f988bf86f141af91ab2d7cd011db47%7C1%7C0%7C638721234160129801%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=th%2FcyzhmXNXC6WLrKPVUVNza8eF%2FN2PTLIty7CIbC54%3D&reserved=0) and [Guideline 18A - Honor High Contrast in Text, Images, and Icons.docx](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/accessibility/EQI3fwnj5QNCtS4eryD20agBeLexVr4BivY1Lhu7mdrJ3Q?e=raRPIT&%3d&sdata=M3M5QzZZcnhRc2JVSjJDY2hxVGNpcTA3cGNjZ1VPWnFqWkVTZTNrV2NmOD0%3d)
* For MacOS: HCL follows the process as mentioned in [Change Display settings for accessibility on Mac - Apple Support (IN)](https://nam06.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsupport.apple.com%2Fen-in%2Fguide%2Fmac-help%2Funac089%2Fmac&data=05%7C02%7Cv-prahu%40microsoft.com%7Cd58e189d56154d4b495108dd31940de0%7C72f988bf86f141af91ab2d7cd011db47%7C1%7C0%7C638721234160152577%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=EdckBC2UISGqUCQ8mF0DqPhzg2ejl6xxgEiQfCXcBIc%3D&reserved=0).
* [MS Guideline 104 – Command Line Tools and Scripts (Google Doc)](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/GitHubAccessibilityProgram/Shared%20Documents/Command-line-tool%20-%20Microsoft.docx) 
* [MS Guideline 104 – Command Line Tools and Scripts (PDF) ](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Vdd2RAcQSrpqinbzvNyGhlaw8XYQ0tNN/view?ts=65eb28cc)
* [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)
* [Accessible CLI colors #12147](https://github.com/github/npm/discussions/12147)
* [Primer guide for CLI](https://primer.style/native/cli/getting-started)
