documents.title: Sample Content Policy
documents.content:
# Sample Content Policy

This document explains how to handle sample content when conducting an accessibility audit.

## What is sample content?

"Sample content" is realistic but fictional content that is created as an example for users to reference in order to assist in completing tasks for specific portions of a user interface (UI). For example, a UI to write blog posts may have an example post containing a heading, image, and a paragraph; this would be considered sample content.

> [!NOTE]
> If the UI prevents a user from creating accessible content, such as not allowing alternative text for an image, then it is absolutely an issue which must be reported.

## Sample content in external properties

_Sample content in external properties must be audited._ For the purposes of this policy, external properties is defined as publicly available content that is owned by GitHub — in GA, public preview, etc.

- [Example 1 of external sample content](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/create-actions/create-a-javascript-action#creating-an-action-metadata-file) (action metadata file)
- [Example 2 of external sample content](https://www.portlandseogrowth.com/free-seo-resources/content-writing-samples/) (writing examples)

## Sample content in internal properties

_Sample content in properties for internal use only should not be audited._

- [Example 1 for internal sample content](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10449) (alt attribute)
- [Example 2 for internal sample content](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/10383) (table header text)

It's highly encouraged to still make this content accessible even if not audited because:

- It provides an accessible example for Hubbers to follow.
- It provides accessible content in general for disabled Hubbers.
- It's time-consuming and frustrating for the same accessibility issues to come up again in future audits.
- It's good professionalism and the right thing to do.

## Filler text

_Filler text does not require an HTML `lang` attribute._

Filler/dummy text (most commonly, the ["lorem ipsum" garbled Latin passage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorem_ipsum)) is sometimes used as placeholder text for content such as templates and components. Filler text does not require an HTML `lang` attribute (to comply with [WCAG 3.1.2 Language of Parts](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#language-of-parts)). 

- [Example 1 of filler text](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/13923)
- [Example 2 of filler text](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/14256)

documents.title: Severity levels - Governance
documents.content:
# Severity levels - Governance

This file defines severity levels that are used to prioritize all accessibility issues within the `github/accessibility-audits` [repo](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits), regardless of their origin (e.g. found during an internal audit, found by an internal user, or found by a customer). The severity levels are based on [guidance from Microsoft CELA](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/accessibility/EQt9laX4e1RDvBces72p70ABAbmw8w26hHf6BQCyUfPIrg?e=ier8q0&CID=02A374B4-AFD3-486C-8010-D59873E0D9A8&wdLOR=cCC9DCFA8-1AD9-4C79-B183-993807F04DD9). However, they have been adapted by GitHub CELA to meet the needs of GitHub. 

See also:
- [Definition of MAS grades](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/policy/MAS-grades.md) defines how severity levels relate to MAS grades.
- [Community feedback severity levels](severity-support.md) defines severity levels for community feedback issues that are tracked in the `github/accessibility-external` [repo](https://github.com/github/accessibility-external).

## Definitions 

### Severity 1 

Applicable label: [`Severity-1`](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/labels/Severity-1)

Severity 1 issues cause harm or block access to core functionality. There are no known workarounds. They must be fixed within 30 days.

An issue is severity 1 if any of the following conditions apply: 
- The issue causes migraines, dizziness, nausea, motion sickness, seizures, or other bodily harm or discomfort.
- The user is not able to access an entire product, site, or app. 
- The user is not able to complete a [core scenario](https://github.com/github/scenarios/blob/main/core-scenarios.md) and there is no known workaround.

### Severity 2 

Applicable label: [`Severity-2`](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/labels/Severity-2)

Severity 2 issues may block users from completing non-core scenarios or cause significant delay or frustration. They must be fixed within 60 days.

An issue is severity 2 if any of the following conditions apply: 
- The user is not able to complete a [core scenario](https://github.com/github/scenarios/blob/main/core-scenarios.md). However, there is a known workaround.
- The user is not able to complete a non-core scenario.
- The issue causes a significant delay or frustration for some users. 

### Severity 3

Applicable label: [`Severity-3`](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/labels/Severity-3)

Severity 3 issues have low impact on the user. They should be fixed as soon as possible.

An issue is severity 3 if any of the following conditions apply: 
- The issue fails to meet one or more success criteria, but the conditions for severity 1 and severity 2 were not met.

### Severity 4 

Applicable label: [`Severity-4`](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/labels/Severity-4)

Severity 4 issues are usability Issues and do not fail any MAS or WCAG success criteria. However, the end-user experience is not efficient or delightful. They should be prioritized as "best effort".

An issue is severity 4 if any of the following conditions apply: 
- The issue does not cause a failure for success criteria, but the user experience is not efficient or delightful.
- The issue describes a feature request that could improve accessibility or usability.

## Guidance

The definitions of the severity levels were written to be as objective as possible. However, some subjective judgement is required. This section provides guidance for making those subjective decisions.

### Severities are relative to scenarios 

We use severities to prioritize issues based on their impact to users as they work to complete a scenario. As a result, a particular bug could be the root causes of multiple issues and those issues could be prioritized as severity 1, 2, or 3, depending on the scenario in which they were found. Use the conditions defined for each severity (above) to determine the appropriate severity for each issue within the context of the corresponding scenario.

### Consider all four principles of WCAG when setting severity

The definitions of severities include phrases such as, "complete a core scenario." When setting severity, remember that the term "complete" includes all four principles of WCAG.

In order to complete a scenario, users must first perceive and understand the content of the user interface including the purpose of controls and how they may be used to change the state of the application. This perception and understanding is required to determine if the information and controls within the user interface are relevant to the scenario to be performed. Some users use assistive technology. So, the content and controls must be robust and inter-operate with assistive technologies to support the act of perceiving and understanding. Users must be able to operate the controls that are required to complete the scenario. After each operation, users must be able to perceive and understand the results of the operation until the scenario is complete. Finally, users must be able to perceive and understand that the scenario has indeed been completed.

In summary, the act of completing a scenario includes many acts of perceiving, understanding, and operating. Those individual acts may be performed using assistive technology. A bug that blocks any one of those individual acts could block the entire scenario.

documents.title: Reporting Issues to External Sources
documents.content: # Reporting Issues to External Sources > [!IMPORTANT] > Always check for and remove PII (e.g., usernames, company names, people's actual names, etc.) before sharing issue information. With some services, you have to send issue information to external parties to get them remediated. This could be because the issue is a third-party issue (e.g., YouTube embedded player, Apple login, Captcha, etc.), a SaaS solution (e.g., Lumos, Zendesk, Port, etc.), or a GitHub-owned site that is partially built and/or maintained by an external vendor (e.g., GitHub Universe site). In these instances, you run into a conundrum. Currently, there isn't a native solution for exporting issues in GitHub's UI, and repo/issue access cannot be granted to non-GitHub org users. That is where this document hopes to help. This document describes a few of the common methods that have been used to share issue information. Use the information here to identify if one of these solutions will work for your situation. > [!NOTE] > Any references to how to perform functions in a content creation program will be geared towards Microsoft programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) when available. Many of these functions may be available in other non-Microsoft applications, but use different terms. You will need to refer to your selected application's support documentation in these circumstances. Additionally, the [Resources section](#resources) of this document provides links to resources that may help you with formatting issue information in an accessible manner based on what format you elect to use. ## Manual copy The most basic option is to manually copy the information from the issue body to a word document, spreadsheet, or other format. This could be tedious for a large number of issues, but may be quicker if you just have a few issues to share. There are a few considerations to have depending on what format you select. ### Spreadsheet When making a spreadsheet of issues: - input the issue information in tabular format - ensure you have descriptive column headers - In Microsoft Excel, highlight your table, including the headers, and use the "Format as Table" option. - This will ensure the content is treated as a table, allowing for sorting and better accessibility options. - Make sure to check the "My table has headers" option if you have added your column headers already. - If you haven't added column headers, it is recommended that you add them before using this function of Excel because it can make formatting easier overall. Some issues you may run into with this option include: - You can only insert one image into a cell. - Adding alt text to images is a bit complicated. - You cannot insert videos into spreadsheets (See [Sharing videos](#sharing-videos)) - Excel doesn't allow you to have links in the middle of a cell's content. - You can add a link to a cell but the entirety of the cell's content is linked rather than just a couple of words in a cell being linked and the rest being plain text. - Additionally, this means you cannot have more than one link per cell. - As a result, if you want more than one URL in a cell, you have to split the links out into multiple cells, or just have the URL as plain text rather than linked text. #### Excel tips The following tips will help with editing a spreadsheet of issues. ##### Copying a lists from an issue without losing formatting If you copy a list from a GitHub issue while it is in its rendered view, you will lose the list formatting. If you instead, open the issue body in edit mode and copy the list from there, the markdown formatting used to define it as a list will be kept. This is important because Excel does not allow you to format text as a list in cell content. If Excel wants to try to change the cell content into a formula, press return after pasting in the content rather than clicking outside the cell. This should avoid that. Alternatively, swap out the dashes (`-`) used in the list formatting for asterisks (`*`). ##### Insert a line break If you paste content into a cell and need to add a line break, you can: 1. double-click to enter the cell. 2. move your cursor to where you want to insert a line break. 3. Use the appropriate keyboard shortcut to insert a line break in the cell: - **macOS**: option + return - **Windows**: alt + return ##### Add image to a cell Since Microsoft Excel now allows you to insert images into cells, you can now insert them into a table in Excel so they are properly associated with their related issue information. This is accomplished by: 1. Select the cell you want to insert the image into. 2. Navigate to the top navigation bar of Excel and click the "Insert" tab. 3. Click the "Insert picture" button to open a context menu. 4. Select "Place in cell" and then "Photo Browser" from the menu to open a window where you can locate the image on your system. 5. Click the "Insert" button once you have selected the image. Please note that you can only add one image per cell, and you cannot insert other content in the cell with the image. So, if you have more than one image, you may need to add columns to your table. You will also want to make sure you add alt text to the image. ##### Add alt text to an image To add alt text to the images in Excel: 1. Select the image and a "Place over Cells" button should appear. 2. Click that button. The image will temporarily be over the cell rather than in it. 3. Right-click the image and select "View Alt Text..." from the context menu. 4. An "Alt Text" pane should appear. Enter your Alt text there and it should automatically be added to the image after you remove focus from that pane. 5. Go back to the image and select the button that now says "Place in Cell" and it should return to the cell. ## Print to PDF You can print/save each issue to a PDF file. Just highlight the content of the main issue body and select the "print to PDF" using the built in print options. It is recommended that you highlight from the title of the issue to the end of the acceptance criteria, and then select the "Print selection" and "Background Images" options, if available, to limit the size of the file while helping to keep the relevant content readable. The biggest issue with this method is that you will need to download and separately provide video files (See [Sharing videos](#sharing-videos)). You may also need to separately download images if they are compressed in a way that makes some details unclear. ### PDF/UA Some applications give you the option to print / save to PDF using PDF/UA compliance. This means the application will use the programmatic layout of the content to try to tag the PDF in a way that makes it more accessible to assistive technology. It is typically not as good as manual tagging of a PDF, but can be sufficient in some instances. ## HCL Spreadsheet HCL can provide their own spreadsheet of the issue information. This will be in a set format that HCL uses and further customization will need to be done by the service team needing to share the issue information. Images and videos will need to be separately downloaded and provided if needed. ## GitHub CLI / API The [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue) or [GitHub API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest) can be used to pull the information about the issues. However, use of either of these methods requires the user to have enough knowledge to customize the CLI commands or write code to use them. Additionally, you will most likely need to manually download images and videos (See [Sharing videos](#sharing-videos)) when using either of these methods. The readability of these solutions may be questionable because of the formats they are exported into. For example, GitHub CLI exports to JSON by default, which removes some of the formatting that can help make issue information more readable. ## Issue Exporter An [issue exporter](https://corgidev.github.io/GitHub-Issue-Exporter/) was built by Corgidev that allows users to export issues to a set of HTML files that can be viewed offline, navigated like a website by clicking on the `index.html` file, and look similar to how they look like when viewed on GitHub. You still have to download the images, but can add them to the individual issue HTML files. You will need a GitHub personal access token (PAT) token with read access to Issues in the `github/accessibility-audits` repo to export that information. One issue with this tool is that it is open to being edited or removed at any time since it is controlled by an individual GitHub user. So, it may become unusable or these instructions may not be up to date in the future. To use this tool: 1. Input the PAT, the repo owner (github), and repo name (accessibility-audits) in the first few inputs on the page. 2. Scroll down and click "Load Repo Labels". 3. Select the labels you want to filter by. 1. Typically you will probably want to select the `service:` label for your service under "Include Labels - ALL", and then select `Severity-1` and `Severity-2` from under "Include Labels - ANY". 4. Scroll down and click "Search Issues". 5. Once the issue results load, click "Export Results as Offline HTML". 1. It will say that it is downloading media, but currently it fails to due to [CORS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS) restrictions. 6. At this point, you can either: 1. send the zip file as-is to the external party, OR 2. extract the folder so you can edit the files to add the linked images and videos before sending the files to the external party. ### Adding media files to the exported html files You can choose whether you want to add the media files now, or wait to see if the external party needs them for context. If you elect to add the linked media to the files: 1. Extract the zip file and open the parent folder created. 1. Inside there should be an "assets" folder where you can add all the media files, an `index.html` which serves as the main page of the files and contains a list of all the exported issues, and an individual HTML file for each issue exported that has just that issue's details. 2. Open the GitHub.com version of each issue. 3. Download the images and videos from the issue into the "assets" folder within the extracted parent folder. 1. It is recommended that you name them similar to what is described in the [Sharing videos](#sharing-videos) section of this doc; as that will make the next section easier. 4. Open the extracted folder in VS Code. 5. Each issue's HTML file will have a placeholder snippet placed where each media file would have have been. Replace that placeholder with an `img` or `video` element (See [Issue Exporter code snippets](#issue-exporter-code-snippets)) as needed. 1. If you use the code snippets, they should already have filepaths formatted as needed for the default file structure. 2. As a result, all you should have to do is replace `fileName` with the name you gave the relevant file in the "assets" folder, and add a value to the `alt` attribute to any `img` elements you add. 6. Once done, close out VS Code and then zip the parent folder that contains all the issue files and the "assets" folder. 7. Share that zip folder with the external party that will remediate them. ### Issue Exporter code snippets ```html ``` ```html ``` ## Sharing videos When you need to share videos, it is recommended that you: 1. Download the videos from the issues. 2. Name them based on the issue number (e.g., `16823.mp4`). 1. If an issue has more than one video file, you can just add some form of suffix to the file name (e.g., `16823a.mp4`, `16823b.mp4`). 3. What you do next depends on what you are wanting to do. Some options include: 1. Add them to a document that you are planning to share. 2. Add all the files to a single zip file that can be shared. 4. Then upload the files to a location shared with the external party so they can access them. ## Resources - [Create accessible Office documents | Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Office/create-accessible-office-documents) - Official Microsoft Support documents for creating accessible files in Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and more. - [Create Accessible Digital Content | Section 508](https://www.section508.gov/create/) - Section 508 documentation on creating accessible versions of various document types, including: PDFs, spreadsheets, presentations, word documents, and much more. - [GitHub API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest) - [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue) - [`accessibility-audits` repo issues](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues/)

documents.title: Stale Issues
documents.content:
# Stale Issues

## Definition

A stale accessibility issue must meet one of the following credentials:

- The issue is over one year old.
- A completely different UI replaced the previous UI that was audited. The new experience must be in GA.
- The issue was resolved because the pertinent UI element/feature was removed.
- The issue was resolved by a component.
- The issue is a duplicate.
- Other extenuating circumstances.

## Overview

A stale accessibility issue should be labeled `stale-validation`. The label will trigger the testing vendor to review the issue. If the issue is indeed resolved, the issue can be closed by anyone on the central accessibility team. For bulk processing, the feature team should complete a stale review request form, see below.

## Skip Stale Validation

The `skip-stale-validation` label is used to identify issues exempt from stale validation.

## Workflow for requesting stale issue validation

This workflow is for when 3-25 issues in an audit are identified as potentially stale. If there are more than 25, please consult with CELA Accessibility. If less than 3 issues, add the `stale-validation` label to each issue.

CELA Accessibility serves as the DRI.

1. The feature team files a [stale audit review request form](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues/new?template=accessibility-audit-stale-review.yml).
1. The DRI adds the `stale-validation` label to the issues.
1. Automation connected to the label pings the testing vendor (via a comment by accessibility-bot-app).
1. Testing vendor determines if each issue is reproducible or not.
1. For each issue that's not reproducible:
   - The testing vendor comments and tags the First Responder (FR) (@github/accessibility-reviewers).
   - The testing vendor removes the `stale-validation` label.
   - The FR closes the issue ("Close as not planned").
1. For each issue that's reproducible:
    - The testing vendor comments and tags the feature owner.
    - The testing vendor removes the `stale-validation` label.
1. After all issues in the stale request form are addressed, the DRI closes the request issue.

## Year Action Disabled

The `stale-validation-one-year` automated workflow has been disabled. Issues over a year old will be manually tagged by the stale issue DRI.

History: In the `accessibility-audits` repo, any audit issues open for over a year automatically have the `stale-validation` label applied via [a GitHub Action modifying the existing reusable `actions/stale` workflow](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/blob/main/.github/workflows/stale-validation-one-year.yml); this will kick off the review process. One problem that occurred was that after an issue was labeled stale, determined to be reproducible, and the label was removed manually, the label was then automatically re-added.

## Monthly stale validation

The monthly stale validation should be done during the first week of each month. Issues over a year old will be evaluated.

### Work tracking issues

For easier tracking of validation tasks, it is recommended that you create issues for them under a yearly "Epic" issue containing links to all the monthly and annual `stale-validation` tasks for that year. This can be a useful way to identify issues you want to follow up on, metrics, and being able to have the filter URLs prepared ahead of time. You can view example templates for each kind of issue in the [Issue Templates section](#issue-templates) of this document.

### Monthly review process

1. Search for all Severity 1, 2, and 3 issues made in that month the previous year.
   1. Use the following query to filter for relevant issues — remember to edit the date range: [is:open created:2023-12-01..2023-12-31 sort:created-desc label:Severity-1,Severity-2,Severity-3 -label:stale-validation](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues?q=is%3Aopen+created%3A2023-12-01..2023-12-31+sort%3Acreated-desc+label%3ASeverity-1%2CSeverity-2%2CSeverity-3+-label%3Astale-validation)
      1. The date range should have the first day of the month and then the last day of the month (**i.e.,** January 1st to January 31st, 2023 would be `2023-01-01..2023-01-31`).
2. Check the issue comments to see whether they are still valid. In the event that they:
   1. are being actively validated by testers or remediated within the past year, skip to next issue.
   2. have had no update in the past year, add the `stale-validation` label.
      1. This will kick off automation to notify the testers to verify the issue as stale or not.
      2. If this issue has an `sla-extension`, add the following comment:
         > Marking this issue with the `stale-validation` label to verify whether it is still valid. This does not impact the current SLA exception.
   3. were confirmed resolved but not closed, tag the `@github/accessibility-reviewers` group and request that the fix be verified.
      - That group will make the call on whether the issue is fixed and can be closed, or is still a valid issue.
      - If `@github/accessibility-reviewers` were already tagged, but it has been more than a month, tag them again and request an update in case the issue was missed.

## Annual stale issue reviews

In addition to the monthly reviews to identify recently stale issues, there are also 2 broader annual reviews.

1. In January, we review issues that already have the `stale-validation` label to ensure they are being reviewed in a timely manner by testers, devs, or other reviewers.
2. In December, we do a deep dive review to cleanup the issue queue further by reviewing issues older than 2 years.

### Previously labeled stale issue review

An additional review should be done in January that covers all issues that have the `stale-validation` label.

1. Search for issues that have the `stale-validation` label using the following filter: [`is:open is:issue label:stale-validation`](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Astale-validation)
2. Check the issue comments to see whether they are still valid. In the event that they:
   1. `stale-validation` label added during January stale review, skip to next issue.
   2. are being actively remediated / discussed, with activity within the last 12 months, remove the `stale-validation` label.
   3. have had no update in the past year, remove `stale-validation` and readd it. This should ping the necessary parties.
   4. were confirmed resolved but not closed, remove `stale-validation` label and tag the `@github/accessibility-reviewers` group to request review.
      - If `@github/accessibility-reviewers` were tagged previously, but there was no response, tag them again and request an update.

### Deep dive stale issue review

An annual review of issues that are older than 2 years be completed every December using the following filters: [`is:open sort:created-desc label:Severity-1,Severity-2,Severity-3 created:<2024-01-01 -label:stale-validation`](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues?q=is%3Aopen+created%3A%3C2024-01-01+sort%3Acreated-desc+label%3ASeverity-1%2CSeverity-2%2CSeverity-3+-label%3Astale-validation).

The year of the created date in the query/filter should be updated to the year before last. This allows us to review all issues, not already labeled as stale, that did not get reviewed or created during the previous year due to being older than 2 years old at the start of the current year.

For example, 2025's monthly reviews would have checked all potentially stale issues created in 2024. 2026's monthly reviews would end up reviewing all issues opened during 2025. So, the 2026 Deep Dive would cover issues created during 2023 or older.

## Issue Templates

<details>
    <summary>Calendar Year Epic Issue</summary>

   - **Recommended issue title**: `YYYY - Stale Issue Validation`
   - **Edits needed before starting**: Add the calendar year to the title, and edit the URL that links to last year's epic issue.
      - Attach all the other stale validation related tasks to this issue as sub-issues.

   ```md
    This is the parent epic issue used to track the stale verification related work. It consists of 2 annual reviews, 12 monthly reviews, and potentially other tasks related to the stale issue validation process. Make sure you set this issue's type to "Epic".
    
    The annual reviews include:

    - January annual review of all issues that already have the `stale-validation` label.
       - Perform this before you do the regularly monthly review in January so you are not being unnecessarily redundant.
    - December annual review of any issues older than 2 years old.
       - For example, the January 2026 annual stale review would include issues created December 31, 2023 or older by filtering for issues older than January 1, 2024.
    
    The monthly reviews cover the issues made during the relevant month during the previous year. For example, the January 2026 monthly review would include issues created in January of 2025. Other stale validation related tasks can also be attached to this epic as seen fit.

    For more details, review the [Stale Validation Process doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/stale-issues.md).
    
    **Last Year's Epic**: https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/issues/NUMBER
    
   ```

</details>

<details>
    <summary>January review of issues currently labeled stale</summary>

   - **Recommended issue title**: `YYYY - Review of Currently Labeled Stale Issues
   - **Query edits needed before starting**: None

```md

> [!NOTE]
> Do this during the month of January by following the ["Previously labeled stale issue review" section of the Stale Validation process](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/stale-issues.md#previously-labeled-stale-issue-review). Do this before you perform the monthly review for the month of January.

## Overview

This task involves reviewing issues that were already labeled with the `stale-validation` label to verify whether they have recent activity that would indicate they have been recently verified or are actively being worked on by service owners.

### Action Items

- [ ] Review issues that already have the `stale-validation` label using the following filter: [`is:open is:issue label:stale-validation](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Astale-validation)
- [ ] Remove the `stale-validation` label if the issue was reviewed and the label just did not get removed.
- [ ] Tag `@github/accessibility-reviewers` if necessary so they know the issue still needs to be checked.
   - Can also add to any weekly meeting you have with the testing managers to bring them to their attention.

### Issue Review Summary

- `00` Total issues reviewed
- `00` / `00` (`00%`) issues re-tagged with the `stale-validation` label
- `00` / `00` (`00%`) issues tagged for review by `@github/accessibility-reviewers`
- `00` / `00` (`00%`) issues where `stale-validation` label was removed
```

</details>

<details>
    <summary>Monthly Stale Review</summary>

   - **Recommended issue title**: `<MonthName> YYYY Stale Validation`
   - **Query edits needed before starting**: Update the month name and year in the title, update the dates in the `[!NOTE]` section and the query to the first and last day of the relevant month the previous year,
      - An easy mistake to make is using the incorrect dates. Particularly for the month of February. Remember that the dates are meant to be for the previous year. The query will fail or provide incorrect results if you enter the incorrect dates.
      - The query uses the `YYYY-MM-DD` date format.

   ```md
    > [!NOTE]
    > Do this on the first/second week of the month by following the ["Monthly reviews" section of the Stale Validation process](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/stale-issues.md#monthly-reviews). If this is being done for the month of January, you want to do this AFTER you complete the review of previously labeled stale issues.
    
    ## Overview
    
    This task involves reviewing issues that were created during the relevant month the previous year to verify whether there is recent activity that would indicate they have been recently verified or are actively being worked on by service owners.
    
    ### Action Items
    
    - [ ] Review issues created between [January 01st through January 31st, 2025](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues?q=is%3Aopen+created%3A2025-01-01..2025-01-31+sort%3Acreated-desc+label%3ASeverity-1%2CSeverity-2%2CSeverity-3+-label%3Astale-validation).
    - [ ] Add the `stale-validation` label as needed.
    - [ ] Add additional issues to check from last verification if needed.
    
    ### Issue Review Summary
    
    - `00` Total issues reviewed
      - `00` / `00` (`00`) issues tagged as `stale-validation`
      - `00` / `00` (`00%`) issues verified
    
   ```

</details>
    
<details>
    <summary>December review of issues older than 2 years</summary>

   - **Recommended issue title**: `YYYY - End of Year stale-validation Deep Dive`
   - **Query edits needed before starting**: Update the year in the issue title to the current year and update the year in the query to be the beginning of year before last year (e.g., if it is the 2026 End of year review, you would set the year to 2024).

   ```md
    > [!NOTE]
    > Do this during the month of December by following the ["Deep dive stale issue review" section of the Manual Stale Validation process](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/stale-issues.md#deep-dive-stale-issue-review).

    ## Overview
    
    This task serves as an additional issue cleanup. By reviewing issues older than one year to verify whether there is recent activity that would indicate they have been recently verified or are actively being worked on by service owners.
    
    ### Action Items
    
    - [ ] Review severity 1 - 3 issues that are older than 2 years using the following filters: [`is:open created:<2024-01-01 sort:created-desc label:Severity-1,Severity-2,Severity-3`](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/issues?q=is%3Aopen%20created%3A%3C2024-01-01%20sort%3Acreated-desc%20label%3ASeverity-1%2CSeverity-2%2CSeverity-3)
    - [ ] Add the `stale-validation` label if deemed necessary.
    
    ### Issue Review Summary
    
    - `##` Total issues reviewed
      - `##` / `##` (`##%`) issues tagged as `stale-validation`
      - `##` / `##` (`##%`) issues verified
    
   ```

</details>

## Related Resources

- [Issues with `stale-validation` label](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/labels/stale-validation)

documents.title: Triage (Refinement) Process
documents.content:
# Triage (Refinement) Process

## Preliminary Process

After an audit has been completed, a refining request issue is created that includes Severity 1 and Severity 2 bugs reported. If there are zero Sev 1 / Sev 2 issues identified, skip to the [Handoff process](handoff-process.md).

Audits that are ready for triage/refinement are listed in the [Step 6. Ready for triage](https://github.com/orgs/github/projects/5332/views/6) panel in the Accessibility WCAG Audit Testing Schedule.

The refiner is responsible for prioritizing refinement requests, assigning coaches and champions as needed, performing triage, and ensuring the triage is completed on time (see Scheduling below).

## Prioritizing Refining Requests

The priority of audits will be determined by considering multiple factors, the most important of which are:

- Strategic service
- MAS grade expiration
- Age (how long has the audit been waiting for refinement)
- Priority labels (which are already added to audit requests)

## Assigning

Reference [Staffing the refinement procedure for accessibility audits](/planning/staffing-refinement-procedure.md) for the assigning of refining tasks during April 2024 through January 2025.

## Scheduling

The completion of refining requests should be:

- 1 week or under for strategic services
- 2 weeks or under for non-strategic services

## Checkpoints

### Ensure general quality

- Ensure the issue description is accurate and sufficient—particularly the actual/expected results, steps to reproduce, and attachments.
  - Create a comment to request updates. Tag the reporter and CELA Accessibility DRI.
  - Please direct any questions to the central accessibility team via an [Accessibility Office Hour](https://github.com/github/accessibility/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aa11y-eng-office-hours%2Ca11y-design-oh+) or an [accessibility Slack channel](https://github-grid.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0FSWLQ0Y).
- Cross reference any related issues within the same audit; add a link to the related issue(s) under the Acceptance Criteria.
- For duplicate issues, not reproducible issues, and false positives, see the Label Management section below.
- If you're concerned about what was reported for screen reader behavior, please contact an internal screen reader specialist (currently Florian Beijers @zersiax).

### Label management

#### Bug issue labels

- Ensure a proper accessibility role of either [Aware, Partner, or Coach](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/docs/three-roles.md) is assigned via the following labels: `a11y role: aware`, `a11y role: partner`, `a11y role: coach`. Any issue marked "partner" or "coach" must be closed by a member of the accessibility team.
- Ensure a _service_ label and _project_ label are assigned and are correct.
- Ensure the [severity level](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audits/labels?q=severity) is correct. If incorrect, adjust and add a comment.
- For any issues discovered via axe, ensure the label `type:axe` is applied.
- Ensure the cited WCAG success criterion is correct. If incorrect, add a comment and add the label `flag-hcl`.
  - In the comment, tag the tester who created the issue and tag the testing manager (currently v-prahu of HCL).
- When providing general feedback for HCL, add the label `feedback-hcl`.
  - In the comment, tag the tester who created the issue and tag the testing manager (currently v-prahu of HCL).
- Duplicate issues:
  - Add the label `duplicate`.
  - Comment with a link to the duplicate issue(s).
  - Close the issue (Close as not planned).
- Not reproducible issues:
  - Add the label `not-replicable`.
  - Add a comment explaining that it is not reproducible.
  - Close the issue (Close as not planned).
- False positives:
  - Add a comment explaining why it is a false positive.
  - Add the labels `not-an-issue` and `flag-hcl`.
  - Close the issue (Close as not planned).
- For any Primer related issues:
  - Add the `service:primer` label.
  - Add a `component: x` label. For example, if the Primer component is a dialog, add the label `component: Dialog`.
- If an issue is blocked by another service (such as a Primer component, see above), it is unfair to give a negative score to the issue owners. To account for this, ensure the following is done.
  - Add the `supersedesScore` label.
  - [Add the issue to the Accessibility Scorecard board](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/docs/how-we-label.md#the-supersedes-score-label).
    - In the `Which team owns this issue?` field, enter the other service team.
  - Add the other service's service label to the audit issue, for example `service:primer`
  - Add a component project label, if applicable, for example `component: Pagination`
  - Related: [Third Party Issues](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/policy-third-party-ally-issues.md)

#### Audit request issue labels

- Ensure the correct _service_ and _project_ labels are applied.
- Ensure an _audit-scope_ label is assigned and is correct: `audit-scope:project` OR `audit-scope:feature`
- Ensure an _audit-type_ label is assigned
   - For project audits: `audit-type:initial`, `audit-type:re-audit`, or `audit-type:fast-pass`
   - For feature audits: `audit-type:feature`
   - For audits prior to July 2024: `audit-type:legacy`
- Ensure a label `strategic` or `non-strategic` is assigned accordingly.

For more information on labels, reference [How we label issues](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/docs/how-we-label.md).

### Provide Acceptance Criteria

- Add acceptance criteria which provides guidance for fixing the bug. This should include the applicable WCAG SC and Techniques from the [WCAG Helper](wcag-helper.md).
  - UPDATE: Testing vendors are now doing this step but must be checked for accuracy.
- If needed, add specific remediation recommendations.
- Attempting to reproduce the bug is optional.

### Complete each issue

In the Refining Request ticket, under the Breakdown of Work heading, tick the box after refining each bug ticket.

### Missed issues

If missed issues are discovered during refining, the triager comments on the associated Refining Request ticket and tags the tester and the CELA Accessibility DRI.

When a bug ticket is added in the refinement stage for a missed issue:

- Testing vendor must add it to the checklist in the Refining Request (if Severity 1 or 2).
- Testing vendor must add it to the [audit project board](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/instructions-for-auditors.md#project-board).

## Related Resources

- [Audit process overview](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/FAQs.md#how-does-the-process-work)
- [Accessibility audit triage process](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/docs/how-we-audit.md)
- [MAS Grade Audit Process](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/process.md)
- [Accessibility Testing Instructions for Auditors](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/audit/instructions-for-auditors.md)
- [The Three Roles of Accessibility Work at GitHub](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/docs/three-roles.md)

documents.title: WCAG 2.2 Auditing and Resources
documents.content:
# WCAG 2.2 Auditing and Resources

## Overview

In order to better accommodate the needs of our users, and to continue to comply with Microsoft Accessibility Standards ([MAS](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/SitePages/Microsoft-Accessibility-Standards-(MAS).aspx)), GitHub accessibility audits will begin measuring against WCAG 2.2 this fall. Microsoft has recently begun testing against WCAG 2.2.

 More information on the transition can be found in the [Preparing for WCAG 2.2 Auditing announcement](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/discussions/1750).

 The following document is meant to provide valuable information and resources related to the changes introduced in WCAG 2.2 as it applies to accessibility audits.

### What stayed from 2.1?

For the most part, all WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 guidelines and success criterion remain. The only exception is [4.1.1 Parsing](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/parsing), which has been determined to be obsolete and thus has been removed.

This is in large part because assistive technologies no longer need to directly parse the markup, and can rely more on the browser instead. As a result, many of the problems 4.1.1 addressed are no longer valid or are addressed better by other success criterion.

#### What is brand new to 2.2?

WCAG 2.2 adds a total of 9 new success criterion of varying [conformance levels (A / AA / AAA)](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#cc1):

* 2.4.1 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA)
* 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced) (AAA)
* 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA)
* 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA)
* 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA)
* 3.2.6 Consistent Help (A)
* 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A)
* 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA)
* 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced) (AAA)

## The new success criterion

This section introduces the 6 new WCAG 2.2 success criterion that are applicable to our accessibility audits due to being conformance level A or AA.

### 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA)

* **Summary**: Ensure when an item gets keyboard focus, it is at least partially visible to help visual keyboard users can navigate the page and identify current keyboard focus.
* [2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) Interpretation Doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/web/WCAG/2.4.11%20Focus%20Not%20Obscured%20(Minimum).md)
* [2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA) Informational Video](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/:v:/s/accessibility/ERI1CNQBkJhOrN4P3eHfJjABKPbJQucooILkjPkJ-11H0Q)

### 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA)

* **Summary**: For any action that involves dragging, provide a simple pointer alternative so it can be performed by keyboard-only users.
* [2.5.7 Dragging Movements Interpretation Doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/web/WCAG/2.5.7%20Dragging%20Movements.md)
* [2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA) Informational Video](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/_layouts/15/stream.aspx?id=/sites/accessibility/Shared%20Documents/WCAG%202.2%20support/2.5.7%20Dragging%20Movements%20%28AA%29.mp4&referrer=StreamWebApp.Web&referrerScenario=AddressBarCopied.view)

### 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA)

* **Summary**: The size/spacing of interactive content is such that there is sufficient size and/or spacing to limit the risk of activating the incorrect content.
* [2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) Interpretation Doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/web/WCAG/2.5.8%20Target%20Size%20(Minimum).md)
* [2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA) Informational Video](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/sites/accessibility/_layouts/15/stream.aspx?id=/sites/accessibility/Shared%20Documents/WCAG%202.2%20support/2.5.8%20Target%20Size%20%28Minimum%29%20%28AA%29.mp4&referrer=StreamWebApp.Web&referrerScenario=AddressBarCopied.view)

### 3.2.6 Consistent Help (A)

* **Summary**: Put help in the same place when it is on multiple pages so people can more easily locate it.
* [3.2.6 Consistent Help Interpretation Doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/web/WCAG/3.2.6%20Consistent%20Help.md)
* [3.2.6 Consistent Help (A) Informational Video](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/:v:/s/accessibility/EZ-hZRQUkihFuacm0bxrPTsBUpfej9vJApCkcFxMtbqNSg)

### 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A)

* **Summary**: Don't ask for the same information twice in the same session unless doing so is [essential](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-essential), required for security, or the previously entered information is no longer valid.
* [3.3.7 Redundant Entry Interpretation Doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/web/WCAG/3.3.7%20Redundant%20Entry.md)
* [3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A) Informational Video](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/:v:/s/accessibility/ERJkFriVWsZMvu8Z8uINK0cBQ1RJqNTD0AXQYxjfiTZu-g)

### 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA)

* **Summary**: A cognitive function test (i.e., remembering a password, CAPTCHA) is not required for the authentication process unless it provides sufficient alternatives or assistance.
* [3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) Interpretation Doc](https://github.com/github/accessibility-audit-guide/blob/main/web/WCAG/3.3.8%20Accessible%20Authentication%20(Minimum).md)
* [3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA) Informational Video](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/:v:/s/accessibility/EUiRsuvy_DBKpQv2rGJU2BIBqQwb9n6PV8I8OUS_nJQVNA)

## Additional resources

* [WCAG 2.2 training slides by HCL](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/GitHubAccessibilityProgram/Shared%20Documents/Audits-%20User-Scenarios/What%E2%80%99s%20New%20in%20WCAG2.2.pptx), Oct. 2024
* Microsoft Content
  * [What’s New in WCAG 2.2 (PowerPoint)](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/:p:/s/accessibility/EaP-UMvKgp1NkGliMUseAW4Baht72YVvBhk1XuC73TJlQw)
  * [MAS Liquid Collection](https://liquid.microsoft.com/Web/Views/View/760511)
* [What's New in WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/new-in-22/)
* [What's new in WCAG 2.2 (Tetralogical)](https://tetralogical.com/blog/2023/10/05/whats-new-wcag-2.2/)
* [New Success Criteria in WCAG 2.2 (TPGi)](https://www.tpgi.com/new-success-criteria-in-wcag22/)
* [What's new in WCAG 2.2? (Hidde de Vries)](https://hidde.blog/new-in-wcag22/)
* [WCAG 2.2 Map (Intopia)](https://intopia.digital/articles/intopia-launches-wcag-2-2-map/)
* [Does WCAG 2.2 apply to native apps? (Tetralogical)](https://tetralogical.com/blog/2024/07/18/WCAG2ICT/)

## Need more help?

If you need more help remediating an accessibility issue there are a plethora of resources available:

* You can tag `@github/accessibility-reviewers` or `@github/accessibility-design` for engineering or design-focused attention.
* Ask a question in the [#accessibility](https://github-grid.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0FSWLQ0Y) Slack.
* Join an [Accessibility Office Hours session](https://thehub.github.com/news/2024-09-03-consolidated-accessibility-design-and-engineering-office-hours/).
* Sign up for an [Accessibility Design pairing session](https://github.com/github/accessibility/blob/main/accessibility-design/a11y-design-pairing.md).

For questions about the move to WCAG 2.2. audits, or about the accessibility audit program, please contact a member of [accessibility-audit-reviewers](https://github.com/orgs/github/teams/accessibility-audit-reviewers) group via Slack, email, or by tagging them on an audit / issue.

documents.title: WCAG Helper
documents.content:
# WCAG Helper

- The following is sample text for use in the Acceptance Criteria section of the bug issues during audit refining.
- The scope is WCAG 2.2 A/AA.
- The default [accessibility role](https://github.com/github/accessibility-governance/blob/main/docs/audits/triage-process.md#label-management) is also listed; the role can be modified per issue as deemed by the triager.

## WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion

### 1.1.1 Non-text Content

Default role: Aware

```md
- All non-text content that is presented to the user has an appropriate descriptive text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.1.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html#techniques)
   - [Understanding "Text Alternatives"](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/conformance#text-alternatives)
   - [Alternative text for images | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/alternative-text-for-images/)
```

#### Decorative content with alternative text

```md
- All non-text content that is [purely decorative](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-pure-decoration), is used only for visual formatting, or is not presented to users, is implemented in a way that allows it to be ignored by assistive technology.
- Some examples include the use of: `role="presentation"`, `alt=""`, `alt`, or `aria-hidden="true"`.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.1.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html#techniques)
   - [WCAG Decorative Images tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/decorative/)
   - [Alternative text for images | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/alternative-text-for-images/)
```

### 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)

Default role: Aware

```md
- All prerecorded audio-only and video-only media has a sufficient alternative that presents equivalent information.
- For example, captioning or a text transcript of audio-only, or an audio / text description of video only content.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.2.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded.html#techniques)
```

### 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded)

Default role: Aware

```md
- Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media, except when the media is a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.2.2 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded.html#techniques)
```

### 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)

Default role: Partner

```md
- An alternative for time-based media or audio description of the prerecorded video content is provided for synchronized media, except when the media is a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.2.3 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded.html#techniques)
   - [Technique G69: Providing an alternative for time based media](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/general/G69)
   - [Description of Visual Information](https://www.w3.org/WAI/media/av/description/)
```

> [!NOTE]
> This SC is level A; issues should most likely be reported under 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) which is AA.

### 1.2.4 Captions (Live)

Default role: Aware

```md
- Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronized media.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.2.4 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live.html#techniques)
```

### 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded)

Default role: Partner

```md
- Audio descriptions are provided for all prerecorded video content in synchronized media.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [Description of Visual Information](https://www.w3.org/WAI/media/av/description/)
   - [1.2.5 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-prerecorded.html#techniques)
```

### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships

Default role: Aware

```md
- Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Content Structure](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/content/)
   - [Semantic HTML and ARIA | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/semantic-html-and-aria/)
```

#### Additional descriptive information not announced

```md
- Additional descriptive information for a control, input, or link is being correctly announced by a screen reader.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Labeling Controls | W3C Forms Tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/)
   - [Grouping Controls | W3C Forms Tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/)
```

#### Unique landmarks

```md
- Landmarks have unique labeling through appropriate methods.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Landmark Regions | APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/)
   - [Using `aria-labelledby` to name regions and landmarks](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA13)
```

#### Headings - level order

```md
- The order of the headings properly reflect the visual presentation required via heading tags (`h1` - `h6`) and CSS styles.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Headings | Page Structure Tutorial | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/headings/)
   - [Headings | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/headings/)
```

#### Headings - missing H1

```md
- An `<h1>` element that represents the overall page content has been added, and appropriate CSS styles have been applied to the heading as needed to reflect its place within the page structure.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Headings | Page Structure Tutorial | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/headings/)
   - [Headings | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/headings/)
```

#### Headings - missing semantics

```md
- All text that looks like or functions as a heading is programmatically marked up using the appropriate heading semantics.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Headings | Page Structure Tutorial | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/headings/)
   - [Headings | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/headings/)
```

#### Table Headers - missing semantics

```md
- Table column / row headers are programmatically identified through appropriate semantic elements so that they can be distinguished from data cells.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Technique H43: Using id and headers attributes to associate data cells with header cells in data tables](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H43)
   - [Technique H63: Using the scope attribute to associate header cells with data cells in data tables](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H63)
   - [Tables Tutorial | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/)
```

#### Table Semantics - missing table semantics for tabular data

```md
- It is important for tabular information to be displayed using proper table semantics.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Tables Tutorial | W3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/)
   - [Tables | APG Patterns](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/)
```

#### Radio buttons

```md
- It's ideal to use the [Primer radio button component](https://primer.style/components/radio) or [Primer radio group component](https://primer.style/product/components/radio-group/) to ensure you have the most complete and accessible radio option.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Radio Group Pattern | APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/)
   - [Radio Component | Primer](https://primer.style/product/components/radio/)
   - [RadioGroup Component | Primer](https://primer.style/product/components/radio-group/)
```

#### Labels

```md
- Consider solutions around [using label elements to associate text labels with form controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H44) or [using the title attribute to identify form controls when the label element cannot be used](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H65).
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Labeling Controls | W3C Forms Tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/)
   - [Grouping Controls | W3C Forms Tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/)
```

#### Group Labels

```md
- Provide a group label with proper semantics such as [Providing a description for groups of form controls using fieldset and legend elements](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H71) and [Using grouping roles to identify related form controls](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA17).
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Grouping Controls | W3C Forms Tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/grouping/)
   - [RadioGroup Component | Primer](https://primer.style/product/components/radio-group/)
   - [ButtonGroup Component](https://primer.style/product/components/button-group/)
   - [CheckboxGroup Component](https://primer.style/product/components/checkbox-group/)
```

#### Lists - li/dt/dd not contained in parent ul/ol/dl

```md
- Ensure that all list elements are contained within an OL or UL, or DL. Also ensure list semantics are only used for content that is a list. Review [Technique H48](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H48) for more information on possible remediation techniques.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Technique H48: Using ol, ul and dl for lists or groups of links](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H48)
   - [Lists | Content Structure | WC3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/content/#lists)
```

#### Lists - ul/ol/dl with invalid child elements

```md
- Ensure that only permitted elements are direct children of an ol, ul, and dl elements. Ensure that other elements are contained within the permitted child elements. Review [Technique H48](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H48) for more information on possible remediation techniques and permitted child elements.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Technique H48: Using ol, ul and dl for lists or groups of links](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H48)
   - [Lists | Content Structure | WC3C](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/content/#lists)
```

#### Required fields not communicated as such by screen readers

```md
- Required form fields are programmatically indicated (for example, using the `required` attribute, `aria-required="true"`, and/or by adding "Required" to the input label.) so assistive technologies can announce that they are required.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships#techniques)
   - [Content Structure](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/page-structure/content/)
   - [Semantic HTML and ARIA | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/semantic-html-and-aria/)
   - [Required field indicator | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/forms/#required-field-indicator)
```

### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence

Default role: Aware

```md
- The programmatic reading order of content matches its logical, visual presentation. This should be able to be verified both with and without a screen reader on.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.2 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence.html#techniques)
   - [Developing a Keyboard Interface | APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/)
   - [Focus Management | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/focus-management/)
   - [Responsive design and accessibility | Accessibility for Web Design | LinkedIn Learning](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/accessibility-for-web-design/responsive-design-and-accessibility-14874212?autoplay=true&resume=false)
```

### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics

Default role: Aware

```md
- Instructions provided for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, color, size, visual location, orientation, or sound. Using [Primer components](https://primer.style/product/components/) when possible can help with this.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.3 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/sensory-characteristics.html#techniques)
   - [Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions | APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/names-and-descriptions/)
   - [Labeling Controls | W3C Forms Tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/)
```

### 1.3.4 Orientation

Default role: Aware

```md
- The content is able to be viewed in a landscape or portrait view without loss of content or functionality.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.4 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/orientation.html#techniques)
   - [Flexible vs Fixed Width Designs | Accessibility for Web Design | LinkedIn Learning](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/accessibility-for-web-design/flexible-vs-fixed-width-designs-14871235?autoplay=true&resume=false)
```

### 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose

Default role: Partner

```md
- The purpose of inputs is able to be identified through the use of descriptive labeling, and appropriate `type` and/or `autocomplete` attributes.
- The general solution is to implement the `autofill` attribute on form of inputs where applicable. Reference [HTML autofill mapping](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#input-purposes) for more context.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.3.5 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-input-purpose.html#techniques)
   - [Technique H98: Using HTML autocomplete attributes](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/html/H98)
   - [HTML <input> type Attribute | W3Schools](https://www.w3schools.com/Tags/att_input_type.asp)
```

### 1.4.1 Use of Color

Default role: Aware

```md
- Color is not be used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color#techniques)
   - [Color Considerations | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/color-considerations/)
   - [Making Color Usage Accessible | Section508.gov](https://www.section508.gov/create/making-color-usage-accessible/)
```

#### Link only differentiated from other text by color

```md
- The linked text is differentiated from surrounding text using sufficient color contrast and/or visual appearance.
- The best method is to have links underlined all the time.
- Sufficient contrast in this instance would be 3:1 with surrounding text AND 4.5:1 with the background.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color#techniques)
   - [Color Considerations | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/color-considerations/)
   - [Visual distinction & contrast | Links | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/links/#visual-distinction--contrast)
```

### 1.4.2 Audio Control

Default role: Aware

```md
- Any audio that automatically plays has a mechanism available to pause or stop the audio, and/or a mechanism to control audio volume independently from the overall system volume level.
   - It is highly recommended that audio not auto-play due to how it can interfere with a screen reader user's ability to navigate and lead to sensory overwhelm in other users.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.2 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-control#techniques)
```

### 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)

Default role: Aware

```md
- Text has sufficient contrast with the background. For regular text the ratio is 4.5:1 and for large text it’s 3:1.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.3 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum#techniques)
   - [Color Considerations | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/color-considerations/)
   - [Making Color Usage Accessible | Section508.gov](https://www.section508.gov/create/making-color-usage-accessible/)
```

### 1.4.4 Resize Text

Default role: Aware

```md
- At 200% zoom, content is:
   - fully visible
   - readable
   - not overlapping
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.4 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text#techniques)
   - [Designing for User Font-size and Zoom | Oddbird](https://www.oddbird.net/2025/07/22/size-preferences/)
   - [A11y 101: 1.4.4 Resize Text | Nat Tarnoff](https://tarnoff.info/2025/04/07/a11y-101-1-4-4-resize-text/)
   - [Truncation | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/truncation/)
```

### 1.4.5 Images of Text

Default role: Aware

```md
- Whenever possible, information is presented as text rather than as an image of text.
    - Exceptions are images that are customizable by the user and images that are essential to the information being conveyed (such as logos).
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.5 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/images-of-text#techniques)
   - [Text over images: The impact on accessibility](https://www.wcag.com/blog/content-over-images-how-does-this-ux-ui-trend-impact-accessibility/)
```

### 1.4.10 Reflow

Default role: Aware

```md
- Content is presented without loss of information or functionality when changing the viewport an equivalent of 320 x 256 pixels, and with no overlapping.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.10 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow#techniques)
   - [Text resize and spacing | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/text-resize-and-spacing)
   - [App-like web experiences: text and UI resizing | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/app-like-web-experiences#text-and-ui-resizing)
```

### 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast

Default role: Aware

```md
- The visual presentation of UI Components and informative graphical objects have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.11 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast#techniques)
   - [Color Considerations | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/color-considerations/)
   - [Making Color Usage Accessible | Section508.gov](https://www.section508.gov/create/making-color-usage-accessible/)
```

### 1.4.12 Text Spacing

Default role: Partner

```md
- Users are able to adjust line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing, and word spacing without loss of content or functionality.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.12 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing#techniques)
   - [Text Spacing Bookmarklet](https://dylanb.github.io/bookmarklets.html)
   - [Truncation | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/truncation/)
```

### 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus

Default role: Partner

```md
- All instances where receiving and then removing pointer hover or keyboard focus triggers additional content to become visible and then hidden, the following are true:
    - Dismissible
    - Hoverable
    - Persistent
- Custom tooltips, sub-menus, and other non-modal popups that display on hover and focus are examples of additional content covered by this criterion.
- Instances where the visual presentation of the additional content is controlled by the user agent and is not modified by the author are exempt.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [1.4.13 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus#techniques)
   - [Tooltip Pattern | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/patterns/primer-components/tooltips/)
   - [Tooltip component accessibility | Primer](https://primer.style/product/components/tooltip/accessibility)
   - [Autocomplete | Primer Component](https://primer.style/product/components/autocomplete/)
   - [SelectPanel | Primer Component](https://primer.style/product/components/select-panel/)
```

### 2.1.1 Keyboard

Default role: Aware, Partner

```md
- All content functionality is operable through a keyboard without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [2.1.1 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard#techniques)
   - [Semantic HTML and ARIA | Primer accessibility guidance](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/semantic-html-and-aria)
   - [Focus management | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/focus-management/)
   - [Keyboard Functionality | Accessibility for Web Design | LinkedIn Learning](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/accessibility-for-web-design/keyboard-functionality-14874210)
```

### 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap

Default role: Aware

```md
- The user is able to navigate all content and functionality with the keyboard without becoming stuck within any component of the page.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [2.1.2 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap#techniques)
   - [Developing a Keyboard Interface | APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/)
   - [Focus management | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/accessibility/design-guidance/focus-management/)
   - [Avoiding Keyboard Traps | Accessibility for Web Design | LinkedIn Learning](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/accessibility-for-web-design/avoiding-keyboard-traps-14870318)
```

### 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts

Default role: Aware, Partner

```md
- All shortcuts using character keys (letters, punctuation, numbers, or symbols) as shortcuts without modifier keys, allow users to turn them off, remap them, or activate them only upon focus.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [2.1.4 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts#techniques)
   - [Keyboard Shortcuts Guidance | The Hub](https://thehub.github.com/epd/engineering/dev-practicals/frontend/keyboard-shortcuts/)
```

### 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable

Default role: Partner

```md
- For each time limit that is set by the UI, one of the following is true:
```

#### Spinner

```md
- Use the [Primer spinner component](https://primer.style/components/spinner) and read about the [loading guidelines](https://primer.style/ui-patterns/loading#accessibility) and [saving guidelines](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/saving/) for accessibility.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
    - [4.1.3 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages#techniques)
```

#### Error message

```md
- All error messages are programmatically tied to their respective inputs/controls and are conveyed to assistive technologies.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [4.1.3 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages#techniques)
   - [Forms | UI Patterns | Primer](https://primer.style/ui-patterns/forms/) (See the various validation sections on this page.)

   - [Notification messaging | UI Patterns | Primer](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/notification-messaging/)
       - Includes Banner and InlineMessage Primer components.
```

#### Status message

```md
- Updated information on the page is conveyed to assistive technology users.
- There are many possible solutions to consider including using [ARIA role="status"](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA22) or sending the focus to the results area on submit.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [4.1.3 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages#techniques)
   - [Loading | Primer Accessibility](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/loading/)

   - [Saving | Primer](https://primer.style/product/ui-patterns/saving/)
```

#### Search results

```md
- Information about the number of search results returned (e.g., "60 results for 'Octocats'"), the lack of results (e.g., "No results returned"), and other messages about the search results returned (e.g., 10 out of 20 results displayed) that displays after the user initiates a search is conveyed to assistive technology users.
- Additionally, the user's focus may be directed to the results area on submit.
- See the following for more information on how to remediate this issue:
   - [4.1.3 Techniques](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages#techniques)
```

bugs.title: No mechanism is provided to pause, stop or hide the auto updating content
bugs.discussion:
[PO] - Should this for sure be reported? or maybe be reported, but with a little more detail?

Like if it is a countdown to when someone's cart expires versus being used for a page timeout versus being used for an auction. 
DENNIS: to close with a comment. Recommend coding in a way to support a11y for the component (stopping/pausing timer), definitely not block. Discuss with Primer team. (And similar items below.) 

Comment added in bug: After discussing this issue with HCL, it was decided to close this issue as not planned. We assume it's possible to implement the component as is and make it accessible. It is also possible that the use-case of an implementation could meet an exception for WCAG SC 2.2.2 Pause Stop Hide.

We do recommend that the component include methods to support 2.2.2 Pause Stop Hide such as providing a play/pause control example and providing support for the prefers-reduced-motion CSS media query.

Primer team: please feel free to discuss further with me.
bugs.conclusion:
Closed as Not planned.
Before logging any bug, please make sure to check wheater any of the possible exception applicable for issue or not. If yes, please don't log the bug.
