bugs.title: Screen reader does not announce search results for valid input.
bugs.discussion:
This should not have been reported. 

Search results are not required to be announced for 4.1.3, unless it is a status message specifically announcing how many results were displayed (e.g., “No results found” or “10 results returned”) or some form of error. See “Additional guidance” section of the 4.1.3 Status Messages Interpretation doc. 

[PA]: - We agree with the feedback, this bug will not mark as WCAG 4.1.3 as there are no visual messages that appear such as (e.g., “No results found” or “10 results returned”). 

 

2- Upon discussing this issue with SME, she tells this is valid issue and can be marked with usable, as there is no visible text/information stating the search result information.  

 

DENNIS to check with Council on above (#10710 regarding 4.1.3) 

 

DECISION FROM COUNCIL (Mar 19): Please close this bug issue as not planned. Although we agree it's good usability, it would require a feature request which is not feasible since it’s not a WCAG violation. And it would set a precedent to continue reporting this which is also not feasible. The issue would come up in usability reviews/testing.
bugs.conclusion: Closed  as not planned but in Future,  if there are no visual messages that appear, these issue can be marked as usable,

bugs.title: Screen reader does not announce the displayed error message
bugs.discussion:
Need to discuss because this potentially needs to be downgraded to a Sev 3. 

My reasoning is, the tester is triggering the error message by dragging and dropping a file in, which most screen reader users would not do. 

If it also happens when the user uses a keyboard to open a file window AND the file window isn't set so it only accepts JSON file types, then I'd maybe see it making sense to keep it as a sev 2. 

If it also happens when the user uses keyboard BUT the file window limits the user to being able to see and select from JSON files, then I would still say make it sev 3 because the user would have to actively ignore the fact that they have been asked to upload a JSON file AND override the system file window to allow themselves to see and select a non-JSON file before they'd see the error. 

Also, this issue needs to be 4.1.3 Status Messages and not 1.3.1 Info and Relationships. 

[PA] - As discussed, this is good to go as SEV2 with WCAG4.1.3 Status message.
bugs.conclusion: Agreed the bug should be under WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages , sev-2

It is a known behavior that screen readers don’t explicitly announce punctuation unless you set your settings to be more verbose.

bugs.title: Target Size for 'Select all' check box is 13px*13px width
bugs.discussion:
Can we confirm how much space is around the checkbox? 

The success criterion has an exception for targets if there is sufficient spacing around them. The Spacing exception states: 

“Undersized targets (those less than 24 by 24 CSS pixels) are positioned so that if a 24 CSS pixel diameter circle is centered on the bounding box of each, the circles do not intersect another target or the circle for another undersized target;” 

The checkbox looks as though it might have sufficient spacing around it to qualify for this exception. 

[PA] - This is good to go

bugs.title: [Screen Reader-GHChangelogUI1.7] Date and Tag Text is not programmatically defined as heading
bugs.discussion:
Ed and Dennis request for HCL to log a new Sev 2 1.3.1 issue for Changelog. Missed in the GA audit. Council also agrees. 

The listings aren’t SR friendly as far as navigation; they don't have helpful accessible semantics (just divs and inline elements). They are marked up as articles, so there should be headings within each article. Currently, a SR shows Landmarks as “article, article, article, etc.”  

Dennis recommends making the date/tag line a heading. Then associate the article with the heading (see code below). 

An alternative is to make it a list. 

Ed: “has a pretty big impact on SR users” 

<article aria-labelledby="foo123"> 
	<reactive-line-state class="ChangelogItem" data-state="resting"> 
		<div class="ChangelogItem-content"> 
			<h3 class="ChangelogItem-content-meta" id="foo123"> 

[PA] - Sure will check and log this bug.
bugs.conclusion: Logged the bug as per discussion

bugs.title: Page does not contain a level one heading
bugs.discussion:
1.	Discuss how Axe best practice items are reported.
	Example 1: Issue #2898, was an Axe best practice item reported as a failure rather than a best practice. 
2.	There is a failure present, but it is in the fact that there is not an appropriate overall heading structure and visual headings that are not marked up as semantic headings.
-	[PA] - Acknowledged.
Comment added:
Axe best practice issues should be reported as Sev 3 / 4 usability issues rather than as failures.

However, for this particular case, there is a failure here, but just not purely due to the lack of an H1.
The issue should be reworded, and its title updated, to reflect that there is a failure due to:

the lack of appropriate heading structure
multiple visual headings that are not marked up as semantic headings
The Acceptance Criteria should be updated to state that:

the NPM logo should be wrapped in an H1
subsequent visual and/or semantic headings updated to be H2-H6 headings in logical order based on page structure
You can reference the WCAG Headings Page Structure tutorial as well.

Additionally, the Success Criterion should be updated to 1.3.1 Info and Relationships since that handles programmatic markup of heading structure, and 2.4.6 Headings and Labels handles the visual presence of them. See the following note for context.
bugs.conclusion: Updated to usable, sev-4

bugs.title: Label is not defined for the 'Sort' dropdown
bugs.discussion:
1.	7776 - The control needs a visible label as it’s a sort by control accessible name does not suffice the issue.
[PA] -  P0 Prateek to check on this and see if this fits 3.3.2 or 4.1.2 more appropriately. Aria-label should be defined in this case.
Comment added:
1. The CELA accessibility team disagrees that a visual text label is required; we feel it passes 3.3.2 (as well as 2.4.6 Headings and Labels). The visual design, particularly the icon, are sufficient. In addition, if you reported this, by the same logic, every icon on the page without a text label would need to be reported.

The element absolutely needs an accessible name (for remediation I suggest aria-label="Sort"). This falls under 4.1.2.

I agree the ascending/descending value should be on the control. Please create a new issue for this. It's a state, so it falls under 4.1.2. My recommendation for remediation is aria-sort or by appending text to the accessible name.
bugs.conclusion: Updated to WCAG 4.1.2 Name Role Value, Sev-2
